daas-irab:147-151.t: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْناهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object. ﴿إِلى مِائَةِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلناه. ﴿أَلْفٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَزِيدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause يزيدون is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم يزيدون" (they are more). ﴿فَآمَنُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فَمَتَّعْناهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿إِلى حِينٍ﴾ both attached to متعناهم. ﴿فَاسْتَفْتِهِمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperative verb and its object, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil. ﴿أَلِرَبِّكَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (inkārī), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿الْبَناتُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَلَهُمُ﴾ a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿الْبَنُونَ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative with the wāw because it is treated like a sound masculine plural. ﴿أَمْ خَلَقْنَا﴾ أم is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْمَلائِكَةَ﴾ the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِناثاً﴾ the second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and هم is mubtadaʾ. ﴿شاهِدُونَ﴾ khabar, nominative with the wāw; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَلا﴾ a particle of calling attention and of opening (tanbīh wa-istiftāḥ). ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ إنّ and its noun. ﴿مِنْ إِفْكِهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb يقولون. ﴿لَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of إنهم.

daas-irab:152-156.t: ﴿وَلَدَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent); the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and إنّ and its noun. ﴿لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and a khabar (predicate), nominative with the wāw; the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَصْطَفَى﴾ a particle of disapproving interrogation (inkārī), and a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿الْبَناتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿عَلَى الْبَنِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) اصطفى; the clause is the maqūl of an omitted verb of saying. ﴿ما لَكُمْ﴾ ما is interrogative, mubtadaʾ (subject), and لكم is [a preposition and its genitive noun,] both attached to the omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is also resumptive. ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لا is negating. ﴿تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to an omitted clause, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿سُلْطانٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of السلطان; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:157-161.t:
﴿فَأْتُوا﴾
the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِكِتابِكُمْ﴾
both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿إِنْ﴾
conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾
كان, its noun and its khabar (predicate), accusative with the yāʾ; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَجَعَلُوا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). ﴿بَيْنَهُ﴾ an adverb. ﴿وَبَيْنَ﴾ an adverb conjoined to بينه. ﴿الْجِنَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿نَسَباً﴾ the first object of جعلوا, and its second object is omitted. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), the lām occurs in the answer of the omitted oath, and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿عَلِمَتِ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الْجِنَّةِ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ إنّ and its noun. ﴿لَمُحْضَرُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and its khabar, nominative with the wāw; إنّ with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of علم. ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ both attached to سبحان. ﴿يَصِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause of the maṣdar (verbal noun) is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿عِبادَ﴾ excepted (mustathnā), accusative. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْمُخْلَصِينَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of عباد. ﴿فَإِنَّكُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and إنّ and its noun. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw of accompaniment (maʿiyya), and ما is a relative pronoun, mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). ﴿تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:162-167.t: ﴿ما﴾ negating, working like ليس. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ its noun. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) فاتنين. ﴿بِفاتِنِينَ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and فاتنين is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of فاتنين. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿صالِ﴾ its khabar. ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle and ما is negating. ﴿مِنَّا﴾ both attached to an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of the omitted mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the nominal clause that comes after إلا. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مَقامٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَعْلُومٌ﴾ a ṣifa. ﴿وَإِنَّا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إنّ and its noun. ﴿لَنَحْنُ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and نحن is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الصَّافُّونَ﴾ the khabar of إنا; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الْمُسَبِّحُونَ﴾ its i'rab is like the preceding verse. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and إن is lightened from the heavy (inna) and inoperative (muhmala). ﴿كانُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿لَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil (agent) being the wāw; the clause يقولون is the khabar of كان, and the clause كان is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:168-173.t: ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, non-jussive. ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿عِنْدَنا﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿ذِكْراً﴾ the postponed noun of أنّ; the khabar (predicate) of أنّ is fronted and omitted, and أنّ with what follows it is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e. "لو ثبت" (if it were established); the omitted clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of ذكرا. ﴿لَكُنَّا﴾ the lām occurs in the answer of لو, and كان and its noun. ﴿عِبادَ﴾ its khabar, accusative. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْمُخْلَصِينَ﴾ a ṣifa of عباد; the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَكَفَرُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) كفروا. ﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and سوف is a particle of futurity. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, the lām occurs in the answer of the omitted oath, and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿سَبَقَتْ﴾ a past verb. ﴿كَلِمَتُنا﴾ its fāʿil; the clause is the answer of the oath, with no grammatical position. ﴿لِعِبادِنَا﴾ both attached to سبقت. ﴿الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ a ṣifa of عبادنا. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ إنّ and its noun. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْمَنْصُورُونَ﴾ the khabar of إنهم; the clause is a badal (substitute) from كلمتنا. ﴿وَإِنَّ جُنْدَنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إنّ and its noun. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ the shifted lām, and هم is a pronoun of separation. ﴿الْغالِبُونَ﴾ the khabar of إنّ, nominative with the wāw; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position. [Translator's note: in the source the brackets around the last three quoted words are garbled («كلمتناَ إِنَّ جُنْدَنا»», «واسمهاَهُمُ»», «لْغالِبُونَ»»); they have been restored here as ﴿وَإِنَّ جُنْدَنا﴾, ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ and ﴿الْغالِبُونَ﴾.]

daas-irab:174-177.t: ﴿فَتَوَلَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) تول. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition. ﴿حِينٍ﴾ a noun, genitive by حتى; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تول; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَأَبْصِرْهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its latent fāʿil, and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾ the fāʾ links the answer of the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), and سوف is a particle of futurity. ﴿يُبْصِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿أَفَبِعَذابِنا﴾ the hamza is for the interrogation of disapproval (inkārī), the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يستعجلون. ﴿يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and إذا is adverbial, conditional and non-jussive. ﴿نَزَلَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿بِساحَتِهِمْ﴾ both attached to نزل. ﴿فَساءَ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and an inflexible (jāmid) past verb. ﴿صَباحُ﴾ fāʿil, nominative. ﴿الْمُنْذَرِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:178-182.t: ﴿وَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى حِينٍ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the verse's i'rab has preceded. ﴿وَأَبْصِرْ فَسَوْفَ يُبْصِرُونَ﴾ its i'rab is clear, as has preceded. ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رَبِّ﴾ a badal (substitute). ﴿الْعِزَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبحان. ﴿يَصِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَسَلامٌ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلَى الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). ﴿وَالْحَمْدُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ both attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ a badal from the Name of Majesty. ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words: ﴿وَٱلصَّافَّاتِ﴾: the tāʾ of ﴿الصافات﴾ and of ﴿التالياتِ﴾ is put in the genitive (khafḍ) because it is an oath (qasam). Ibn Masʿūd used to assimilate (idghām) ﴿وَٱلصَّافَّاتِ صَفَّا﴾, and likewise ﴿والتاليات﴾ ﴿والزاجرات﴾, assimilating the tāʾ in them; but pronouncing it distinctly (tibyān) is better, because recitation is built upon separation and clear articulation.
These words — according to what they have mentioned — are the angels.

farraa:6-6.t: His words: ﴿نَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلْكَوَاكِبِ﴾ [Translator's note: the quotation is printed thus in the source, beginning ﴿نَّا﴾ for «إِنَّا», and with tanwīn on ﴿بِزِينَةٍ﴾ although the comment explains the reading with iḍāfa]: "adornment" (al-zīna) is put in iḍāfa (genitive construct) to "the stars" (al-kawākib). This is the reading of the majority. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Qays and Abū Muʿāwiya related to me from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, that he read (بِزِيَنَةٍ الكَوَاكبِ), putting "the stars" in the genitive by repetition (takrīr, i.e. as a badal (substitute)), so he made a definite noun refer back to an indefinite one, just as He said ﴿لَنَسْفَعاً بِالنَاصِيةِ نَاصِيَةٍ كاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئةٍ﴾, where He made an indefinite noun refer back to a definite one. If you put ﴿الكواكب﴾ in the accusative when you give tanwīn to "adornment", it would be a correct option, meaning: "by Our adorning the stars". And if you put ﴿الكواكب﴾ in the nominative, you would mean: "We adorned it by the stars' adorning it", making the stars the ones that adorned the sky.

farraa:8-9.t:
His words: ﴿لاَّ يَسَّمَّعُونَ﴾: the companions of ʿAbdallāh [ibn Masʿūd] read it with the doubled consonant (tashdīd), in the sense of yatasammaʿūna ("they strain to listen"). The people read it ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ ("they hear"), and Ibn ʿAbbās read it so too; and he said: they ﴿يَتسَمَّعُون ولا يَسْمَعُون﴾ ("they strain to listen but do not hear").
The meaning of (لا) here is as in His words ﴿كَذَلكَ سَلَكْنَاهُ فىِ قُلُوبِ المُجْرِمِينَ لاَ يُؤمِنُون بِهِ﴾: if (أَنْ) stood in the place of (لا) it would be sound, just as He said ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا﴾ and as He said ﴿وَأَلْقىَ فِى الأَرْضِ رَوَاسِىَ أن تمِيدَ بكم﴾. And on this meaning the jussive (jazm) is acceptable after (لا). The Arabs say: rabaṭtu al-farasa lā yanfalit ("I tied the horse so that it would not break loose"), and awthaqtu ʿabdī lā yafrir ("I bound my slave so that he would not flee"). Someone of the Banū ʿUqayl recited to me:
وَحتّى رَأينا أحسَنَ الوُدِّ بينَنَا * مساكتةً لا يَقْرِفِ الشرَّ قَارفُ
(Until we saw that the best affection between us was keeping silent [with one another], so that no one commits evil.)
Some of them say: lā yaqrifu al-sharra (with the indicative). The nominative (rafʿ) is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and with it the Quran came.

His words: ﴿مِن كُلِّ جَانِبٍ دُحُوراً...(8-9)﴾ with ḍamma on the dāl. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī gave it fatḥa [daḥūran]. Whoever gives it ḍamma makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun), as when you say: daḥartuhu duḥūran ("I drove him away with a driving"). Whoever gives it fatḥa makes it a noun, as if He had said: "they are pelted with a repeller and with what repels". I do not care for it, because if it were construed that way correctly, the bāʾ would be in it, as you say: yuqdhafūna bi-l-ḥijāra ("they are pelted with stones"), and you do not say yuqdhafūna al-ḥijāra. Yet it is permissible; the poet said:
نُغَالى اللحم للأضيافِ نِيئاً * وتُرخصه إذا نضِجَ القدورُ
(We pay a high price for the meat for our guests while it is raw, and make it cheap [i.e. give it away freely] when the pots have cooked.)
and the ordinary speech is: nughālī bi-l-laḥm (with the preposition).
His words: ﴿عَذابٌ وَاصِبٌ﴾ and ﴿وَلَهُ الدِّينُ وَاصِباً﴾: [wāṣib means] constant, pure.

farraa:11-11.t:
His words: ﴿مِّن طِينٍ لاَّزِبٍ﴾: al-lāzib is "the sticking". Qays say: ṭīn lātib. One of them recited to me:
صُدَاعٌ وتَوْصيم العظام وفَتْرة * وغَثْىٌ مع الإشراق فى الجَوْف لاتب
(Headache, aching of the bones, languor, and nausea at sunrise that clings in the belly.)
And the Arabs say: laysa hādhā bi-ḍarbati lāzibin and lāzimin ("this is not something fixed and binding"), replacing the bāʾ with a mīm because of the closeness of their points of articulation.

farraa:12-12.t:
His words: ﴿بَلْ عَجِبْتَ وَيَسْخَرُونَ﴾: the people read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ [ʿajibta, "you marvelled"] and with ḍamma [ʿajibtu, "I marvelled"]. The ḍamma is dearer to me, because it is the reading of ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd and ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Mindal ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAnazī related to me from al-Aʿmash; he said: Shaqīq said: I recited in the presence of Shurayḥ (بَلْ عجبتُ ويَسْخَرُوَن), and he said: "Allah does not marvel at anything; only one who does not know marvels." He said: I mentioned that to Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, and he said: "Shurayḥ is a poet who is pleased with his own knowledge, and ʿAbdallāh [ibn Masʿūd] knew this better than he did. He read it (بل عجبتُ ويَسْخَرُونَ)."
Abū Zakariyyā [al-Farrāʾ] said: Marvelling — even if it is attributed to Allah — does not have the same meaning from Allah as it has from His servants. Do you not see that He said ﴿فيَسْخَرُونَ منهمْ سَخِر اللهُ مِنْهُمْ﴾, and mockery from Allah is not like its meaning ﴿منَ العبَاد﴾ (from the servants); and likewise His words ﴿اللهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾ — that is not from Allah like its meaning from the servants. So in this there is a clear proof (to refute the statement) of Shurayḥ. Yet [the fatḥa] is permissible, because the commentators said: "Rather, you marvelled, O Muḥammad, while they mock." This is the reasoning for the fatḥa [Translator's note: the source says "naṣb" (accusative), meaning the fatḥa on the tāʾ].

farraa:28-28.t:
His words: ﴿كُنتُمْ تَأْتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾: He says: you used to come at us from the side of religion, i.e. you used to come at us deceiving us in the strongest of ways. "The right hand" (al-yamīn) means power and strength. Likewise His words ﴿فَرَاغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْباً بِاليَميِن﴾, i.e. with strength and power.
The poet said:
إذا مَا غاية رُفِعت لمجدٍ * تلقَّاهَا عَرَابةُ باليمينِ
(Whenever a banner is raised for glory, ʿArāba receives it with the right hand.)
[that is,] with power and strength. And concerning His words ﴿فَرَاغَ عَليهِمْ ضَرْباً بِاليمينِ﴾ it has also come that He means: he struck them by his oath (yamīn) which he spoke: ﴿وَتَاللهِ لأكِيدَنَّ أصْنَامَكُمْ﴾.

farraa:47-47.t:
His words: ﴿لاَ فِيهَا غَوْلٌ﴾: if you said lā ghawla fīhā, it could be nominative or accusative. But when you separate lā from al-ghawl by a lām or by other prepositional expressions (ṣifāt) [Translator's note: the Kufan term ṣifāt here refers to prepositions/adverbials such as fīhā], nothing but the nominative is possible. And al-ghawl: He says there is no treachery (ghīla), no harm (ghāʾila), no ghūl and no ghawl in it.
His words: ﴿وَلاَ هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنزَفُونَ﴾ and ﴿يُنْزَفُون﴾; the companions of ʿAbdallāh read (يُنْزِفُون), and it has two meanings. It is said: anzafa al-rajul when his wine has run out, and anzafa when his reason has gone. These are two senses. And whoever says ﴿يُنْزَفونَ﴾, it is said [to mean]: their minds do not go [Translator's note: the source reads «تقولهم», apparently a misprint for «عقولهم» "their minds"], and it is from nuzifa al-rajul, fa-huwa manzūf ("the man was made drunk, so he is manzūf").

farraa:54-54.t:
His words: ﴿هَلْ أَنتُمْ مُّطَّلِعُونَ﴾: this is a man from the people of Paradise who had a brother from the people of disbelief; he wished to see his place, so Allah gives him leave, and he looks down into the Fire and addresses him. When he sees him he says ﴿تَاللّهِ إنْ كِدْتَ لَتُرْدِين﴾ — and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh (إنْ كِدْت لَتُغْوِين) — "and were it not for the mercy of my Lord" ﴿لَكُنتُ مِنَ المُحْضَرِينَ﴾, i.e. brought with you into the Fire. Allah says ﴿لِمثْلِ هَذَا فَلْيَعْمَلِ العَامِلُونَ﴾, and this is from Allah's words.
One of the readers read ﴿قَالَ هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُطْلِعُونِ فأُطْلِعَ﴾, with kasra on the nūn. It is irregular (shādhdh), because the Arabs choose nothing other than iḍāfa (genitive construct) when they attach an agent noun, plural or singular, to a pronoun (ism mukannā ʿanhu). Of that is their saying: anta ḍāribī ("you are striking me"); and they say for two: antumā ḍāribāya, and for a plural: antum ḍāribiyya; they do not say for two: antumā ḍāribānnī, nor for a plural: ḍāribūnanī. This nūn occurs only with faʿala and yafʿalu, as in (ḍarabūnī, yaḍribunī, ḍarabanī). Sometimes the poet errs and goes after the meaning, saying: anta ḍāribunī, imagining that he meant "will you strike me?", and that is not sound.
The poet said:
هل الله من سَرْو العَلاَة مُرِيحُنِى * وَلَمَّا تَقَسَّمْنى النِّبَارُ الكوانِسُ
(Will Allah give me rest from the hillside of al-ʿAlāt, before the lurking nibr-insects share me out among themselves?)
al-nibr is a creature resembling the tick. Another said:
وما أدرى وظنَّى كلُّ ظنٍّ * أمسلُمِنى إلى قَومٍ شَرَاحِ
(I do not know — and my thinking is every kind of thinking — whether he will hand me over to the people of Sharāḥ.)
159 ا He means Sharāḥīl; and he did not say amuslimiyya [Translator's note: the source reads «أمسلمِىّ»], which is the normal way of speech. Another said:
هم القائِلُون الخيرَ والفاعلونَه * إذا ما خَشُوا من محدَث الأمر مُعْظَما
(They are the ones who speak good and do it, whenever they fear something grave from a new turn of events.)
and he did not say al-fāʿilūhu, which is the normal way of speech.
They chose iḍāfa with the pronoun only because it blends with what precedes it, so that the two become like a single word. For that reason they preferred iḍāfa with the pronoun, while they said: humā ḍāribāni Zaydan and ḍāribā Zaydin, because Zayd, being an overt noun, does not blend with what precedes it, since it is not a single letter, whereas the pronoun is a single letter.
As for His words ﴿فأُطْلِعَ﴾, it may be in the sense of this being done to him, as you say: daʿā fa-ujība yā hādhā ("he called and was answered, O you"). Or it may be: "Will you let me look down (muṭliʿūni), so that I may look (fa-aṭṭaliʿa)?", in which case it is accusative as the answer with the fāʾ.

farraa:64-64.t: His words: ﴿شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (شجرة نابتة فى أصْل الجحيم) ("a tree growing at the bottom of Hell").

farraa:65-65.t:
His words: ﴿كَأَنَّهُ رُءُوسُ ٱلشَّيَاطِينِ﴾: in Arabic there are three explanations of this. One is that its spathes are likened in their ugliness to the heads of devils, because these are described as ugly even though they are not seen; you say of a man, when you find him ugly: "he is like a devil". The second is that the Arabs call a certain kind of snake shayṭān; it is a snake with a crest.
The poet said, censuring a wife of his:
عنجرد تحلف حين أحلف * كمِثْل شيطانِ الحَمَاط أعرف
(A foul-tongued shrew who swears whenever I swear, like the crested shayṭān-snake of the ḥamāṭ tree.)
And it is said that it is an ugly plant called "the heads of devils". All three explanations come to a single meaning: ugliness.

farraa:67-67.t: His words: ﴿لَشَوْباً﴾: mixing. One says: shāba al-rajul ṭaʿāmahu yashūbuhu shawban ("the man mixed his food").

farraa:70-70.t: His words: ﴿فَهُمْ عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ﴾, i.e. they hasten in their going. al-ihrāʿ is hastening in it, resembling a trembling (and it is said: qad uhriʿa ihrāʿan).

farraa:78-78.t: His words: ﴿وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي ٱلآخِرِينَ﴾ (He says: We left for him a good praise among later generations). And it is said: ﴿تَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى الآخِرِينَ سَلاَمٌ عَلى نُوحٍ﴾, i.e. We left upon him this phrase; just as you say: "I recited from the Quran ﴿الحمدُ لله ربّ العالمين﴾", where the sentence is in the sense of an accusative while you put it in the nominative by its own wording. Likewise (سَلام عَلى نوحٍ): you make it nominative by ʿalā, while it is to be interpreted as accusative. And had it been "We left upon him salāman" (accusative), it would have been correct.

farraa:83-83.t: His words: ﴿وَإِنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِ لإِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾: He says: Among the party of Muḥammad is Abraham, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He says: [he is] upon his religion and his way, so he is of his party, even though Abraham preceded him. This is like His words ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهُمْ أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾, i.e. the offspring of ﴿هو منهم﴾ (those of whom they are); He made it their offspring although it preceded them.

farraa:89-89.t: His words: ﴿إِنِّي سَقِيمٌ﴾, i.e. stricken by plague (ṭāʿūn). And it is said: it is a word containing an equivocation (miʿrāḍ), i.e. everyone who has death hanging on his neck is sick, even if he had no visible sickness when he said it. That is a good explanation. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Yaḥyā ibn al-Muhallab Abū Kudayna related to me from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmāra 159 ب from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb al-Anṣārī concerning His words ﴿لا تُؤَاخِذْنِى بِمَا نَسِيتُ﴾; he said: He did not forget, but it is one of the equivocations of speech (maʿārīḍ al-kalām). And ʿUmar said concerning this: ﴿إنّ فى مَعَاريض الكلام لَمَا يُغنينا عن الكذب﴾ ("In the equivocations of speech there is what spares us from lying") [Translator's note: these are ʿUmar's words, not a Quranic verse, though the source prints them between Quranic brackets].

farraa:93-93.t: His words: ﴿فَرَاغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْباً بِٱلْيَمِينِ﴾, i.e. he turned upon them striking, seizing the opportunity of their being left alone, away from the people of their religion. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (فَراغَ عَليهم صَفْقا باليمين). And it is as if the "turning aside" (rawgh) here is that he made an excuse, slipping away, in order to do to their gods what he did.

farraa:94-94.t:
His words: ﴿فَأَقْبَلُوۤاْ إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ﴾: al-Aʿmash read it ﴿يُزِفُّونَ﴾, as if it were from azfaftu. We have heard it only as zafaftu: you say of a man: jāʾanā yaziffu ("he came to us hurrying"). Perhaps al-Aʿmash's reading is from the Arabs' saying: aṭradtu al-rajul, i.e. I made him an outcast, and ṭaradtuhu when you say to him: "go away from us". So ﴿يُزِفّون﴾ would mean: they came in this manner, like one driven along in this state, and so the alif [of the fourth form] enters; just as you say of a man: huwa maḥmūdun when you make his praise public, and huwa muḥmadun when you see that his affair is heading toward praise but you have not spread his praise. He said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
تمنَّى حُصَين أن يسود جِذَاعَه * فأَمْسَى حُصَين قد أَذَلّ وأَقْهَرَا
(Ḥuṣayn wished to lord it over his clan's youths, but Ḥuṣayn ended up humiliated and overpowered.)
So he said aqhara, i.e. he came into a state of being overpowered, whereas it is properly quhira. After that the people read ﴿يَزِفُّونَ﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the zāy. Some readers read ﴿يَزِفونَ﴾ without doubling, as if from wazafa yazifu; al-Kisāʾī claimed that he did not know it. Al-Farrāʾ said: I do not know it either, unless it simply has not reached us.

farraa:100-100.t: His words: ﴿هَبْ لِي مِنَ ٱلصَّالِحِينَ﴾, and He did not say "a righteous one". This is like the saying: "Come near and take some of the food", and it is frequent: min suffices in place of the implied [noun], as Allah said ﴿وَكَانُوا فِيهِ مِنَ الزَّاهِدِينَ﴾ and did not say "abstainers from among the abstainers".

farraa:101-101.t: His words: ﴿بِغُلاَمٍ حَلِيمٍ﴾: He means: [forbearing] in his adulthood (kibar).

farraa:102-102.t: His words: ﴿فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْيَ﴾: He says: he was able to help him in his work and his toil. Ishmael was at that time thirteen years old. ﴿فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ﴾ is also read ﴿تُرِى﴾. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Hushaym related to me from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, that he read (فَانْظُرْ ماذَا تُرِى). Al-Farrāʾ said: And Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth related to me from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmāra ibn ʿUmayr, from al-Aswad, that he read it (تَرَى), and that Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it (تُرِى); and (تُرِى) has been traced back to ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd. Al-Farrāʾ said: And Qays related to me from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, who said: (فانْظُرْ مَاذا تُرِى) means "what you advise", and ﴿مَاذَا تَرَى﴾ means "what you command". Abū Zakariyyā said: And I think — and Allah knows best — that he did not consult him about Allah's command, but rather said: "See what you will show me of your patience or your distress"; so he said ﴿سَتَجِدُنِيۤ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّابِرِينَ﴾. It may also be that he informed his son of what he had been commanded in order to see what his opinion was, while he himself was going ahead with what he had been commanded.

farraa:103-103.t:
His words: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ﴾: He says: aslamā, i.e. they both submitted and obeyed. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (سلَّمَا); He says sallamā from taslīm ("submission"), as you say: "If a calamity befalls you, submit (sallim) to Allah's command", i.e. be content with it.
He said ﴿افْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ﴾ and did not say (به) ("with it"), as if He meant: "do the thing that you are commanded". Had it been (به) it would have been a good option; and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (إنى أَرى فىِ المَنَامِ افعلْ ما أُمِرْت به). And it may be asked: where is the apodosis (jawāb) of His words ﴿فَلَمّا أسْلَما؟﴾?
Its apodosis is in His words ﴿وَنَادَيْنَاهُ﴾. The Arabs 160 ا insert the wāw in the apodosis of fa-lammā and ﴿وحَتّى إذا﴾, and they drop it. Of that are Allah's words ﴿حَتَّى إذَا جاءُوهَا فُتِحَتْ﴾ and in another place ﴿وَفُتِحَتْ﴾, and all of it is correct. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بجَهَازِهِمْ وجَعَل السِّقَايَةَ}, while in our reading it is without the wāw. We have explained this in [Sūrat] al-Anbiyāʾ.

farraa:107-107.t: His words: ﴿وَفَدَيْنَاهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾: al-dhibḥ is the ram, and anything you have prepared for slaughter (dhabḥ) is a dhibḥ. It is said that it had grazed in Paradise for forty autumns — so how great it is! And Mujāhid said: ﴿عظيمٍ﴾ means "accepted".

farraa:116-116.t: His words: ﴿وَنَصَرْنَاهُمْ فَكَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلْغَالِبينَ﴾: He made them like a plural «[Translator's note: i.e. Moses and Aaron]», and afterwards mentioned them as two. This is from the breadth of Arabic: that the leader — the prophet, the commander and the like — is treated as a plural, because of his troops and followers, and as a singular, because he is originally one. Similar is ﴿عَلَى خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ ومَلَئِهِمْ﴾ and in another place ﴿وَمَلَئِهِ﴾. And sometimes the Arabs treat two as a plural, just as one is treated as a plural; do you not see that you address a man and say: "You (pl.) did not do well, nor act nobly", while you mean him in particular; and a man says of a legal opinion (fatwā) that he gives: "We say such and such", while he means himself. Similar to that are His words in Sūrat Ṣād: ﴿وَهَلْ أَتَاكَ نَبَأُ الخَصْمِ إذ تَسوَّرُوا المِحْرَابَ﴾, then He mentioned them again in the dual when He said: ﴿خَصْمَانِ بَغَى بَعْضُنَا عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾.

farraa:123-123.t: His words: ﴿وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾: It is mentioned that he was a prophet, and that this name is one of the Hebrew names, like their saying Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq, with the alif and lām part of it. If you made it Arabic, from al-alyas, making it of the pattern ifʿāl like ikhrāj and idkhāl, it would be declinable (la-jarā).

farraa:125-125.t: His words: ﴿أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلاً﴾: They mentioned that it was an idol of gold called Baʿl, so He said ﴿أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلاً﴾, i.e. [do you call upon] this idol as a lord? And it is said: do you call upon a baʿl as a lord other than Allah? And it is mentioned of Ibn ʿAbbās that a stray animal was being announced, and its owner came and said: "I am its baʿl." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "This is Allah's word ﴿أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلاً﴾", i.e. a lord.

farraa:126-126.t: His words: ﴿ٱللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ وَرَبَّ آبَآئِكُمُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾ is read in the accusative and the nominative. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khaytham read it in the accusative.

farraa:130-130.t:
His words: ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ إِلْ يَاسِينَ﴾: He gave it a nūn. The Arabs sometimes do this with foreign names. They say: Mīkāl, Mīkāʾīl, Mīkāʾil and Mīkāʾīn with a nūn. It is found among the Banū Asad, who say: "This is Ismāʿīn who has come", with a nūn, while the rest of the Arabs [say it] with a lām. He said: and one of the Banū Numayr recited to me about a lizard (ḍabb) that one of them had caught:
يقول أهلُ السوق لما جينا * هذا وَربِّ البيت إسرائينا
(The people of the market said when we came: "By the Lord of the House, this is Isrāʾīn!")
So this is one explanation of His saying Ilyāsīn. And if you wish, you may take Ilyāsīn as a plural, making his companions included in his name, as you say of a people whose chief is al-Muhallab: "al-Mahāliba and al-Muhallabūn have come to you"; so it would be like the saying al-Ashʿarīn, al-Saʿdīn and the like. The poet said:
* أنا ابن سعدٍ سَيّدِ السَّعْدِينا *
(I am the son of Saʿd, chief of the Saʿds.)
And this is more frequent with two: that one is combined with his companion when he is more famous by name; as the poet says:
جزانى الزَّهدمان جزاء سَوءٍ * وكنتُ المرءَ يُجزَى بالكرامَهْ
(The two Zahdams repaid me with an evil repayment, while I was a man who used to be repaid with honour.)
and the name of one of them was Zahdam. Another said:
جزى الله فيهَا الأعوَرَين ذَمَامَةً * وفروة ثَغْر الثورَةِ المتضَاجِم
(May Allah repay the two one-eyed men for it with blame, and Farwa, the crooked-mouthed one of the uprising.)
and the name of one of them was Aʿwar.
Some read ﴿وَإنّ اليَأْسَ﴾, making his name Yaʾs and adding the alif and lām to it. Then they read ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ آل يَاسِينَ﴾; in the commentary of al-Kalbī the explanation came of "upon the family of Yāsīn" as: upon the family of Muḥammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. The first is closer to being correct — and Allah knows best — because in the reading of / 160 ب ʿAbdallāh it is ﴿وَإِنَّ إِدْرِيسَ لَمِنَ المرسَلينَ﴾ ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلى إِدْراسِين﴾. And His words ﴿وَشَجَرَةً تُخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْنَاءَ﴾ bear witness to the correctness of this; then He said in another place ﴿وَطُورِ سِينِينَ﴾, and it is one meaning and one place. And Allah knows best.

farraa:140-140.t: His words: ﴿ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ﴾: when a ship is equipped and filled, this name applies to it. al-fulk is treated as masculine and feminine and is also taken as a plural; Allah said ﴿حَتَّى إذَا كُنْتُمْ فِى الفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ﴾, making it a plural. It is like al-ṭifl ("child"), which is singular and plural; and al-ḍayf ("guest") and al-bashar ("mankind") are similar.

farraa:141-141.t: His words: ﴿ٱلْمُدْحَضِينَ﴾: the defeated. One says: adḥaḍa Allāhu ḥujjataka fa-daḥaḍat ("Allah refuted your argument, so it collapsed"). Its original sense is a man slipping.

farraa:142-142.t: His words: ﴿وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ﴾: he is one who has earned blame even if he has not been blamed. al-malūm is one who has actually been blamed with the tongue. It is like the Arabs' saying aṣbaḥta muḥmiqan muʿṭishan, i.e. you have foolishness and thirst [around you]. This is frequent in speech.

farraa:146-146.t: His words: ﴿مِّن يَقْطِينٍ﴾: it was said in the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās: "It is the leaf of the gourd." He said: "And what made the gourd leaf, among all plants, yaqṭīn? Every leaf that is broad and gives cover is yaqṭīn."

farraa:147-147.t: His words: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَىٰ مِئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾: aw here is in the sense of bal ("rather"). So it is in the commentary, while also being sound in Arabic.

farraa:148-148.t: His words: ﴿فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbdallāh (فمتّعناهم حَتَّى حِين). ḥattā and ilā are the same in [expressing] limits when used with nouns.

farraa:149-149.t: His words: ﴿فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ﴾, i.e. ask them — ask the people of Mecca.

farraa:152-153.t: His words: ﴿لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ ﴿أَصْطَفَى﴾ is a question containing a rebuke to them. The interrogative alif is sometimes dropped from a rebuke. Similar is His saying ﴿أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّبَاتِكُمْ﴾, which is read both with and without the interrogative, and the meaning of both is one. And the alif of (اصْطفى), when it is not interrogative, drops in connected speech, and you begin it with kasra.

farraa:158-158.t: His words: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ نَسَباً﴾: it is said that al-jinna here are the angels. They set up a kinship between Him and His creation. ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَتِ ٱلجِنَّةُ﴾ that those who said this ﴿مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ — [will be brought] into the Fire.

farraa:161-161.t: His words: ﴿فَإِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾: He means: and your gods which you worship ﴿مَا أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفَاتِنِينَ﴾: [you are not] leading astray.

farraa:162-162.t: His words: ﴿مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾, i.e. you are not leading [anyone] astray upon that religion. And His words ﴿عَلَيه﴾, ﴿بِهِ﴾ and ﴿لَهُ﴾ are equivalent here. The people of Najd say: bi-muftinīna. The people of the Hijaz [say]: fatantu al-rajul, while the people of Najd say: aftantuhu.

farraa:163-163.t:
His words: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنْ هُوَ صَالِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾: except one for whom it was decreed, in Allah's prior knowledge, that he would burn in Hell. Al-Ḥasan read (إلاَّ مَنْ هو صَالُ الجحيم), with ḍamma on the lām, according to what they have mentioned. If he meant a singular, it is not permissible, because you do not say hādhā qāḍun nor rāmun. But if he knew a metathesized form (lugha maqlūba) in it, like ʿātha and ʿathā, then it is correct. The Arabs have said: jurufun hārun and hārin, and huwa shāku al-silāḥ 161 ا and shākī al-silāḥ ("bristling with weapons"). One of them recited to me:
فلو أَنَّى رميتك من بَعيد * لعَاقكَ عن دعاء الذئبِ عَاقِى
(Had I shot at you from afar, a hindrance would have kept you from calling the wolf.)
He means ʿāʾiq; this is one of the metathesized forms. And from it are ﴿ولاَ تَعْثوا﴾ and wa-lā taʿīthū — two dialect forms. It may also be that you make ﴿صَالو﴾ a plural; as you say: "Among the men are those who (man huwa) are your brothers", taking huwa to refer to the unspecified noun, and putting its verb in the plural; as the poet said:
إذا ما حَاتم وُجد ابن عمّى * مَجَدنَا مَن تكلّم أجمعينَا
(When Ḥātim is found to be my cousin, we surpass in glory all who speak.)
and he did not say takallamū. The best in Arabic, when you bring out the pronoun reference (kināya), is to bring it out according to the meaning and the number, because you intend the reality of the noun.

farraa:164-164.t:
His words: ﴿وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ﴾: this is the speech of the angels, up to His words ﴿وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ المسَبِّحُونَ﴾; He means ﴿المصَلُّونَ﴾ ("those who pray"). In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (وإن كُلَّنا لمَّا له مقام معلوم).
And in [Sūrat] Maryam: ﴿إنْ كُلُّ مَنْ فِى السّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ لَمَّا أَتَى الرَّحْمَنَ عَبْداً﴾. The meaning of in ḍarabtu la-Zaydan is like the meaning of your saying: mā ḍarabtu illā Zaydan ("I struck no one but Zayd"); that is why I mentioned this.

farraa:167-167.t: His words: ﴿وَإِن كَانُواْ لَيَقُولُونَ﴾: He means the people of Mecca: ﴿لَوْ أَنَّ عِنْدَنَا ذِكْراً مِنَ الأَوَّلينَ﴾; He says: a scripture or prophethood; ﴿لَكُنَّا عِبَادَ اللهِ المُخْلَصِينَ﴾.

farraa:170-170.t: Allah said: ﴿فَكَفَرُواْ بِهِ﴾. The meaning is: Muḥammad had been sent to them with the Quran, and they disbelieved in it. This is implied, not mentioned, because its meaning is known; like His words ﴿يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ﴾, then He said ﴿فمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ﴾, joining Pharaoh's speech to their speech because the meaning is clear.

farraa:171-171.t:
His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا﴾: those for whom felicity was preordained. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (ولقد سبقت كلمتنا عَلى عبادنا المرسَلين). ʿAlā is acceptable in the place of the lām, because their meanings come back to one thing. It is as if the meaning were: it was made due upon them and for them; as He said ﴿عَلَى مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَان﴾, whose meaning is: during (fī) the reign of Solomon. So just as it was permitted to alternate between fī and ʿalā when the meaning agrees, so it was done with this.
His words: ﴿فإذَا نَزَل بِسَاحَتِهِمْ﴾: its meaning is: upon them. The Arabs make do with "the courtyard" (al-sāḥa) and "the vicinity" (al-ʿaqwa) for the people themselves.
Their meaning is one: "the punishment descended upon you" and "upon your courtyard" are the same.
His words: ﴿فسَاءَ صَبَاحُ المُنْذَرِينَ﴾: He means: evil is the morning of… In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: ﴿فبئس صَبَاح المُنْذِرِين﴾. And in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "I have announced to you with the announcement of the messengers, you will surely be asked about this great tiding." It was said to him: "It is only 'and I announced to you'", and he said: "This is how it is with me."

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive, and the preposition [phrase] is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (muqaddar) (أقسم, "I swear"). «صفا»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), governed by «الصافات».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «فالزاجرات»: a conjoined noun, and «زجرا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (إن إلهكم لواحد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the response to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «رب»: second khabar (predicate) of {إِنَّ}. «ما»: a relative noun conjoined to «السماوات». «بينهما»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «وحفظا»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governing word is implied, i.e.: We guarded it with a guarding; the governing word is conjoined to the preceding clause {زَيَّنَّا}. The preposition «من كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied governing word «حفظناها».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «لا يسَّمَّعون» is resumptive, and the verb is made to carry (mudammin) the sense of «لا يُصْغون» ("they do not incline their ears"). It cannot be adjectival, since there is no sense in guarding against a devil that does not listen.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «دحورا»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); it is synonymous with «يُقذفون». The clause «ولهم عذاب» is conjoined to the clause {لا يَسَّمَّعُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: His words «مَن»: a relative noun, accusative as the excepted. «الخطفة»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause «فأتبعه» is conjoined to the clause «خطف».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «فاستفتهم» is resumptive. The interrogative clause is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «استفتهم», which is made to carry the sense of a verb of the heart. «خلقا»: tamyīz (specification). His words «مَن»: a relative noun conjoined to «هم», and «أم» is a connected (muttaṣila) conjunction.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «عجبت» is resumptive. The clause «ويسخرون» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being «هم»; the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the wāw is circumstantial.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: (وإذا ذكروا لا يذكرون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is conjoined to the clause «يسخرون».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: (وإذا رأوا آية يستسخرون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding clause.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «وقالوا» is conjoined to the clause that is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «إنْ» is negating.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the sense of the apodosis, i.e.: we will be resurrected. The clause «إنا لمبعوثون» is explicative of the apodosis; this clause cannot be the apodosis of «إذا», because what comes after «إنّ» does not govern what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «آباؤنا»: mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being «مبعوثون»; the clause of the mubtadaʾ and khabar is conjoined to the clause «إنا لمبعوثون».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) is implied, i.e.: yes, you will be resurrected. The clause «وأنتم داخرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تبعثون».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «فإنما هي زجرة» is resumptive, and the clause «فإذا هم ينظرون» is conjoined to the resumptive [clause]; «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya).

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «وقالوا» is conjoined to the clause {هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ}, and the clause «هذا يوم الدين» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «هذا يوم الفصل» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of a new speech. «الذي»: naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «احشروا» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied speech. «وأزواجهم»: a noun conjoined to «الذين», and «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «أزواجهم».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun. The clause «فاهدوهم» is conjoined to the clause {احْشُرُوا}.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The clause «لا تناصرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The interrogative clause is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied speech.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The adverb «اليوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «مستسلمون».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «وأقبل» is resumptive, and the clause «يتساءلون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «أقبل».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The preposition «عن اليمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) in «تأتوننا».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) is implied, i.e.: we did not lead you astray; rather, you were not... The clause «لم تكونوا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «وما كان لنا عليكم من سلطان» is conjoined to the clause {لَمْ تَكُونُوا}. The preposition «لنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «كان», and the preposition «عليكم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سلطان»; «سلطان» is the noun of «كان», and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «كنتم» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «فحق» is conjoined to the clause {كُنْتُمْ}, and the clause «إنَّا لذائقون» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl).

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «فأغويناكم» is conjoined to the clause {لَمْ تَكُونُوا}, and the clause «إنَّا كنا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «فإنهم يومئذ مشتركون» is resumptive, and the prepositional phrase and the adverb are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «مشتركون».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: (إنا كذلك نفعل بالمجرمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: We do a doing like that doing.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «إذا»: a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يستكبرون». The clause of declaring [Allah] transcendent (tanzīh) is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied speech. «الله»: badal (substitute) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar (predicate). The clause «يستكبرون» is the khabar of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «ويقولون» is conjoined to the clause {يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ}. The preposition «لشاعر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تاركو».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جاء», and the clause «جاء» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: (إنكم لذائقو العذاب الأليم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive, and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: «ما»: a relative noun, second object, and «إلا» is for restriction.

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: (إلا عباد الله المخلصين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] [«عباد» is] excepted in a disjoined exception, and «المخلصين» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «لهم رزق» is the khabar (predicate) of «أولئك».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «فواكه»: badal (substitute) of {رِزْقٌ}. The clause «وهم مكرمون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «لهم».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The preposition «في جنات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {مُكْرَمُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The preposition «على سرر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متقابلين», and «متقابلين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in {مُكْرَمُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «يطاف» is resumptive. «عليهم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The preposition «بكأس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يطاف», and the preposition «من معين» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «كأس».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: «بيضاء»: second naʿt (adjective) of «كأس»; «لذة»: third naʿt; «للشاربين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of «لذة».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The clause «لا فيها غول» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كأس»; «غول» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «ولا هم ينزفون» is conjoined to the nominal clause, and the preposition «عنها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينزفون».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «عندهم قاصرات» is conjoined to the clause {يُطَافُ}. «عين»: naʿt (adjective) of «قاصرات».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: (كأنهن بيض مكنون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of {قَاصِرَاتُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «فأقبل» is resumptive. The preposition «على بعض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أقبل», and the clause «يتساءلون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بعضهم».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «قال قائل» is resumptive. The preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قائل». The clause «كان لي قرين» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The clause «يقول» is a naʿt (adjective) of {قَرِينٌ}, and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the sense of the apodosis, "we will be resurrected". The clause «متنا» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct), and the clause «أئنا لمدينون» is explicative of the apodosis.

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «فاطلع» is conjoined to the clause {قَالَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: «إنْ» is lightened from the heavy [إنّ] and left inoperative, and the lām is the distinguishing one (al-lām al-fāriqa). «تردين»: an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ; the nūn is that of protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ, dropped for lightness, is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «تردين» is the khabar (predicate) of «كاد», and the clause «إن كدت لتردين» is the response to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the response to the oath. «نعمة»: mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "existing".

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: «ما» acts like «ليس», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in its khabar (predicate). The clause is conjoined to the content of an implied speech, i.e.: the people of Paradise said: Are we to abide forever? So we are not going to die.

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: «موتتنا»: excepted in a disjoined exception; «الأولى»: naʿt (adjective). The clause «وما نحن بمعذبين» is conjoined to the clause «ما نحن بميتين», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: (إن هذا لهو الفوز العظيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الفوز» its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: (لمثل هذا فليعمل العاملون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يعمل»; «هذا» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and the lām is of the command, making [the verb] jussive.

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The clause «ذلك خير» is resumptive. «نزلا»: tamyīz (specification). The connected (muttaṣila) «أم» is a conjunction, and «شجرة» is a noun conjoined to the mubtadaʾ (subject) «ذلك».

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: «فتنةً»: second object, and the clause is resumptive. The preposition «للظالمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فتنة».

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The clause «طلعها كأنه رءوس» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «شجرة».

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: The clause «فإنهم لآكلون» is resumptive; the preposition «منها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آكلون». His words «فمالئون»: conjoined to «آكلون»; «البطون» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle «مالئون», and the second preposition «منها» is attached to «مالئون».

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: The preposition «عليها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حميم», and the lām is for emphasis. The preposition «من حميم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «شوبا». The clause is conjoined to the clause «إنهم لآكلون».

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: (ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause «إن لهم لشوبا», and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: The clause «ألفوا» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and «ضالين» is the second object of «ألفى».

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: (فهم على آثارهم يهرعون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّهُمْ أَلْفَوْا}; the clause «يهرعون» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The clause «ولقد ضلَّ قبلهم» is resumptive; «أكثر» is the fāʿil (agent).

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: The clause «ولقد أرسلنا» is conjoined to the clause «لقد ضلَّ». «منذرين»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The clause «فانظر» is resumptive. The clause «كيف كان» is the object of the looking, which carries the sense of knowing and is suspended [from operating] by the interrogative; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, khabar (predicate) of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: «عباد»: excepted in a disjoined exception, and «المخلصين» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The clause «ولقد نادانا نوح» is resumptive, and the clause «لقد نادانا» is the response to the oath. The fāʾ is a conjunction, and the lām occurs in the response to the oath; the clause is conjoined to the preceding response to the oath, and there is no need to assume a second oath. The one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, its implied form being «نحن», and «المجيبون» is the fāʿil (agent) of «نِعْم».

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: The clause «ونجيناه» is conjoined to the clause that is the preceding response to the oath. His words «وأهله»: a noun conjoined to the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: «هم»: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). «وجعلنا» takes two objects: «ذريته» and «الباقين».

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: The clause «وتركنا» is conjoined to the clause «جعلنا». The two prepositional phrases are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the object of «تركنا» is implied as something like: praise.

harrat-mujtaba:79-79.t: (سلام على نوح في العالمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is explicative of the preceding implied object. «سلام» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition after it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it denotes a supplication. The preposition «في العالمين» is attached to the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:80-80.t: The kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: He recompenses those who do good with a recompense like that recompense. The clause «إنَّا نجزي» is resumptive, and the clause «نجزي» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: (إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: (ثم أغرقنا الآخرين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause «تركنا» in verse (78).

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: (وإن من شيعته لإبراهيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; the lām is for emphasis, and the preposition «من شيعته» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, object of an implied (muqaddar) «اذكر» ("remember"). The clause «جاء» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). The preposition «بقلب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «جاء».

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, badal (substitute) of the preceding {إِذْ}. «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا»: a relative noun, its khabar (predicate); and the clause «تعبدون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

harrat-mujtaba:86-86.t: «إفكا»: object of «تريدون»; «آلهة»: badal (substitute); «دون»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آلهة». The clause «تريدون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:87-87.t: (فما ظنكم برب العالمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause {تُرِيدُونَ}. «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ظنكم» is its khabar (predicate). The preposition «برب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ظنكم».

harrat-mujtaba:88-88.t: The clause «فنظر» is resumptive; «نظرة» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:89-89.t: The clause «فقال» is conjoined to the clause «نظر».

harrat-mujtaba:90-90.t: The clause «فتولَّوا» is conjoined to the clause «قال». The verb is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, which was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). «مدبرين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:91-91.t: (فراغ إلى آلهتهم فقال ألا تأكلون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause «تَوَلَّوا». «ألا» is for offering (ʿarḍ).

harrat-mujtaba:92-92.t: «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive within the scope of the speech. The clause «لا تنطقون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in «لكم».

harrat-mujtaba:93-93.t: (فراغ عليهم ضربا باليمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause «قال» in verse (91). «ضربا»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied verb, and the clause of the implied verb is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «راغ». The preposition «باليمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) «ضربا».

harrat-mujtaba:94-94.t: The clause «فأقبلوا» is resumptive, and the clause «يزفُّون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «أقبلوا».

harrat-mujtaba:95-95.t: «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:96-96.t: The clause «والله خلقكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw, and «ما» is a relative conjoined to the kāf.

harrat-mujtaba:97-97.t: «بنيانا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause «فألقوه» is conjoined to the clause «ابنوا».

harrat-mujtaba:98-98.t: The preposition «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كيدا», and «الأسفلين» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:99-99.t: The clause «وقال» is resumptive. The preposition «إلى ربي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ذاهب». The clause «سيهدين» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:100-100.t: «رب»: the one addressed, in a construct (munādā muḍāf), accusative with the yāʾ implied on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, which was dropped for lightness. The vocative clause is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied speech. The clause «هب» is the response to the vocative, resumptive. The preposition «من الصالحين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of an implied object, i.e.: a son being among the righteous.

harrat-mujtaba:101-101.t: The clause «فبشَّرناه» is conjoined to the preceding implied speech.

harrat-mujtaba:102-102.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. The adverb «معه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (أعني, "I mean"); it is not attached to «بلغ», because that would require that both of them reached the age of striving together. His words «يا بني»: the one addressed, in a construct (munādā muḍāf), accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أني أذبحك» takes the place of the two objects of «رأى» of dreaming. «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» a relative noun, its khabar (predicate); the clause «ماذا ترى» is the object of the looking, which carries the sense of knowing and is suspended [from operating] by the interrogative. The clause «فانظر» is resumptive. His words «يا أبت»: the one addressed, in a construct, accusative with an implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, which has been changed into tāʾ. The clause «ستجدني» is resumptive. The conditional clause is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The preposition «من الصابرين» is attached to the second object of (وجد).

harrat-mujtaba:103-103.t: (فلما أسلما وتله للجبين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding conditional clause, and the clause of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: their patience became manifest.

harrat-mujtaba:104-104.t: The clause «وناديناه» is conjoined to the clause {أَسْلَمَا}. «أنْ» is explicative (mufassira), and the vocative clause is explicative of the calling.

harrat-mujtaba:105-105.t: The clause «قد صدَّقت» is the response to the vocative, resumptive. The clause «إنا نجزي» is resumptive, and the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: We recompense those who do good with a recompense like that recompense.

harrat-mujtaba:106-106.t: The clause «لهو البلاء» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:108-108.t: (وتركنا عليه في الآخرين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The two prepositional phrases are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the object of «تركنا» is implied as something like: praise.

harrat-mujtaba:109-109.t: (سلام على إبراهيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is explicative of the preceding implied object. «سلام» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition after it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:110-110.t: The clause «نجزي» is resumptive, and the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: We recompense those who do good with a recompense like that.

harrat-mujtaba:111-111.t: (إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:112-112.t: The clause «وبشَّرناه» is conjoined to the clause {وَتَرَكْنَا}. «نبيا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «إسحاق». The preposition «من الصالحين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نبيا».

harrat-mujtaba:113-113.t: The preposition «من ذريتهما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «محسن», and the clause «من ذريتهما محسن» is resumptive. The lām in «لنفسه» is for strengthening, because its governing word «ظالم» is an active participle, which is secondary [to the verb], so it is strengthened with the lām; «نفسه» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «ظالم». «مبين»: naʿt (adjective) of «ظالم».

harrat-mujtaba:114-114.t: (ولقد مننا على موسى وهارون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive, and the lām occurs in the response to an implied oath.

harrat-mujtaba:115-115.t: His words «وقومهما»: a noun conjoined to the hāʾ. The preposition «من الكرب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نجَّيناهما».

harrat-mujtaba:116-116.t: The clause «فكانوا هم الغالبين» is conjoined to the clause «نصرناهم», and the pronoun «هم» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:119-119.t: (وتركنا عليهما في الآخرين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The two prepositional phrases are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the object of «تركنا» is implied.

harrat-mujtaba:120-120.t: (سلام على موسى وهارون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is explicative of the preceding implied object.

harrat-mujtaba:121-121.t: The clause «نجزي» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:122-122.t: (إنهما من عبادنا المؤمنين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive, and «المؤمنين» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:123-123.t: (وإن إلياس لمن المرسلين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:124-124.t: «إذ»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «المرسلين». «ألا» is for offering (ʿarḍ). The clause «قال» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:125-125.t: The clause «أتدعون» is resumptive. «أحسن»: the object of «تذر».

harrat-mujtaba:126-126.t: «الله»: badal (substitute) of {أَحْسَنَ}; «ربكم»: badal of the Divine Name; «الأولين»: naʿt (adjective) of «آبائكم».

harrat-mujtaba:127-127.t: The clause «فكذَّبوه» is conjoined to the clause {قَالَ} in verse (124), and the clause «فإنهم لمحضرون» is conjoined to the clause «كذَّبوه»; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:129-129.t: (وتركنا عليه في الآخرين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The two prepositional phrases are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the object of «تركنا» is implied, i.e.: praise.

harrat-mujtaba:130-130.t: (سلام على إل ياسين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is explicative of the implied object.

harrat-mujtaba:131-131.t: The clause «نجزي» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:132-132.t: (إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:133-133.t: (وإن لوطا لمن المرسلين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:134-134.t: «إذ»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «المرسلين». «أهله»: a noun conjoined to the hāʾ. «أجمعين»: tawkīd (emphasis).

harrat-mujtaba:135-135.t: The preposition «في الغابرين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «عجوزا».

harrat-mujtaba:136-136.t: (ثم دمرنا الآخرين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause {نَجَّيْنَاهُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:137-137.t: (وإنكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive. «مصبحين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تمرون»; it is from the complete (tāmm) «أصبح».

harrat-mujtaba:138-138.t: (وبالليل) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) conjoined to the preceding ḥāl, i.e.: and while being in the night. The clause «أفلا تعقلون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:139-139.t: (وإن يونس لمن المرسلين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive, and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:140-140.t: «إذ»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) {الْمُرْسَلِينَ}, and the clause «أبق» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:141-141.t: The clause «فكان» is conjoined to the clause «فساهم».

harrat-mujtaba:142-142.t: The clause «وهو مليم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in the clause «التقمه».

harrat-mujtaba:143-143.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to «التقمه». «أن» and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "existing", i.e.: were it not that his being among those who glorify [Allah] existed.

harrat-mujtaba:144-144.t: The preposition «إلى يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لبث», and the clause «يبعثون» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:145-145.t: The clause «فنبذناه» is resumptive, and the clause «وهو سقيم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:146-146.t: The preposition «من يقطين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «شجرة».

harrat-mujtaba:147-147.t: «أو» here is for permission (ibāḥa), i.e.: one looking at them is permitted to estimate them at this amount or at this amount. The clause «يزيدون» is conjoined to the clause «أرسلناه».

harrat-mujtaba:148-148.t: The clause «فآمنوا» is conjoined to the clause «أرسلناه».

harrat-mujtaba:149-149.t: (فاستفتهم ألربك البنات ولهم البنون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive, and the interrogative clause after it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «استفتهم», which is made to carry the sense of a verb of the heart taking two objects.

harrat-mujtaba:150-150.t: (أم خلقنا الملائكة إناثا وهم شاهدون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «أم» is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) one, interpreted as (بل) plus the hamza, and the clause after it is resumptive. «إناثا»: ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause «وهم شاهدون» is a ḥāl.

harrat-mujtaba:151-151.t: The preposition «من إفكهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied «أعني» ("I mean"). The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). The clause «ألا إنهم ...» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:152-152.t: The clause «وإنهم لكاذبون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «يقولون».

harrat-mujtaba:153-153.t: (أصطفى البنات على البنين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive. The preposition «على البنين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اصطفى».

harrat-mujtaba:154-154.t: «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). «كيف»: an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «تحكمون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:156-156.t: (أم لكم سلطان مبين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «أم» is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) one, and the clause after it is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:157-157.t: The clause «فأتوا» is resumptive, and the conditional clause is resumptive; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:158-158.t: The clause «وجعلوا» is resumptive. «بينه»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied second object. The clause «ولقد علمت الجنة» is conjoined to the clause «جعلوا», and the clause «لقد علمت» is the response to the oath. The clause «إنهم لمحضرون» takes the place of the two objects of «علم», and the hamza is given kasra because the lām comes [in the khabar].

harrat-mujtaba:159-159.t: The clause (نسبح سبحان) is resumptive. «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb that makes «سبحان» accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:160-160.t: «عباد»: excepted in a disjoined exception, accusative; that from which the exception is made is the wāw in {يَصِفُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:161-161.t: (فإنكم وما تعبدون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ is resumptive. «ما»: a relative noun conjoined to the noun of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:162-162.t: (ما أنتم عليه بفاتنين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». The bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of «ما», which acts like «ليس». The object of «فاتنين» is implied, i.e.: anyone.

harrat-mujtaba:163-163.t: His words «مَن»: excepted from the implied object «أحدا». «صال»: khabar (predicate), nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:164-164.t: The wāw is resumptive. The preposition «منا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the implied mubtadaʾ (subject) «أحد». «إلا» is for restriction. «مقام» is a second mubtadaʾ, and the preposition «له» is attached to the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ. The clause «له مقام» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied mubtadaʾ, which is preceded by negation.

harrat-mujtaba:165-165.t: (وإنا لنحن الصافون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause {وَمَا مِنَّا إِلا لَهُ مَقَامٌ}. «نحن الصافون» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:166-166.t: (وإنا لنحن المسبحون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause «إنا لنحن الصافون».

harrat-mujtaba:167-167.t: (وإن كانوا ليقولون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive. «إنْ» is lightened and left inoperative, and the lām is the distinguishing one (al-lām al-fāriqa).

harrat-mujtaba:168-168.t: (لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl). The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from «أن» and what follows it is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied (ثبت, "it were established"). The preposition «من الأولين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ذكرا».

harrat-mujtaba:169-169.t: The clause «لكنا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:170-170.t: The clause «فكفروا» is resumptive, and the clause «فسوف يعلمون» is conjoined to the clause «فكفروا».

harrat-mujtaba:171-171.t: (ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive. The preposition «لعبادنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كلمتنا».

harrat-mujtaba:172-172.t: (إنهم لهم المنصورون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is explicative of the word, and the clause «هم المنصورون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:173-173.t: (وإن جندنا لهم الغالبون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the preceding one.

harrat-mujtaba:174-174.t: (فتول عنهم حتى حين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive. «حتى» is a particle of limit and of the genitive; «حين» is a genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تولَّ».

harrat-mujtaba:175-175.t: The clause «فسوف يبصرون» is conjoined to the clause «أبصرهم».

harrat-mujtaba:176-176.t: (أفبعذابنا يستعجلون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ is resumptive, and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «يستعجلون»; the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:177-177.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to {يَسْتَعْجِلُونَ}. The fāʾ in «فساء» is connective (rābiṭa), and it is obligatory; [«ساء» is] a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e.: their morning.

harrat-mujtaba:178-178.t: (وتول عنهم حتى حين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «حين» is a noun made genitive by «حتى», and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:179-179.t: The clause «وأبصر» is conjoined to the clause «تولّ», and the clause «فسوف يبصرون» is conjoined to the clause «أبصر».

harrat-mujtaba:180-180.t: «عَمَّا» is composed of the preposition «عن» and the maṣdar-forming «ما»; the maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (أسبح, "I glorify"). The second «ربِّ» is a badal (substitute).

harrat-mujtaba:181-181.t: (وسلام على المرسلين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «سلام» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause (نسبح).

harrat-mujtaba:182-182.t: (والحمد لله رب العالمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to «سلام على المرسلين», and «رب» is a badal (substitute).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying, the Exalted, بزينة الكواكب: whoever puts الكواكب in the genitive and gives بزينة nunation — this is a genitive reading from ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza — makes الكواكب a badal (substitute) for زينة, because they (the stars) are the adornment. [Translator's note: the source has «الوينة», evidently a misprint for «الزينة».] Abū Bakr read from ʿĀṣim with الكواكب in the accusative and زينة nunated, on the view that he made زينة govern الكواكب and put it in the accusative by it, its implied form being "by Our having adorned the stars in it". It has also been said that the accusative is by an implied أعني ("I mean"); its implied form is (also) a badal from زينة according to its position. As for the reading of the majority, with the nunation dropped and the construct (iḍāfa), it is the obvious one, because it is on the implied sense "We adorned the lowest heaven with the adorning of the stars", i.e. with the beauty of the stars. It is also possible that the nunation was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents and that الكواكب is a badal for زينة, like the reading of whoever nunated زينة.

His saying وحفظا is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and We guarded it with a guarding".

mekki-muskil:8-8.t:
His saying لا يسمعون إلى الملأ: إلى entered with يسمعون, in the reading of whoever pronounced the sīn without doubling, though it does not need a preposition, only because it was treated like its reflexive counterpart (muṭāwiʿ), which is يستمع: just as يستمع takes its object with إلى, يسمع took its object with إلى, since (the patterns) افتعلت and تفعّلت are the same in transitivity. يسّمع (yassammaʿu) is the reflexive of سمّع, and استمع is likewise the reflexive of سمع, so سمع took its object in the same way as its reflexive.

[Translator's note: the source reads «وفعلت في التعدي سواء فيسمع مطاوع س سمع», which is garbled; the rendering above follows the evident sense.]

It has also been said that the meaning of إلى entering here is that it is construed according to the sense, because the meaning is "they do not incline their hearing toward them". One says سمعت إليه كلاما, i.e. "I inclined my hearing toward him".

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying {بل عجبت}: whoever gives the tāʾ ḍamma makes it a statement by the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace, about himself, or a statement by every believer about himself, of wonder at the disbelievers' denial of the resurrection despite the established power to originate creation in the first place. It is thus like the reading with fatḥa on the tāʾ, in that the wonder is from the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace. Similar to it in the reading of whoever gives the tāʾ ḍamma is His saying أسمع بهم وأبصر, i.e. they are among those of whom it ought to be said "how well they hear and how well they see on the Day of Resurrection!"; and similar to it is فما أصبرهم على النار.

His saying دحورا is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of يقذفون is يدحرون ("they are driven off").

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying {مَا لكم لَا تناصرون}: (لا تناصرون) is in the accusative position as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in لكم. مَا is an interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لكم the khabar (predicate), just as you say مالك قائما ("what is with you, standing?").

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ}: it may be in the accusative position as the khabar of كان, or in the nominative position as the khabar of إنّ, with كان treated as inoperative (mulghā).

His saying {لذائقوا الْعَذَاب}: العذاب is genitive by the construct (iḍāfa). In (ordinary) speech the accusative is permissible, with لذائقو governing it, assuming that the nūn was dropped for lightness, as in construct.

His saying فواكه is nominative as a badal (substitute) for رزق, or as "they are fruits", i.e. possessors of fruits.

[Translator's note: لذائقوا العذاب is āya 38 and فواكه is āya 42, though they are printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {لَا فِيهَا غول}: غول is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and فيها the khabar (predicate). It is not permissible to make it indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa with لا, because you have separated it from لا by the ẓarf (adverbial phrase).

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {هَل أَنْتُم مطلعون}: it is related that some read it مُطْلِعونِ, without doubling and with kasra on the nūn. That is not permissible, because it combines the construct (iḍāfa) with the nūn; it ought to have said مُطْلِعِيَّ, with a doubled yāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His saying فاطلع: the reading is with doubling; it is a past verb on the pattern افتعل. It has also been read فأُطْلِعَ, on the pattern أفعل; it is also a past verb, equivalent to اطّلع. One says طلع, أطلع and اطّلع with one meaning.
