muyesser-irab:139-139.t: ﴿وإن يونس لمن المرسلين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, or resumptive; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «يونس» is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «من المرسلين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of «إن»; and the clause «وإن يونس...» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:140-140.t: ﴿إذ أبق إلى الفلك المشحون﴾: «إذ» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «المرسلين», i.e. he is one of the messengers even in this situation; «أبق» is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause «أبق» is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); «إلى الفلك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أبق»; and «المشحون» is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:141-141.t: ﴿فساهم فكان من المدحضين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ساهم» is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو ("he"); «فكان» is conjoined to «فساهم»; «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, its noun being latent, its implied form being هو; and «من المدحضين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna.

muyesser-irab:142-142.t: ﴿فالتقمه الحوت وهو مليم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to an omitted clause understood from the context of the speech, i.e. "so they cast him into the sea, and the whale swallowed him" (فألقوه في البحر فالتقمه الحوت); and it is said: "so he threw himself into the water" (فألقى نفسه في الماء). «التقمه» is a past verb; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), placed first; «الحوت» is the fāʿil (agent), placed later; the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl); «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «مليم» is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:143-143.t: ﴿فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «لولا» is a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd); «أن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the noun of «كان» being latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو ("he"); «من المسبحين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of «كان»; the clause of «كان» is the khabar of «أن»; and أن together with what falls within its scope is a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar being obligatorily omitted.

muyesser-irab:144-144.t: ﴿للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون﴾: the lām is the one occurring in the answer of lawlā; «لبث» is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو ("he"); «في بطنه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لبث», or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "settled" (مستقرًا); «إلى يوم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «لبث»; the clause «يبعثون» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and «يبعثون» is an imperfect verb built for one whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:145-145.t:
﴿فنبذناه بالعراء﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to an omitted clause, i.e. "We commanded the whale to cast him out, so We cast him out" (أمرنا الحوت بنبذه فنبذناه); «نبذناه» is a past verb, «نا» is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وهو سقيم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «سقيم» is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:146-146.t: ﴿وأنبتنا عليه شجرة من يقطين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «أنبتنا» is conjoined to «فنبذناه»; «أنبتنا» is a past verb, and «نا» is the fāʿil (agent); «عليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنبتنا»; «شجرة» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and «من يقطين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «شجرة».

muyesser-irab:147-147.t: ﴿وأرسلناه إلى مائة ألف أو يزيدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «أرسلناه» is a past verb, «نا» is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «إلى مائة ألف» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أرسلناه»; «أو» is a conjunction; and «يزيدون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).

muyesser-irab:148-148.t: ﴿فآمنوا فمتعناهم إلى حين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «آمنوا» is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the fāʾ is a conjunction; «متعناهم» is a past verb, «نا» is the fāʿil, and «هم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and «إلى حين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متعناهم».

muyesser-irab:149-149.t: ﴿فاستفتهم ألربك البنات ولهم البنون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «استفتهم» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت ("you"), and «هم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); «لربك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) placed first; «البنات» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later; the wāw is a conjunction; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar placed first; and «البنون» is a mubtadaʾ placed later.

muyesser-irab:150-150.t: ﴿أم خلقنا الملائكة إناثا وهم شاهدون﴾: أم is a conjunction; «خلقنا» is a past verb, and «نا» is the fāʿil (agent); «الملائكة» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «إناثًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl); «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «شاهدون» is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:151-151.t: ﴿ألا إنهم من إفكهم ليقولون﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; «ألا» is a particle of drawing attention (tanbīh); «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «هم» is its noun; «من إفكهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يقولون»; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause «يقولون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنهم»; and يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:152-152.t: ﴿ولد الله وإنهم لكاذبون﴾: «ولد» is a verb, a past verb [Translator's note: the source repeats the word "verb" (فعل فعل ماض), apparently a typographical slip]; «الله» is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl); the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl); «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «هم» is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and «كاذبون» is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:153-153.t: ﴿أصطفى البنات على البنين﴾: the hamza with fatḥa is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); «اصطفى» is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو ("He"), referring to Allah; «البنات» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative with the kasra; and «على البنين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اصطفى».

muyesser-irab:154-154.t:
﴿ما لكم﴾: «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate), the implied form being: "what is established and settled for you" (ما ثبت واستقر لكم); it is an interrogative of disapproval; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿كيف تحكمون﴾: «كيف» is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is an interrogative of disapproval and of astonishment at their judgement; «تحكمون» is an imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:155-155.t: ﴿أفلا تذكرون﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to an omitted clause understood from the context, i.e. "have you become blind to the realities and strayed from the evidences?" (أعميتم عن الحقائق وضللتم عن الشواهد); «لا» is negating; and «تذكرون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:156-156.t: ﴿أم لكم سلطان مبين﴾: «أم» is a conjunction for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) placed first; «سلطان» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later; and «مبين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سلطان».

muyesser-irab:157-157.t: ﴿فأتوا بكتابكم إن كنتم صادقين﴾: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition); «ائتوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «بكتابكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ائتوا»; إن is conditional; «كنتم» is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; «صادقين» is its khabar (predicate); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:158-158.t:
﴿وجعلوا بينه وبين الجنة نسبا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; «جعلوا» is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «بينه» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «جعلوا»; «بين الجنة» is conjoined; «نسبًا» is the first object of «جعلوا»; and the clause «وجعلوا...» is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ولقد علمت الجنة إنهم لمحضرون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «علمت» is a past verb; «الجنة» is the fāʿil; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «هم» is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «محضرون» is its khabar (predicate); and إن together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of «علمت».

muyesser-irab:159-159.t: ﴿سبحان الله عما يصفون﴾: «سبحان»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an omitted verb. The word of majesty (Allah): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «عما»: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سبحان»; «يصفون»: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «يصفون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted. And the clause «سبحان الله...» is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:160-160.t: ﴿إلا عباد الله المخلصين﴾: «إلا» is a particle of exception meaning "but" (لكن); «عباد الله» is excepted from the wāw in «تجزون» [Translator's note: «تجزون» does not occur in this passage; it appears in 37:39, where the same exception «إلا عباد الله المخلصين» follows (37:40). The note seems to have been carried over from there; here the exception is from the subject of «يصفون» (37:159) or of «لمحضرون» (37:158)]; and «المخلصين» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «عباد الله».

muyesser-irab:161-161.t: ﴿فإنكم وما تعبدون﴾: the fāʾ gives the reason (taʿlīliyya); «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and the kāf is its noun; the wāw is the wāw of accompaniment (maʿiyya); «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); «تعبدون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «تعبدون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; or «ما» is conjoined to the noun of inna, and the khabar (predicate) of inna is the clause «ما أنتم» in the following ayah.

muyesser-irab:162-162.t: ﴿ما أنتم عليه بفاتنين﴾: «ما» is the Ḥijāzī negating mā, which operates like laysa; «أنتم» is the noun of mā; «عليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فاتنين»; «بفاتنين»: the bāʾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and «فاتنين» is the khabar (predicate) of the Ḥijāzī «ما», accusative in position and genitive in form by the bāʾ; and the clause «ما أنتم...» is the khabar of «إن» in the previous ayah.

muyesser-irab:163-163.t: ﴿إلا من هو صال الجحيم﴾: إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and «من» is the object of فاتنين, the exception being emptied (mufarragh); or the object of فاتنين is omitted, i.e. "anyone" (أحدًا), in which case إلا is a particle of exception and «مَن» is excepted (mustathnā) from the omitted object; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and صال is the khabar (predicate), nominative with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; الجحيم is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause «هو صال الجحيم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:164-164.t: ﴿وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ما is negating; منا is a khabar (predicate) placed first, and the mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted, its adjective standing in its place, the implied form being: "and there is none of us but has a known station" (وما منا أحد إلا له مقام معلوم); or منا is an adjective of an omitted word which is the mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the clause «إلا له مقام معلوم»; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); له is a khabar placed first; مقام is a mubtadaʾ placed later; معلوم is an adjective (ṣifa); and the clause «وما منا إلا...» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:165-165.t: ﴿وإنا لنحن الصافون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «نا» is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «الصافون» is the khabar (predicate) of «نحن»; and the nominal clause is the khabar of «إن»; or «نحن» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and «الصافون» is the khabar of «إن»; and the object of «الصافون» is omitted, i.e. "we align our feet" (نصف أقدامنا).

muyesser-irab:166-166.t: ﴿وإنا لنحن المسبحون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «نا» is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «المسبحون» is the khabar (predicate) of «نحن»; and the nominal clause is the khabar of «إن»; or «نحن» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and «المسبحون» is the khabar of «إن».

muyesser-irab:167-167.t: ﴿وإن كانوا ليقولون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن» is lightened from the heavy (inna) and inoperative (muhmala); «كانوا» is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, and the wāw is its noun; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); «يقولون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause «يقولون» is the khabar (predicate) of «كانوا».

muyesser-irab:168-168.t: ﴿لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين﴾: «لو» is conditional; «أن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «عندنا» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of «أن», placed first; «ذكرا» is the noun of anna; anna together with what falls within its scope is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e. "it were established" (ثبت); and «من الأولين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «ذكرًا».

muyesser-irab:169-169.t: ﴿لكنا عباد الله المخلصين﴾: the lām is the one occurring in the answer of «لو»; «كنا» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and «نا» is its noun; «عباد الله» is its khabar (predicate); the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; and «المخلصين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عباد الله».

muyesser-irab:170-170.t: ﴿فكفروا به فسوف يعلمون﴾: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (implying an unstated clause); «كفروا» is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «به» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كفروا»; the fāʾ is a conjunction; «سوف» is a particle of the future; and «يعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:171-171.t: ﴿ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «سبقت» is a past verb; «كلمتنا» is the fāʿil (agent); «لعبادنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سبقت»; and «المرسلين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عبادنا».

muyesser-irab:172-172.t: ﴿إنهم لهم المنصورون﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and «هم» is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «المنصورون» is the khabar (predicate) of «هم»; and the clause is the khabar of «إنهم»; or «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and «المنصورون» is the khabar of inna.

muyesser-irab:173-173.t: ﴿وإن جندنا لهم الغالبون﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «جندنا» is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «الغالبون» is the khabar (predicate) of «هم»; and the clause is the khabar of «إنهم» [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently carried over from the previous ayah; here the particle is «إن» with its noun «جندنا»]; or «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and «الغالبون» is the khabar of «إن».

muyesser-irab:174-174.t: ﴿فتول عنهم حتى حين﴾: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (implying an unstated condition); «تول» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, its fāʿil (agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت ("you"); «عنهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تول»; «حتى» is a particle of limit and a preposition; «حين» is a noun, genitive (majrūr) by «حتى»; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تول».

muyesser-irab:175-175.t: ﴿وأبصرهم فسوف يبصرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «أبصرهم» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and «هم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ links the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); «سوف» is a particle of the future; «يبصرون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e. "what will befall them as the recompense of their disbelief" (ما يحيق بهم جزاء كفرهم).

muyesser-irab:176-176.t: ﴿أفبعذابنا يستعجلون﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative; the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to an omitted clause, implied according to the situation; «بعذابنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يستعجلون»; and «يستعجلون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:177-177.t: ﴿فإذا نزل بساحتهم فساء صباح المنذرين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) of the future containing the sense of a condition; «نزل» is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو ("it"), i.e. the punishment; «بساحتهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نزل»; the fāʾ links the answer of «إذا»; «ساء» is an invariable (jāmid) verb for expressing blame (dhamm); «صباح المنذرين» is the fāʿil, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "their morning" (صباحهم); and it is said: the pronoun of «ساء» refers to the one specified, the tamyīz (specification) is omitted, and «صباح المنذرين» is the one specified for blame and not the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:178-178.t: ﴿وتول عنهم حتى حين﴾: conjoined to what preceded; «تول» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, its fāʿil (agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت ("you"); «عنهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تول»; «حتى» is a particle of limit and a preposition; «حين» is a noun, genitive (majrūr) by «حتى»; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تول».

muyesser-irab:179-179.t: ﴿وأبصر فسوف يبصرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «أبصر» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is also latent [Translator's note: so in the source (مستتر); an object is not normally described as latent — it is omitted, as the entry itself says at the end]; the fāʾ links the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); «سوف» is a particle of the future; «يبصرون» is an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e. "what will befall them as the recompense of their disbelief" (ما يحيق بهم جزاء كفرهم).

muyesser-irab:180-180.t: ﴿سبحان ربك رب العزة عما يصفون﴾: سبحان: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an omitted verb; and ربك: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «رب العزة» is a badal (substitute); «عما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سبحان»; «يصفون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause «يصفون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما», with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:181-181.t: ﴿وسلام على المرسلين﴾: «سلام» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «على المرسلين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:182-182.t: ﴿والحمد لله رب العالمين﴾: «الحمد» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «لله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); and «رب العالمين» is a badal (substitute) or an adjective (ṣifa).

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reported (أنهم) with a fatḥa on the hamza. Al-Kisāʾī said: that is, "because they" (لأنهم) and "in that they" (بأنهم).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: In the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: Qatāda said: surrendering in the punishment of Allah.

nahhas-irab:27-28.t: وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ: the ignorant person may imagine that this is related to the saying of the Majestic and Mighty: فَلا أَنْسابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَلا يَتَساءَلُونَ [al-Muʾminūn: 101], but it has nothing to do with it, because His saying, Majestic and Mighty, فَلا أَنْسابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَلا يَتَساءَلُونَ means only that they will not ask one another by the ties of kinship, one of them saying: "I ask you by the kinship that is between me and you either to benefit me, to drop a right you have against me, or to grant me a good deed" — because before it comes: فلا أنساب بينهم, that is, they will not benefit from the lineages that are between them, as has come in the ḥadīth: «On the Day of Resurrection a man will be glad that some right be established in his favour against his father or his son so that he may take it from him, because it is good deeds and bad deeds» ] «[Translator's note: a stray bracket stands here in the source.]», and in another ḥadīth: «May Allah have mercy on a man whose brother had a grievance against him concerning wealth or honour, and he went to him and asked to be absolved of it before he demanded it of him, so that he would take from his good deeds; and if he had no good deeds, some of the bad deeds of the claimant would be added to him». And «يتساءلون» here means only that they ask one another and reproach one another for having led him astray or opened for him a door of disobedience. What makes that clear is that after it comes: إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ. Saʿīd said on the authority of Qatāda: that is, you came to us by way of the path of good and turned us away; and something similar is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās. It has also been said: you came to us from the right, from the direction that we love and to which we yield, and you deceived us by that. The Arabs take a good omen from what is on the right and call it al-sāniḥ (the auspicious [bird or animal] passing from left to right). It has also been said: you came to us in the manner of one who, if he swore to us, we would believe him.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: Qatāda said: this is a saying of the devils to them.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: سُلْطانٍ is in the position of the nominative, because «من» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis. بَلْ كُنْتُمْ قَوْماً طاغِينَ: that is, increasing in disbelief; and one says طغى الماء (the water rose) when it increases.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنا قَوْلُ رَبِّنا: that is, what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, wrote for us has become binding upon us, and what He made known to His angels, may Allah's blessings be upon them all. This accords with the ḥadīth: «Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has written for the Fire its people and for the Garden its people; none will be added to them and none taken away from them».

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: That is, we were a cause of your going astray.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: That is, the one led astray and the one who leads astray. Were it outside the Qurʾān, the accusative of مشتركين would be permissible.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: The kāf of كذلك is in the position of the accusative, as a naʿt (adjective) of an [omitted] maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: يستكبرون may be in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كان; and it may be in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «إنّ», with كان being inoperative (mulghāh).

nahhas-irab:38-38.t:
The original is لذائقون; the nūn was dropped for lightness, and it was put in the genitive because of the iḍāfa (genitive construct). The accusative is also permissible, as Sībawayh recited: [al-Mutaqārib] 367-
فألفيته غير مستعتب ... ولا ذاكر الله إلّا قليلا
(I found him not seeking to make amends, nor remembering Allah except a little.)
And Sībawayh permitted وَالْمُقِيمِي الصَّلاةِ [al-Ḥajj: 35] on this basis.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: فَواكِهُ is a badal (substitute) for رزق.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: ʿIkrima said: they do not look at one another's backs. And سرر (with the rāʾ unvowelled) is permissible, because of the heaviness of the ḍamma together with the doubling.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
It is reported that Ibn ʿAbbās said: [the cup is] wine; and that Mujāhid said: it is a white wine; and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: every كأس in the Qurʾān is wine. Someone trustworthy among the people of language reported that the Arabs say of a drinking vessel, when there is wine in it: كأس; and if there is no wine in it, it is a قدح (bowl) — just as a table, when there is food on it, is called مائدة, and if there is no food on it, it is not called مائدة. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: and similar is ظعينة, said of a camel-litter when there is a woman in it. Abū Isḥāq said: بكأس من معين:
wine whose springs run over the face of the earth.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: He said: and لَذَّةٍ means "possessing delight" (ذات لذّة).

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: لا فِيها غَوْلٌ وَلا هُمْ عَنْها يُنْزَفُونَ (47) لا فِيها غَوْلٌ: one also says, with the same meaning, غيلة and غائلة; it is whatever harms a person, such as headache or something else. وَلا هُمْ عَنْها يُنْزَفُونَ is the reading of the people of Medina, the people of Basra and ʿĀṣim; and the rest of the Kufans except ʿĀṣim read يُنْزَفُونَ with a kasra on the zāy. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading is clearer and sounder in meaning, because the meaning of «ينزفون» according to the eminent exegetes, among them Mujāhid, is: their minds do not go away. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, negated of the wine of the Garden the afflictions that attach to the wine of this world, such as headache and drunkenness. As for the meaning of «ينزفون» «[Translator's note: the context requires the reading with kasra, يُنْزِفُونَ, here; the source prints the word without distinguishing vowels.]», what is correct about it is that one says أنزف الرجل when his drink has run out, and it is far-fetched that the drink of the people of the Garden be described with this; but its figurative sense would be that it means "it never runs out" (لا ينفذ) «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably لا ينفد.]».

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb that they said: they have restrained their glances to their husbands, so they do not desire others. ʿIkrima said: قاصرات الطرف means confined to their husbands. The first interpretation is clearer, because it is not in the verse مقصورات; [in] another place [there is] حُورٌ مَقْصُوراتٌ [al-Raḥmān: 72] «[Translator's note: the sentence is elliptical in the source; the sense appears to be "the verse does not say مقصورات, though elsewhere there is حُورٌ مَقْصُوراتٌ".]», from the Arabs' saying امرأة قصيرة and مقصورة when a woman is kept to her husband. عِينٌ is the plural of عيناء; its original form is فُعْل, and the ʿayn was given a kasra so that the yāʾ would not turn into a wāw.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t:
Maṭar al-Warrāq said: that is, pure eggs, that is, which hands have not soiled. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is what the Arabs say when they describe something as beautiful and clean: as though it were an ostrich's egg covered with feathers.

nahhas-irab:50-52.t:
فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ: assimilating the tāʾ into the sīn is permissible in Arabic. Al-Akhfash said: he only asked about his companion, then reported, saying: إِنِّي كانَ لِي قَرِينٌ. Saʿd ibn Masʿūd said:
And his partner was his قرين. They were two men of the Children of Israel who went into partnership in trade and made a profit of six thousand dinars. Each of them took three thousand dinars and they parted. Then one of them met his companion and said to him: "Do you know that I have married a woman of the best women of the Children of Israel for a thousand dinars?" His companion went off, took a thousand dinars and gave them in charity to the needy and the poor, and said: "O Allah, my companion has married a woman who will die and leave him, or he will grow old and she will part from him; and I ask You to marry me to a woman of the women of the people of the Garden with this thousand." Then his companion met him and said to him: "Do you know that I have bought a dwelling among the best dwellings of the Children of Israel for a thousand dinars?" His companion went off and gave a thousand dinars in charity to the poor and the needy, and said:
"O Allah, I have bought from You a dwelling among the dwellings of the people of the Garden with this thousand dinars." Then he met his companion, who said: "Do you know that I have bought a garden among the best gardens of the Children of Israel for a thousand dinars, so that I have become one of the best of them in my wife, my dwelling and my garden?" His companion went off and gave the remaining thousand in charity to the poor and the needy, and said: "O Allah, I have bought from You the Garden of Eternity with this thousand." Then his companion hired labourers for his garden, and there was his companion among them. He recognised him, called him and said to him: "Is this out of stinginess, or have you squandered your property?" So he told him the story, and he said to him: "Do you imagine that you will be raised and then requited for what you did? You are surely deluded, and this is surely false." So concerning the two of them Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed «قالَ قائِلٌ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّي كانَ لِي قَرِينٌ» up to مِنَ الْمُحْضَرِينَ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied sense is أَإِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُصَدِّقِينَ that we are to be requited (مدينون), that is, called to account and recompensed for our deeds. Then the yāʾ was dropped «[Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps the bāʾ of بأنّا is meant.]», and «إنّ» was given a kasra because in its khabar (predicate) there is the lām. And «أنك لمن المصدّقين» «[Translator's note: presumably the reading المصّدّقين, "the alms-givers", is meant.]» is not permissible, because charity has no meaning here.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t:
And it is reported: هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُطَّلِعُونَ «[Translator's note: the context indicates the variant مُطْلِعُونَ is meant here; the source prints the word with the same vowelling as the standard reading.]». Abū Isḥāq said: one says طلع and أطلع with one meaning. And it has been reported: هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُطَّلِعُونَ with a kasra on the nūn; this is a solecism (laḥn) that is not permissible, because it combines the nūn with the iḍāfa (genitive construct); were it in construct, it would be هل أنتم مطلعيّ — even though Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ reported something similar, and recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 368-
هم القائلون الخير والآمرونه ... إذا ما خشوا من محدث الأمر معظما
(They are the ones who speak good and command it, whenever they fear a grave turn of events.)
Al-Farrāʾ's version is «والفاعلونه». Sībawayh alone recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 369-
ولم يرتفق والنّاس محتضرونه ... جميعا وأيدي المعتفين رواهقه
(He did not lean back at ease while the people all attended him and the hands of the suppliants pressed upon him.)
And al-Farrāʾ alone recited: [al-Wāfir] 370-
وما أدري وظنّي كلّ ظنّ ... أمسلمني إلى قومي شراح
(I do not know — and my thought is every kind of thought — whether Shurāḥ will hand me over to my people.)
As for the two verses that Sībawayh recited, al-Farrāʾ sharing with him in one of them, it is not known who composed them, and no proof is established by them; and even if it were known who composed them, they would be anomalous (shādhdh), outside the speech of the Arabs, and what is like this is not used as proof concerning the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, nor does it enter into eloquent speech.
As for the verse that al-Farrāʾ recited, what is to be said about it is what Abū Isḥāq reported; he said: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd recited it to us «أأسلمني». And al-Farrāʾ claimed that by شراح he means شراحيل; and this is among the ugliest of poetic licences, to truncate (tarkhīm) a name outside the vocative. «هل أنتم مطلعون» with a kasra on the nūn is not permitted only because it comes to something that is not separated from what precedes it by the nūn, and this has no justification. This is the view of trustworthy grammarians, among them Muḥammad ibn Yazīd; and it is also the view of al-Farrāʾ, except that he spoiled it afterwards by saying: ضاربني is made to resemble يضربني.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: And it is reported: فَاطَّلَعَ فَرَآهُ «[Translator's note: here too the variant (presumably فَأُطْلِعَ / فأَطَّلِعَ) is printed in the standard vowelling.]». There are two views on it. One is that it is an imperfect (future) verb, that is, "so I look", and it is accusative as the answer to the question. The second view is that it is a past verb, أطلع and اطّلع being one and the same. فَرَآهُ فِي سَواءِ الْجَحِيمِ: from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: in its middle, with thorns (al-ḥasak) around him.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: Al-Kisāʾī said: that is, لثهّلكني «[Translator's note: so in the source; read لتهلكني, "to destroy me".]». Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: if it were said: لتردين means "to cast me into the Fire", it would be permissible.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: What follows لولا is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted. Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, I would have been with you in the Fire, brought [to it].

nahhas-irab:58-59.t: إِلَّا مَوْتَتَنَا الْأُولى may be an exception not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) [in the accusative], because it is qualified by an adjective.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: هو may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of «إنّ»; and هو may be a separating pronoun (fāṣila).

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: The original is ليعمل with a kasra on the lām; the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness. The implied sense — and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best — is: فليعمل العاملون لمثل هذا. If someone says: the fāʾ in Arabic indicates that the second comes after the first, so how can what follows it be intended as placed before? The answer is that the fronting is like the postponement, because the proper place of prepositions and what goes with them is to come later.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: أَذلِكَ خَيْرٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); نُزُلًا is by way of clarification (tamyīz, specification). The meaning is: Is the bliss of the people of the Garden better as a hospitality, or the tree of al-Zaqqūm better as a hospitality? النزل in the language is provision that is ample; likewise النُّزْل and النُّزُل. However, النُّزْل with the zāy unvowelled may be a dialectal form, or its original may be النُّزُل with the ḍamma dropped for its heaviness. From it is: أقيم للقوم نزلهم (the people's hospitality was provided). Its derivation is that it is the nourishment with which it is fitting for them to alight and stay. The tree of al-Zaqqūm is derived from التزقّم, which is swallowing with effort and hardship; it was called the tree of al-Zaqqūm because they swallow it with effort, and it sticks in their throats because of its loathsomeness and stench.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: إِنَّها شَجَرَةٌ: the khabar (predicate) of «إن». It is not permissible to drop the alif from «إنها» as the wāw is dropped from إنه, because of the heaviness of the wāw and the lightness of the alif. تَخْرُجُ فِي أَصْلِ الْجَحِيمِ is a khabar after a khabar, like كَلَّا إِنَّها لَظى نَزَّاعَةً لِلشَّوى [al-Maʿārij: 16]; and تخرج may be a naʿt (adjective) of الشجرة.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: طَلْعُها is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is in the clause; or you make the kāf mean "like" (مثل), so it is the khabar.

nahhas-irab:66-68.t: فَإِنَّهُمْ لَآكِلُونَ مِنْها: the lām entered for emphasis, and likewise لَشَوْباً. Al-Farrāʾ reported: شاب طعامه وشرابه (he mixed his food and drink) when he mixes them with something other than them; يشوبهما شوبا وشابة.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: الإهراع is hastening with something like trembling in it. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: المهرع is المستحب «[Translator's note: so in the source; probably المستحثّ, "the one urged on".]»; one says: جاء فلان يهرع إلى النار (so-and-so came hastening to the fire) when the cold urges him towards it. Abū Isḥāq reported:
هرع and أهرع, both.

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: وَلَقَدْ نادانا نُوحٌ: from calling (nidāʾ) that is a cry for help and supplication. فَلَنِعْمَ الْمُجِيبُونَ: al-Kisāʾī said: and excellent answerers to him We were.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: وَنَجَّيْناهُ وَأَهْلَهُ: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t: وَجَعَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ: the first object; هُمُ is redundant (zāʾida), called the separating pronoun (fāṣila); الْباقِينَ is the second object. As for the meaning of وَجَعَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ هُمُ الْباقِينَ, among the best of what has been reported about it is what is mentioned from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty, وَجَعَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ هُمُ الْباقِينَ: that all people are of the descendants of Noah ﷺ «[Translator's note: the source uses the blessing formula صلّى الله عليه وسلّم for Noah.]», and that all of them are from three sons of Noah: Sām, Ḥām and Yāfith. The Arabs — meaning their Yemenis and their Nizār — and the Byzantines and the Persians are of the descendants of Sām; the blacks — meaning their races, of Sind, Hind, the Zaghāwa and others — and the Berbers and the Copts are of the descendants of Ḥām; and the Slavs, the Turks and Gog and Magog are of the descendants of Yāfith. And goodness is in the descendants of Sām. Abū Jaʿfar said: I have treated نوح and سام as declinable (fully inflected), even though they are foreign names, because they consist of three letters and so are light. This is the correct view; and it has been said that they are Arabic and derived.

nahhas-irab:78-79.t: Al-Kisāʾī claimed that there are two implied constructions in it. One is: and We left upon him among later generations [the saying]: it is said: سلام على نوح, that is, We left upon him this praise; this is the doctrine of Abū al-ʿAbbās, who said: the Arabs often omit "saying". The other view is that the meaning is: and We cast upon him — and the sentence is complete — then He began anew and said: سلام على نوح. Al-Kisāʾī said: and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is سلاما, accusative by تركنا, that is, We left upon him good praise.

nahhas-irab:80-80.t: That is, the good praise remains for them; and the kāf is in the position of the accusative, that is, a recompense like that.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا الْآخَرِينَ (82): the singular is آخر. Its basic usage is for «من» to be with it, but it was omitted because the meaning is known: something is not called آخر unless there is with it something of its own kind.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī said: I asked Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn: what is the sound heart? He said: the one sincere towards Allah regarding His creatures.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t: «ما» may be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «ذا» its khabar (predicate); and «ما» and «ذا» may be in the position of the accusative by تعبدون.

nahhas-irab:86-86.t: أَإِفْكاً is accusative by تعبدون. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: الإفك is the worst of lying, that which does not stand firm and is unsteady; and from it is ائتفكت بهم الأرض (the earth was overturned with them). آلِهَةً is a badal (substitute) for إفك.

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: فَما ظَنُّكُمْ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:88-88.t: It may be the plural of نجم (star), and it may be a singular, a maṣdar (verbal noun); this is the view of al-Khalīl, that is, in the opinion that appeared (نجم) to him.

nahhas-irab:89-89.t:
From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ill. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, stricken with plague, so that they would move away from him lest he infect them. Abraham spoke the truth in this, because everyone will become ill with death, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ [al-Zumar: 30]. So the meaning is: I shall be ill in what is to come, and they imagined that he was ill at that hour.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a case of indirect speech (maʿārīḍ al-kalām).

nahhas-irab:91-94.t:
فَراغَ إِلى آلِهَتِهِمْ فَقالَ أَلا تَأْكُلُونَ: he addressed them as one addresses beings endowed with reason, because they had given them that rank in their worship of them; likewise «قال ألا تأكلون», marvelling at them; likewise ما لَكُمْ لا تَنْطِقُونَ; and likewise فَراغَ عَلَيْهِمْ, and He did not say عليها or عليهنّ. ضَرْباً is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Mujāhid, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read فَأَقْبَلُوا إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ with a ḍamma on the yāʾ «[Translator's note: i.e. يُزِفُّونَ; the source prints the standard vowelling.]». Abū Ḥātim claimed that he did not know this dialectal usage, but a group of scholars knew it, among them al-Farrāʾ, who likened it to their saying أطردت الرجل, that is, I caused him to come to that [state of being driven out], whereas طردته means I drove him away. He and others recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 371-
تمنّى حصين أن يسود جذاعه ... فأضحى حصين قد أذلّ وأقهرا
(Ḥuṣayn wished to lord it over his clan of Judhāʿ, but Ḥuṣayn came to be humbled and overpowered.)
That is, he was brought to that state; and likewise «يزفّون»: they are brought to زفيف (rushing). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said:
الزفيف is hastening. Abū Isḥāq said: الزفيق «[Translator's note: so in the source; read الزفيف.]» is the first stage of the ostrich's running. Abū Ḥātim said: al-Kisāʾī claimed that some people read فَأَقْبَلُوا إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ ] «[Translator's note: i.e. the lightened يَزِفُونَ; the source prints the doubled form, followed by a stray bracket.]» from وزف يزف, like وزن يزن. This is Abū Ḥātim's report, and Abū Ḥātim did not hear anything from al-Kisāʾī. Al-Farrāʾ, who was al-Kisāʾī's companion, transmitted from al-Kisāʾī that he did not know «يزفون» with the light form. Al-Farrāʾ said: and I do not know it. Abū Isḥāq said:
Others besides them knew it: that one says وزف يزف when one hastens; but I know of no one who read «يزفون» [in this way].

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: One says نحت ينحِت and ينحَت, because there is a guttural letter in it.

nahhas-irab:96-96.t:
«ما» is in the position of the accusative, that is: and [He] created what you make. It may also be in the position of the accusative by يعملون «[Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has تعملون.]», that is: and what thing do you make?
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: when he was placed in the structure he said: Allah is sufficient for me, and how excellent a Guardian He is.

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: The original is إنّني; [a nūn] was dropped because of the clustering of the nūns.

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: That is, a righteous [son] among the righteous; such omission is frequent.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t: That is, he will be forbearing in his old age.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: the scholars differed over the one whom he was commanded to sacrifice. Most of them said: the one to be sacrificed (al-dhabīḥ) was Isaac. Among those who said that were al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and his son ʿAbd Allāh — that is what is soundly reported from him. Al-Thawrī transmitted it from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the ransomed one was Isaac. Al-Thawrī and Ibn Jurayj transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
The one to be sacrificed was Isaac. This is what is soundly reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: Shuʿba transmitted it from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that a man said: "I am the son of the noble elders", and ʿAbd Allāh said: "That is Joseph son of Jacob son of Isaac, the one to be sacrificed of Allah, son of Abraham, the Friend of Allah." Ḥammād ibn Zayd transmitted from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «The noble one, son of the noble one, son of the noble one: Joseph son of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham, may Allah's blessings be upon them all». Abū al-Zubayr transmitted from Jābir, who said: the one to be sacrificed was Isaac. That is also reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar: that the one to be sacrificed was Isaac, upon him be peace. So these are six of the Companions; and of the Successors and others, among them ʿAlqama, al-Shaʿbī, Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl, Mālik ibn Anas and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, they said: the one to be sacrificed was Isaac ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: as for those who said it was Ishmael ﷺ, there is Abū Hurayra, and he transmits it from Ibn ʿUmar. Then the scholars spoke after that. Some of them said: the explicit text of the interpretation indicates that he was Ishmael, upon him be peace, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَبَشَّرْناهُ بِإِسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا [al-Ṣāffāt: 112] — so how could He command him to sacrifice him when He had promised him that he would be a prophet? This has been said, but it is not decisive — and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best — because the good tidings of his prophethood, according to what is reported, were good tidings confirmed after the command to sacrifice him, as a reward for what he had done. As for His promise that Isaac would have a son — so how could He command him to sacrifice him? — it is possible that a child was born to Isaac other than [the promised] child, because he had already reached the age of striving. The apparent sense of the revelation indicates that the one to be sacrificed was Isaac, because He, Majestic and Mighty, reported that He ransomed the forbearing boy of whom Abraham was given good tidings when he said: هَبْ لِي مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ. So the ransomed one is the one of whom he was given good tidings, and He has made clear that the one of whom he was given good tidings is Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob; and that every place in the Qurʾān that mentions His giving him good tidings of a son, it is Isaac, a prophet — that is, His giving him good tidings in His saying فبشرناه بغلام حليم refers only to Isaac. As for the argument of those who argue that the two horns of the ram were hung in the Kaʿba, it is not impossible that they were carried from Syria to Mecca; besides, a group of scholars have said that the command to sacrifice was [there] «[Translator's note: the sentence appears truncated in the source: "قد قالوا كان الأمر بالذبح".]». As for His saying إِنِّي أَرى فِي الْمَنامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فَانْظُرْ ماذا تَرى, it is among the difficult passages, and the scholars have spoken about its meaning. Some of them said: Abraham ﷺ had been commanded that, if he saw a dream in which there was such and such, he should sacrifice his son. The proponent of this view adduced as evidence that in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is إنّي أرى في المنام أفعل ما أمرت به; this is a reading by way of exegesis, indicating that he had been commanded this beforehand, since something like this is not undertaken on the basis of a dream. The proponent of this view also said: Abraham ﷺ did sacrifice him, because the meaning of ذبحت الشيء is "I cut it", and this is not something that can be abrogated in any way. He adduced as evidence the saying of Mujāhid: Isaac said to Abraham, upon them both be peace: "Do not look at my face and feel pity for me; rather, turn my face towards the ground." So Abraham took the knife and passed it over his خلفة «[Translator's note: so in the source; probably حلقه, "his throat".]», and it turned over. He said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "The knife turned over." He said: "Stab me with it", and he did; then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, ransomed him. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah ransomed him with a ram that had grazed in the Garden for forty years. Al-Ḥasan said: Allah ransomed Ishmael only with a male mountain goat (from the arwā) brought down to him from Thabīr. Abū Isḥāq said: it is said that he was ransomed with a وعل, and الوعل is the mountain ibex; but the exegetes hold that he was ransomed with a ram. فَانْظُرْ ماذا تَرى: that is, what opinion will you come up with? The people of Kufa except ʿĀṣim read فَانْظُرْ ماذا تَرى «[Translator's note: i.e. تُرِي; the source prints the standard vowelling.]».
Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is: see what you will show of your patience or your distress. Others said: its meaning is: what do you advise? Abū ʿUbayd rejected «تري» and said: this can only be from seeing with the eye specifically; Abū Ḥātim said the same. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistake; this can be from seeing with the eye and otherwise, and it is well known: one says أريت فلانا الصواب (I showed so-and-so what is right) and أريته رشده (I showed him his right course), and this is not from seeing with the eye. قالَ يا أَبَتِ افْعَلْ ما تُؤْمَرُ: the other view about Abraham's dream ﷺ is that he did not resolve to sacrifice him on account of the dream; he only laid him down awaiting the command. Do you not see that he said: يا أبت افعل ما تؤمر, that is, if you are commanded to do something, do it.

nahhas-irab:103-105.t:
فَلَمَّا أَسْلَما: Qatāda said: one of them surrendered himself to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and the other surrendered his son. وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ: it is said: he laid him face down and turned his face towards the qibla. The apodosis (jawāb) of لمّا is omitted according to the Basrans, that is: and when they had both submitted, they attained happiness and He gave them an abundant reward. The Kufans said: the apodosis is نادَيْناهُ, and the wāw is redundant (zāʾida).
Abū Jaʿfar said: the wāw is one of the particles of meaning, so it is not permissible for it to be redundant. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: فلما سلّما وناديناه أن يا إبراهيم قد صدّقت الرؤيا, that is, you have done what you were commanded and what you saw in sleep.
إِنَّا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ: that is, We reward them with deliverance from hardships in this world and the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:106-106.t:
That is, the manifest favour. One says: أبلاه الله بلاء وإبلاء when He bestows favour on him; and one may say: بلاه. Zuhayr said: [al-Ṭawīl] 372-
جزى الله بالإحسان ما فعلا بكم ... وأبلاهما خير البلاء الّذي يبلو
(May Allah reward with kindness what the two of them did for you, and grant them the best favour with which He tests.)
Some claimed that he used both dialectal forms; others said: rather, the second is from بلاه يبلوه when He tests him; for testing one only says بلاه يبلوه, and from الابتلاء one does not say بلاه. The root of all this is testing, because testing is with good and evil. He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً [al-Anbiyāʾ: 35]. Ibn Zayd said: this refers to the trial that befell him in having to sacrifice his son. He said: and this is of the disliked kind of trial.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t:
الذِّبح is the noun for what is slaughtered, and its plural is ذبوح; الذَّبح with a fatḥa is the maṣdar (verbal noun).
Al-Thawrī transmitted from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, وَبَشَّرْناهُ بِإِسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ: he said: he was given good tidings of his prophethood; and he held that the good tidings about him came twice.

nahhas-irab:113-113.t: وَبارَكْنا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلى إِسْحاقَ: that is, We made the favour firm upon them both.

nahhas-irab:115-115.t: Abū Isḥāq said concerning the meaning of وَنَجَّيْناهُما وَقَوْمَهُما مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ: from the drowning that overtook the people of Pharaoh.

nahhas-irab:116-116.t: وَنَصَرْناهُمْ: Moses, Aaron and their people. Al-Farrāʾ held that it refers to Moses and Aaron alone, and argued that two are a plural.

nahhas-irab:123-123.t: Abū Isḥāq transmitted from ʿUbayda ibn Rabīʿa, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: Isrāʾīl is Jacob, and Ilyās is Idrīs; and it has been said: he is al-Khiḍr. Al-Farrāʾ said: if you derive إلياس from الأليس, you treat it as declinable (fully inflected).

nahhas-irab:125-125.t:
Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān transmitted from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلًا.
He said: an idol. ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib transmitted from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: «أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلًا», he said: a lord. Abū Jaʿfar said: both views are correct, that is: do you call an idol that you made a lord? «أَتَدْعُونَ» means "do you name", as Sībawayh reported. وَتَذَرُونَ أَحْسَنَ الْخالِقِينَ.

nahhas-irab:126-126.t:
With the accusative «[Translator's note: i.e. اللهَ رَبَّكُمْ وَرَبَّ آبائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ; the headword is not quoted in the source.]» is the reading of al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, and Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim incline to it. Abū ʿUbayd reported that it is as a naʿt (adjective). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a mistake; it is only a badal (substitute), and the naʿt is not permissible here because it is not a description. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Nāfiʿ read الله ربكم with the nominative.
Abū Ḥātim said: in the sense of "He is Allah, your Lord". Abū Jaʿfar said: better than what he said is that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) without any implied element or omission. I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān holding that the nominative is preferable and better, because what precedes it is the end of a verse, so beginning anew (istiʾnāf) is preferable.

nahhas-irab:130-130.t:
[سَلامٌ عَلى إِلْ ياسِينَ «[Translator's note: the headword is not quoted in the source; from the discussion it is the reading سلام على آل ياسين.]»] is the reading of al-Aʿraj, Shayba and Nāfiʿ. There are two other readings of it: ʿIkrima, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read سلام على إلياسين; and al-Ḥasan read سلام على الياسين with a connective alif, as though it were «ياسين» to which the definite article al- had been prefixed. Whoever reads سلام على آل ياسين has, as it were — and Allah knows best — made his name both «الياس» and «ياسين», and then sent peace upon his family (āl), that is, the people of his religion and those who followed his way; and it is known that if peace is sent upon his family for his sake, he himself is included in the peace, as the Prophet ﷺ said: «Bless the family of Abū Awfā», and He, Majestic and Mighty, said: أَدْخِلُوا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ أَشَدَّ الْعَذابِ [Ghāfir: 46]. As for «الياسين», the scholars have more than one view about it. Hārūn transmitted from Ibn Abī Isḥāq, who said: إلياسين is like إبراهيم — he held that it is a name of his. Abū ʿUbayd held that it is a sound (masculine) plural, in the sense that peace is sent on him and the people of his way, and he recited: [al-Rajaz] 373-
قدني من نصر الخبيبين قدي
(Enough for me of supporting the Khubaybs — enough!)
He means only Abū Khubayb ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, and he put it in the plural meaning that those who followed his way are included with him. Others than Abū ʿUbayda «[Translator's note: so in the source, here "Abū ʿUbayda" after "Abū ʿUbayd" above.]» transmit it «الخبيبين» as a dual, meaning ʿAbd Allāh and Muṣʿab. Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān explaining it more fully than this. He said: the Arabs name a man's people by the name of the eminent man among them, so they say المهالبة, as though they called each one of them al-Muhallab. He said: on this basis, «سلام على الياسين» names every man of them Ilyās. Sībawayh mentioned something of this «in his Book», except that he mentioned that the Arabs do this by way of relation (nisba), saying الأشعرون, meaning relation to him. Abū ʿUbayda argued for his reading «سلام على الياسين», and that it is his name just as الياس is his name, because there is no «سلام على آل» in the sūra for any other of the prophets, may Allah bless him; and as the prophets were named, so was he named. This argument originally belongs to Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, and it is not binding, because we have made clear the view of the people of language that if peace is sent on his family for his sake, then peace is sent on him. The view that his name is both الياس and الياسين needs proof and transmission. And since there is difficulty in the matter, it was preferable to follow the script in the muṣḥaf, and in the muṣḥaf it is «سلام على آل ياسين», written separately; and in this there is no difficulty. Al-Farrāʾ ] «[Translator's note: a stray bracket stands here in the source.]» has a good view on this that is not the established one «[Translator's note: "ليس بالمشروع" in the source; perhaps "ليس بالمشهور", "not the well-known one".]», which we shall mention and explain, if Allah wills. It is that he likened it to the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْناءَ [al-Muʾminūn: 20], while He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَطُورِ سِينِينَ [al-Tīn: 2]. He said: the two have one meaning and one referent. The explanation of this is that الياس is a foreign name, and when foreign names reach the Arabs they alter them in various ways, saying إبراهيم, إبراهم and إبرهام; likewise also سيناء and سينين, and الياس, الياسين and يس in the reading «سلام على آل ياسين» have one meaning.

nahhas-irab:135-137.t:
إِلَّا عَجُوزاً is accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ), and مُصْبِحِينَ
is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:138-138.t:
وَبِاللَّيْلِ
is conjoined according to the sense, that is: in the morning and in the night.

nahhas-irab:139-139.t: [يونس] is a diptote because it is a foreign name. If it were Arabic it would be declinable, even though there is a yāʾ at its beginning, because there is no يَفْعُل pattern among verbs [matching it] — just as, if you name [someone] يعفر (Yuʿfur) you treat it as declinable, but if you name him يعفر (Yaʿfur) you do not «[Translator's note: the source does not vowel the two forms; the distinction is between a pattern found in verbs and one not found in them].»

nahhas-irab:140-140.t:
إِذْ أَبَقَ
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the root sense of أبق is "to go far away"; from it is غلام آبق and أبق (a runaway slave). Others said:
It was said of Jonah أبق only because he went out without Allah's command, Majestic and Mighty, hiding from people. إِلَى الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ
Al-Farrāʾ said: الفلك is masculine and feminine, and may be taken in the sense of a plural. Others said:
When it is taken in the sense of a plural, it is the plural of فلك, like وَثَن and وُثْن.

nahhas-irab:141-141.t:
فَساهَمَ
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: he cast lots. He said: its origin is from the arrows (sihām) that are shuffled. فَكانَ مِنَ الْمُدْحَضِينَ
That is, of those overcome by it. Al-Farrāʾ said: one says دحضت حجّته (his argument was refuted) and أدحضها الله (Allah refuted it); its origin is from slipping.

nahhas-irab:142-142.t: [مُلِيمٌ] is from ألام, when one does what he ought to be blamed for, like أحمق, so he is محمق. As for الملوم, he is the one who is blamed, whether he deserved it or not.

nahhas-irab:143-144.t:
Al-Kisāʾī said: «أنّ» is not given a kasra on account of the entry of the lām, because the lām does not belong to it. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The matter is as he said: the lām is only in the apodosis (jawāb) of لولا. From Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, «فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين»: they said: that is, of those who pray. Qatāda said: he used to pray before that, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, kept that for him and saved him. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: had he not had righteous deeds before that, لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ. He said: and it is written in the wisdom that righteous deeds raise up their owner when he stumbles «[Translator's note: the source reads "يرفع ربّه إذا عشر"; presumably "يرفع صاحبه إذا عثر".]».
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: when he said: There is no god but You, glory be to You, I have been of the wrongdoers, the whale cast him out.

nahhas-irab:145-145.t: Among the things asked about: it is said that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, reports here that he was cast onto the bare shore, while He, Majestic and Mighty, said: لَوْلا أَنْ تَدارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَراءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ [al-Qalam: 49]. The answer is that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, reports here that He cast him onto the bare shore while he was not blameworthy, and had it not been for Allah's favour upon him, Majestic and Mighty, He would have cast him onto the bare shore while he was blameworthy. Al-Akhfash reported as the plural of سقيم: سقمى, سقامى and سقام.

nahhas-irab:146-146.t: [يقطين] is the plural of يقطينة. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: every plant that has no stem and whose leaves spread over the ground is called يقطينة, such as the gourd, the melon and the colocynth. If it has a stem that holds it up, it is simply شجرة (a tree); and if it stands upright, that is, without leaves spread out, it is a نجمة, and its plural is نجم.

nahhas-irab:147-147.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: I have mentioned the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: the mission came after the whale cast him out; and it has no chain of transmission except through Shahr ibn Ḥawshab. Better than it in its chain, and sounder, is what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us; he said: al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad related to us; he said: ʿAmr al-ʿAnqarī related to us; he said: Isrāʾīl related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq «[Translator's note: so in the source; probably Abū Isḥāq.]», from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, who said: ʿAbd Allāh related to us in the treasury (bayt al-māl) about Jonah the Prophet ﷺ. He said: Jonah ﷺ threatened his people with punishment and told them that it would come to them within three days. So they separated every mother from her child, went out, cried aloud to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and sought forgiveness, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, withheld the punishment from them. And Jonah ﷺ was waiting for the punishment and saw nothing. Whoever lied and had no proof used to be killed, so Jonah ﷺ went out in anger. He came to some people in a ship, and they took him on board and recognised him. When he entered the ship, the ship stood still, while the [other] ships were moving right and left. They said: What is the matter with your ship?
They said: We do not know. Jonah, may Allah bless him, said: In it is a slave who has run away from his Lord, Majestic and Mighty, and it will not move until you throw him overboard. They said: As for you, O Prophet of Allah, we will not throw you overboard. He said: Then cast lots, and whoever loses, let him fall in. So they cast lots and Jonah, may Allah bless him, lost, but they refused to leave him [to it]. They said: Cast lots three times, and whoever loses, let him fall in. So they cast lots and Jonah, may Allah bless him, lost three times — or he said: thrice — and he fell in. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, had appointed a whale for him, and it swallowed him and went plunging down with him to the bottom of the earth. Jonah, may Allah bless him, heard the glorification of the pebbles, and he called out in the darknesses: There is no god but You, glory be to You, I have been of the wrongdoers. He said: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea and the darkness of the whale's belly. He said: فَنَبَذْناهُ بِالْعَراءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ — he said: like a plucked chick that has no feathers on it. He said: and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, caused a gourd plant to grow over him, and it grew, and he used to shade himself with it. Then it withered and he wept over it. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed to him: Do you weep over a plant that has withered, yet you do not weep over a hundred thousand or more whom you wanted to destroy? He said: Jonah ﷺ went out, and there was a boy herding [animals]. He said: Boy, who are you? He said: Of the people of Jonah. He said: When you go to them, tell them that you have met Jonah. He said to him: If you are Jonah, you know that whoever lies is killed if he has no proof; so who will testify for me? He said: This tree and this patch of ground. He said: Then command them. So Jonah, may Allah bless him, said to them: When this boy comes to you, testify for him. They said: Yes. The boy went back to his people; he was under protection and had brothers. He came to the king and said: I have met Jonah, and he sends you greetings of peace. He said: [The king] ordered that he be killed. They said: He has proof. So they sent [men] with him, and he came to the tree and the patch of ground and said to them: I adjure you by Allah, Majestic and Mighty: did Jonah ﷺ ask you to bear witness? They said: Yes. He said: So the people returned terrified, saying: The tree and the earth bore witness for him. They came to the king and told him what they had seen. ʿAbd Allāh said: The king took the boy by the hand, seated him in his own seat and said: You are more entitled to this place than I. ʿAbd Allāh said: That boy managed their affairs for them for forty years. So it has become clear in this ḥadīth that Jonah, may Allah bless him, had been sent before the whale swallowed him, by this chain of transmission, which is not something arrived at by analogy. There is also benefit in it, in that the people of Jonah, may Allah bless him, believed and repented before they saw the punishment, because in it [it says] that he told them it would come to them within three days, so they separated every mother from her child — and the fāʾ in the language indicates that the second follows the first. So the ruling of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, concerning them was like His ruling concerning others in His saying, Majestic and Mighty: فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهُمْ إِيمانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنا [Ghāfir: 85], and He, exalted be His praise, said: وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ حَتَّى إِذا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ [al-Nisāʾ: 18] — the verse. Some scholars have said: they saw the signs of the punishment and repented. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not impossible. As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic, إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ [Yūnus: 98], it is an exception not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). We have mentioned the meaning of أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ, and the view of al-Farrāʾ that it means «بل» (rather), and the view of others that it means the wāw (and), and that these two views are not sound: because this is not one of the places of «بل», since it is for turning away from the first and affirming what comes after it — and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is exalted above that — or for moving from one thing to another, and this is not the place for that. And the meaning of the wāw differs from the meaning of «أو»; if either of them meant the other, meanings would be nullified; and if that were permissible, "and We sent him to more than a hundred thousand" would have been more concise. There are two views on the verse besides these two. One is that the meaning is: and We sent him to a multitude such that, had you seen them, you would have said: they are a hundred thousand or more — the servants being addressed only according to what you know. The other view is that it is as when you say: Zayd or ʿAmr came to me, while you know which of them came to you, but you leave it vague for the one addressed.

nahhas-irab:148-149.t:
In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: فآمنوا فمتعناهم حتى حين, and the meaning is the same.
فَاسْتَفْتِهِمْ: Abū Isḥāq said: that is, ask them a question of rebuke and of making them acknowledge: أَلِرَبِّكَ الْبَناتُ وَلَهُمُ الْبَنُونَ — because the meaning of «فاستفتهم» is "so say to them".

nahhas-irab:150-150.t: إِناثاً is the plural of أنثى. Abū Isḥāq said: «أم» means "or rather, …?" (أبل). وَهُمْ شاهِدُونَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:151-151.t: أَلا إِنَّهُمْ: «إنّ» after «ألا» takes a kasra because it is at the start [of a sentence]. Sībawayh reported that after «أما» it can take a fatḥa or a kasra: the fatḥa on the basis that أما means "truly" (حقا), and the kasra on the basis that أما means ألا. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: its fatḥa is permissible after «ألا», by analogy with أما; but in the verse only the kasra is permissible, because the lām comes after it.

nahhas-irab:153-154.t: أَصْطَفَى الْبَناتِ عَلَى الْبَنِينَ is a question carrying the sense of rebuke. As for what is reported from Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Nāfiʿ, that they read وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ أَصْطَفَى الْبَناتِ with a connective alif «[Translator's note: i.e. اصْطَفَى; the source prints the standard form.]», it is not soundly reported from them. Abū Ḥātim claimed that it has no justification because after it comes ما لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ, so the speech runs on the lines of rebuke. Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading, though anomalous (shādhdh), is permissible from two angles. One is that it is an explanation of what they said, and ما لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ is cut off from what precedes it. The other angle is that the grammarians, among them al-Farrāʾ, have reported that rebuke can be with a question and without a question, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ فِي حَياتِكُمُ الدُّنْيا [al-Aḥqāf: 20]. وجعلوا بينه وبين الجنّة نسبا: most exegetes hold that الجنّة here means the angels. The people of derivation said: they were called جنّة because they are not seen. There is another, strange view, which Isrāʾīl transmitted from al-Suddī from Abū Mālik, who said: the angels were called جنّة only because they are in charge of the gardens (al-jinān), and the angels are all جنّة.

nahhas-irab:158-158.t: إنّ takes a kasra because of the entry of the lām.

nahhas-irab:160-160.t: إِلَّا عِبادَ اللَّهِ is accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ). الْمُخْلَصِينَ is their naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:161-162.t:
The exegetes are agreed, as far as I know, that the meaning is: you do not lead anyone astray except one for whom Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has decreed that he go astray. Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ transmitted from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said:
None will follow you in worshipping your gods and in your worship except one for whom Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has written that he will burn in Hell. ʿUmar ibn Dharr transmitted from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, may Allah have mercy on him: you are not misleaders إِلَّا مَنْ هُوَ صالِ الْجَحِيمِ. And from Ibn ʿAbbās: you are not misleaders except of one for whom it has been decreed that he go astray.
Abū al-Ashhab Jaʿfar ibn Ḥayyān transmitted from al-Ḥasan, who said: O sons of Iblīs, you do not lead any of the people astray except one for whom Allah has decreed that he go astray. Abū Jaʿfar said: so in this verse there is a refutation of the Qadariyya from the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Among its meanings is that the devils do not manage to lead anyone astray except one of whom Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has written that he will not be guided; had Allah, Majestic and Mighty, known that he would be guided, He would have come between him and them. On this basis is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِمْ بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ [al-Isrāʾ: 64], that is: you will not reach anything of them except what is in My knowledge. Al-Farrāʾ said: the people of the Hijaz say فتنته, and the people of Najd say أفتنته.

nahhas-irab:163-163.t:
It is reported that al-Ḥasan read إِلَّا مَنْ هُوَ صالِ الْجَحِيمِ with a ḍamma on the lām «[Translator's note: i.e. صالُ; the source prints the standard form.]». A group of Arabic scholars say: it is a solecism (laḥn), because one cannot say: هذا قاضُ, so know it. Abū Jaʿfar said: among the best of what has been said about it is what I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: it is construed according to the sense, because the meaning of «من» is a group, so the implied form is: in it, صالون; the nūn was dropped for the iḍāfa (genitive construct), and the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters. There is another view about them: that it is by metathesis (qalb); when inverted it would be صايل, then the yāʾ is dropped and one says:
صال, just as one says شاك.

nahhas-irab:164-164.t: The Arabic scholars have two implied constructions for it. One is: وما منا إلّا من له, with من dropped; this is the doctrine of the Kufans, and it involves what is plainly [objectionable], the omission of the relative noun. The other view is that the meaning is: وما منّا ملك إلّا لهم مقام معلوم «[Translator's note: so in the source, "لهم"; presumably له.]»; this is the view of the Basrans. As for the connection of this with what precedes it, it is, according to what is reported, that the angels disowned those who worshipped them and marvelled at that, because of their own striving; so He said: وما منا إلّا له مقام معلوم.

nahhas-irab:165-166.t: In the ḥadīth from Jābir ibn Samura, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were in the mosque and said: «Will you not form rows as the angels form rows before their Lord? We said: O Messenger of Allah, how do the angels form rows before their Lord? He said: They complete the rows and stand close together in the row».

nahhas-irab:167-167.t:
When «إن» is lightened, it enters upon the verb, and the lām becomes obligatory with it, to distinguish between negation and affirmation.
The Kufans say «إن» means «ما» and the lām means إلّا.

nahhas-irab:168-169.t: That is: had a reminder come to us as it came to the earlier peoples, we would have made our worship sincere.

nahhas-irab:170-170.t: فَكَفَرُوا: that is, in the reminder. Al-Farrāʾ construes it as involving an omission, that is: then Muḥammad ﷺ came to them with the Qurʾān, and they disbelieved in it. فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ: Abū Isḥāq said: that is, they will come to know the consequence of their disbelief.

nahhas-irab:171-171.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: [Our word] of felicity. Others said: the implied form is: and Our word has already gone forth for Our servants, the messengers.

nahhas-irab:172-172.t: When the lām enters, «إن» is given a kasra.

nahhas-irab:173-173.t: [لَهُمُ الْغالِبُونَ] is according to the sense; if it were according to the wording, it would be هو الغالب, like His saying: جُنْدٌ ما هُنالِكَ مَهْزُومٌ مِنَ الْأَحْزابِ [Ṣād: 11]. Al-Kisāʾī said: it came here in the plural because it is the end of a verse.

nahhas-irab:174-174.t: Qatāda said: that is, until death. Abū Isḥāq said: that is, the time until which they were granted respite.

nahhas-irab:177-177.t:
فَإِذا نَزَلَ بِساحَتِهِمْ: that is, the punishment. Abū Isḥāq said: the punishment of these people was by being killed.
ساء means بئس (how evil), and صَباحُ is nominative by it.

nahhas-irab:180-180.t: سُبْحانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ الْعِزَّةِ: as a badal (substitute). Abū Isḥāq said: the accusative is permissible as praise (ʿalā al-madḥ), and the nominative in the sense of "He is the Lord of might".

nahhas-irab:181-182.t: Were it outside the Qurʾān, the accusative would be permissible, as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:1-3.t: This [reading without assimilation] is the reading of most of the readers. Ḥamza read with assimilation in them [«والصافّات صّفّا، فالزاجرات زّجراً، فالتاليات ذّكراً»]. [Translator's note: the bracketed forms illustrate the assimilation described; the source does not spell them out.] This is the reading which Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal shrank from when he heard it. Abū Jaʿfar said: it is far-fetched in Arabic from three angles. One of them is that the tāʾ is not from the point of articulation of the ṣād, nor of the zāy, nor of the dhāl, nor is it one of their sisters; its sisters are only the ṭāʾ and the dāl; the sisters of the zāy are the ṣād and the sīn; and the sisters of the dhāl are the ẓāʾ and the thāʾ. The second angle is that the tāʾ is in one word and what follows it in another word. The third angle is that if you assimilate and say «والصافّات صّفّا», you combine two quiescent letters from two words; combining two quiescent letters in the like of this is permissible only when they are in one word, as in «دابّة». The justification of Ḥamza's reading is that the tāʾ is close in point of articulation to these letters. «والصافّات» is genitive by the wāw of the oath, and the wāw stands in place of the bāʾ; the implied form is "I swear by those ranged in rows", and its true sense is "by the Lord of those ranged in rows". «فالزاجرات» is conjoined, and likewise «فالتاليات».

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (إِلَّا مَنْ خَطِفَ الْخَطْفَةَ): there are several dialectal forms in it, some of which have been read, and they do not differ from the written form. When one takes something quickly, one says «خَطِف», «خَطَف», «خَطَّف», «خِطَّف» and «خِطِّف». [Translator's note: the source lists the five forms without vowels; they are vowelled here according to the explanation that follows.] The original of the doubled forms is «اختطف»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ because it is its sister, and the khāʾ was given fatḥa because the vowel of the tāʾ was cast onto it. Whoever gives it kasra does so because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and whoever gives the ṭāʾ kasra makes the kasra follow the kasra. (فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهابٌ ثاقِبٌ): [ثاقب] is a naʿt (adjective) of «شهاب». Abū Isḥāq said: one says «تبعه» and «أتبعه» when one goes after him. «شهاب», plural «شُهُب»; the analogical plural of paucity is «أشهبة», though it has not been heard from the Arabs. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd reported, in the plural, «شهب ثُقُب», «ثواقب» and «ثِقاب». Al-Kisāʾī reported «ثقب يثقب ثقابة وثقوباً».

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: (فَاسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَهُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَمْ مَنْ خَلَقْنا): «مَن» is in the sense of «الذين», and the meaning is "or those whom We created"; mention of the angels and others has preceded. (إِنَّا خَلَقْناهُمْ مِنْ طِينٍ لازِبٍ): al-Farrāʾ reported from the Arabs «طين لاتب» with the same meaning, i.e. sticky.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: This [«بل عجبتَ», with fatḥa on the tāʾ] is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read «بل عجبتُ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and Abū ʿUbayd follows it; he argued from the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (وَإِنْ تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ) [al-Raʿd: 5], but there is no proof in it; its meaning, according to what Abū Ḥātim said, is "if you wonder, then for you there is a wonder in their saying, and for whoever hears it there is a wonder in it". The reading with ḍamma on the tāʾ is reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and from Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah have mercy on him; Shuʿba reported it from al-Aʿmash from Abū Wāʾil from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he read «بل عجبتُ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ; and it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
