[Translator's note: the source prints both readings as (بَلْ عَجِبْتَ); the vowelling is supplied from the descriptions.] Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the meaning of the two readings is one, and the implied form is "Say, O Muḥammad: Nay, I wonder", because the Prophet ﷺ is the one addressed by the Qurʾān. This is a good view. (وَيَسْخَرُونَ) is with sīn in the main text [of the muṣḥaf]; outside the Qurʾān, according to al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, one may say «صخرت منه» with ṣād; and an anomalous dialectal form is «سخرت به» with the bāʾ. [Translator's note: the source reads «بالياء» "with yāʾ", evidently for «بالباء» "with bāʾ".]

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: I.e. they call for mockery. «إذا» is in the position of the accusative by an implied verb before it, and what comes after it does not govern it. Al-Kisāʾī reported «دخر يدخر دخوراً» (to be abased).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: (فَإِنَّما هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ واحِدَةٌ): the plural is «زَجَرات», with the jīm vowelled, to distinguish between the noun and the adjective.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: (وَقالُوا يا وَيْلَنا) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that its implied form is «يا وَيْ لنا», «وَيْ» meaning grief. Had it been as he said, it would have been [written] separate, whereas in the muṣḥaf it is joined, and we know of no one who writes it other than joined. The Kufans went further than this: some of them reported various forms, that one says «ويل للشيطان», «ويلا للشيطان», «ويل للشيطان», «ويل الشيطان», «ويل الشيطان» and «ويل الشيطان». [Translator's note: the source gives these forms without vowels, so several look identical; they differ in the case ending of «ويل» and the vowel of the lām, as the following explanation shows.] As for «وَيْلٌ للشيطان», it is clear and needs no consideration; «وَيْلاً للشيطان» is permissible in the sense of "may Allah impose woe on him"; and as for the [other] «ويل للشيطان», it is anomalous and likened to interjections (aṣwāt). As for «وَيْلَ الشيطان», according to the Basrans it is accusative, also in the sense of "may Allah impose woe on him". Al-Farrāʾ said: when their use of it became frequent, they made it like a noun joined to a noun, as they said «يا لَبكر», which is the lām of the genitive. Whoever says «ويلِ الشيطان» brought it according to the original; and whoever says «ويلُ الشيطان», the original according to him is «ويل للشيطان», then [the lām] was dropped because of the number of lāms, just as (إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْكِتابَ) [al-Aʿrāf: 196] was read, in the sense of «إنّ وليّيَ الله», with [one yāʾ] dropped because of the number of yāʾs. Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading is not known; but ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «إنّ وليَّ اللهِ الذي نزّل الكتاب», in the sense of "the friend of Allah is the one who sent down the Book — Jibrīl ﷺ, who sent down the Book"; then the naʿt (adjective) was put in the place of the qualified noun. [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variants here is not marked in the source and is supplied from the explanations; the attribution of the vowel patterns to «ويلِ» and «ويلُ» is likewise inferred.] (هذا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī said: i.e. this is the Day of Reckoning.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: «الذي» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «اليوم», and it may be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of «الفصل».

nahhas-irab:22-23.t: (احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَأَزْواجَهُمْ): [أزواجهم] is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «الذين», and its singular is «زوج». Sufyān reported from Simāk from al-Nuʿmān from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him; he said: (وَأَزْواجَهُمْ) — their companions. This is explained in the ḥadīth of Sharīk from Simāk from al-Nuʿmān; he said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَأَزْواجَهُمْ): the fornicator with the fornicator, the wine-drinker with the wine-drinker, and the thief with the thief. Sufyān reported from his father from al-Musayyab ibn Rāfiʿ from Ibn ʿAbbās: «احشروا الذين ظلموا وأزواجهم» — he said: their likes. Abū Jaʿfar said: these views are not to be rejected, because of the eminence of those who held them, and because they are known in the language: one says «هذا زوج هذا», i.e. its companion and its like; from this the man is called the «زوج» of the woman and the woman the «زوج» of the man, and two shoes are called «زوجان», because each of them is a «زوج» to its fellow; and of two one says only «زوجان». Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: (احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَأَزْواجَهُمْ) — he said: the disbelievers with the disbelievers. (وَما كانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): he said: the idols. (فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلى صِراطِ الْجَحِيمِ): one says «هديته إلى الطريق» and «هديته الطريق», i.e. I guided him to it; «أهديت الهديّة» (I gave the gift); and «هديت العروس» (I conducted the bride), and one also says «أهديتها», i.e. I made her like a gift.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: The answer to the oath. Al-Kisāʾī permitted fatḥa on «أنّ» in an oath.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: (رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) is a khabar (predicate) after a khabar; it may be a badal (substitute) for «واحد»; and it may be nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Akhfash reported «ربَّ السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وربَّ المشارق» in the accusative, as a naʿt (adjective) of the noun of «إنّ». [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with the standard nominative vowelling (رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما وَرَبُّ الْمَشارِقِ).]

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
﴿إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِزِينَةٍ الْكَواكِبِ﴾ (6)

«بزينةِ الكواكب» [without tanwīn, in genitive construct] is the reading of al-Ḥasan, the people of Medina and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, and it is the known reading of Abū ʿAmr. Yaʿqūb the reader reported that Abū ʿAmr and al-Aʿmash read «بزينةٍ الكواكبَ», with tanwīn on «زينة» and the accusative on «الكواكب»; and this is the known reading of ʿĀṣim. As for Ḥamza, he read (بِزِينَةٍ الْكَواكِبِ) with tanwīn on «زينة» and the genitive on «الكواكب». A fourth reading is permissible: «بزينةٍ الكواكبُ», with tanwīn on «زينة» and the nominative on «الكواكب». [Translator's note: the source prints the first reading with the same vowelling as Ḥamza's, (بِزِينَةٍ الْكَواكِبِ), and the others without vowels; the vowelling here follows the descriptions.] The first reading, «بزينةِ الكواكب», with the tanwīn dropped from «زينة» for the genitive construct, is a clear, good reading, i.e. "We have adorned the lowest heaven with the adornment of the stars", i.e. with their beauty. ʿĀṣim read it with tanwīn on «زينة» and the accusative on «الكواكب»; there are three views on it. The first of them is that «الكواكب» is accusative because the action falls on it, i.e. "by Our having adorned the stars", as you say «عجبتُ من ضربٍ زيداً» ("I wondered at a beating of Zayd"); and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً) [al-Balad: 14] — except that this one is better because of the separation. The second view is that the implied form is "I mean the stars". The third view, mentioned by Abū Isḥāq, is that «الكواكب» is a badal (substitute) for «زينة» according to the position, because its position is accusative. The reading of Ḥamza, (بِزِينَةٍ الْكَواكِبِ), is as a badal of a definite noun from an indefinite one.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: (وَحِفْظاً) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the verb being omitted; and it is conjoined to «زيّنّا». (مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطانٍ مارِدٍ): [مارد] is a naʿt (adjective) of «شيطان». Every insolent one of the jinn and mankind is a devil; the Arabs call him a devil.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (لا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ الْأَعْلى): this is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with doubled letters, (لا يَسَّمَّعُونَ), which is in fact the reading of the Kufans other than ʿĀṣim; the reading of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim is «لا يَسْمَعُون».] The rest of the Kufans read «لا يسّمّعون», on the basis that the original is «يتسمّعون», and the tāʾ was assimilated into the sīn because of its closeness to it. Abū ʿUbayd inclined to this reading and argued that the Arabs hardly say «سمعتُ إليه», but rather «تسمّعتُ إليه». He said: had it been «يسمعون الملأ» without «إلى», it would have been with the light form. Abū Jaʿfar said: one says «سمعتُ منه كلاماً» and «سمعتُ إليه يقول كذا», and the meaning of «سمعت إليه» is "I inclined my hearing towards him". As for his saying "had it been «يسمعون الملأ»", it seems to be an error, because one does not say «سمعتُ زيداً» and fall silent; you only say «سمعت زيداً يقول كذا وكذا»; so «يسمعون إلى الملأ» is, on this basis, clearer. Al-Aʿmash reported from Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās: (لا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ الْأَعْلى) — he said: they do not hear, while they try to listen. And this is a clear statement. (وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِنْ كُلِّ جانِبٍ).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
(دُحُوراً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read «دَحوراً» with fatḥa on the dāl, making it a maṣdar on the pattern «فَعول», like «القَبول». [Translator's note: the source prints his reading with the standard vowelling, (دُحُوراً).] As for al-Farrāʾ, he construed it as an active participle, i.e. "they are pelted with what drives them away", i.e. «بدَحور», and then the bāʾ was dropped; the Kufans use this frequently, as they recited from Jarīr: [al-Wāfir] 366-
تمرّون الدّيار ولم تعوجوا ... كلامكم عليّ إذا حرام
(You pass by the dwellings and do not turn aside — then speaking to you is forbidden to me.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: I read [this verse] before ʿUmāra ibn ʿAqīl ibn Bilāl ibn Jarīr [as] «مررتم بالديار».

nahhas-meani:1-3.t:
Of that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلصَّافَّاتِ صَفَّا. فَٱلزَّاجِرَاتِ زَجْراً. فَٱلتَّالِيَاتِ ذِكْراً﴾ [verses 1–3].
Masrūq related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, and ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, that they both said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَٱلصَّافَّاتِ صَفَّا. فَٱلزَّاجِرَاتِ زَجْراً. فَٱلتَّالِيَاتِ ذِكْراً﴾: these are all the angels.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ﴿الصَّافَّاتُ﴾ is the plural of ṣāffa, as though it were a company ranged in rows, i.e. drawn up in ranks, remembering Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and glorifying Him.
And ﴿الزَّاجِرَاتِ﴾ is the plural of zājira, i.e. those that drive the clouds, as has passed.
Qatāda said: ﴿الزاجراتُ﴾ is everything that has been forbidden — as though he means "things possessing restraint".
And it is possible that ﴿الزَّاجِرَاتُ﴾ is everything that restrains from acts of disobedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and that ﴿التَّالِيَاتُ﴾ is everything that recites the remembrance of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and His Books.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَشَارِقِ﴾.
Abū Ẓabyān related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the sun has a rising-place every day and a setting-place every day; those are the risings and the settings.
And summer has a rising-place and a setting-place, and winter has a rising-place and a setting-place; that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿رَبُّ المَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ المَغْرِبَيْنِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ ٱلْكَوَاكِبِ﴾.
As a badal (substitute). And ﴿بِزِينَةٍ الكَوَاكِبَ﴾ — Abū Ḥātim said: [meaning] "I mean the stars".
Abū Jaʿfar said: better than what he said is that it means: by Our having adorned the stars in it. And ﴿بِزِينَةٍ الكَوَاكِبُ﴾ is also possible, meaning: by the stars having adorned it, or meaning: it is the stars.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَحِفْظاً مِّن كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَّارِدٍ﴾.
That is, and We guarded it with a guarding from every rebellious devil.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لاَّ يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَىٰ ٱلْمَلإِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ﴾.
He means the angels. [Translator's note: the source has «الملاكة», a misprint for «الملائكة».]
Abū Ḥātim said: that is, so that they may not listen; then "أَنْ" was omitted and the verb became nominative (marfūʿ), as the poet said:
أَلاَ أيُّها اللاَّئِمي احْضُرُ الوَغَى * وأنْ أشْهَدْ اللَّذَّاتِ هَلْ أنْتَ مُخْلِدِي
(O you who blame me for being present at battle and for attending pleasures — can you make me live forever? — «احضر» stands for «أن أحضر».)

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جَانِبٍ دُحُوراً﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَيُقْذَفُونَ﴾ — that is, they are pelted; ﴿دُحُوراً﴾ — that is, driven away.
Qatāda said: ﴿دُحُوراً﴾ — that is, a casting into the Fire.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says "daḥarahu" when he drives him away and distances him, duḥūran and daḥran.
It is related from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [al-Sulamī] that he read ﴿دَحُوراً﴾ with fatḥa on the dāl; and maṣdars (verbal nouns) on the pattern "faʿūl" are few.
Some grammarians said: it is not a maṣdar, but means "with that which drives them away"; but if it were as he said, it would be "bi-daḥūrin", i.e. "with a distancer".
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ وَاصِبٌ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that is, perpetual.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنْ خَطِفَ ٱلْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ﴾.
One says "khaṭifa the thing" when he takes it quickly. ﴿فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda and Abū Mijlaz said: ﴿ثَاقِبٌ﴾ — that is, shining.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is well known in the language, as [the poet] said:
* "وَزَنْدُكَ أَثْقَبُ أَزْنَادِهَا" *
(And your fire-stick is the brightest-kindling of its fire-sticks.)

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَهُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَم مَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ﴾? [verse 11].
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it means the heavens, the earth and the seas.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the angels and others must be included in this along with the heavens, the earth and the seas, because "مَنْ" is not used on its own for what does not reason.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُم مِّن طِينٍ لاَّزِبٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, cleaving (lāzim).
Qatāda said: that is, sticky (lāziq).
Al-Farrāʾ holds that the bāʾ is a substitute for the mīm, and it is reported that "lātib" is said with the same meaning. Al-Nābigha said:
فَلاَ تَحْسَبونَ الخَيْرَ لاَ شَرَّ بَعْدَهُ * وَلاَ تَحْسَبُونَ الشَّرَّ ضَرْبَةَ لاَزِبِ
(Do not think good has no evil after it, nor think evil a stroke that sticks forever.)

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿بَلْ عَجِبْتَ وَيَسْخَرُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: rather you marvelled at the Book and the revelation, and they mock at what you brought.
And it has been said that the meaning is: rather you marvelled at their denial of the Resurrection.
Shurayḥ objected to its being read ﴿بَلْ عَجِبْتُ﴾ with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and said: Allah does not marvel; only one who does not know marvels.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what he said does not follow. With ḍamma on the tāʾ read "ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib", "Ibn Masʿūd" and "Ibn ʿAbbās".
The meaning of marvelling in the language is that a thing is found strange and rare, so it is marvelled at. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is the Knower of things and of what will be, but marvelling only occurs after [a thing's] coming into being.
So from Him, Majestic and Exalted, it is different from [marvelling] among humans, because He knew it before and after; it resembles the knowledge of what is witnessed, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ﴾.
And the meaning may be: Say: rather I marvel.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَوْاْ آيَةً يَسْتَسْخِرُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, they mock.
Mujāhid said: that is, they mock and ridicule.
And it has been said: ﴿يَسْتسخِرُونَ﴾ means they invite others to mockery; and this is the view of Mujāhid and Qatāda.
Its parallel in the speech of the Arabs is "qarra and istaqarra" and "ʿajiba and istaʿjaba", with the same meaning.
And the people of Kufa read ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُسْتَنْفَرَةٌ﴾, i.e. fleeing (nāfira). [Translator's note: the source cites this as a parallel of istafʿala = faʿala; the commonly reported Kufan/Medinan variant there is «مستنفَرة» (passive).]

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ نَعَمْ وَأَنتُمْ دَاخِرُونَ﴾.
The meaning: Say: yes, you will be raised, ﴿وَأَنتُمْ دَاخِرُونَ﴾ — Qatāda said: that is, abased.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t: Then He informed that this will be a single cry, and said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَإِذَا هُمْ يَنظُرُونَ﴾ — that is, they have come to life, looking.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالُواْ يٰوَيْلَنَا هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, the day on which Allah, Majestic and Mighty, requites the servants for their deeds.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ ٱلْفَصْلِ ٱلَّذِي كُنتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾.
That is, it will be said to them: yes, this is the Day of Separation, i.e. the day of separating between the doer of good and the doer of evil.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿يَوْمُ الفَصْلِ﴾ is the Day of Judgement.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱحْشُرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعْبُدُونَ. مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَٱهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ﴾.
That is, this will be said.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr from ʿUmar, said: ﴿وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ﴾ — that is, and their likes.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says "I paired (zawwajtu) the she-camel with the she-camel", i.e. I joined them; and from it the man is called zawj and the woman zawj.
And one says "I guided him (hadaytuhu) to the road", i.e. I showed him to it.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مَا لَكُمْ لاَ تَنَاصَرُونَ. بَلْ هُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ مُسْتَسْلِمُونَ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda: ﴿مَا لَكُمْ لاَ تَنَاصَرُونَ﴾? — that is, none of you defends another; ﴿بَلْ هُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ مُسْتَسْلِمُونَ﴾ — he said: that is, surrendering in the punishment.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ. قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَأْتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: this is what the unbelievers say to the devils.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: this is what humans say to the jinn. They said to them ﴿إِنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَأْتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾ — that is, from the way of Paradise, holding us back from it and turning us away.
And it has been said: this is what the followers say to those who were followed.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this resembles His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَعَنْ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾: he said: I will confuse for them the matter of their religion.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the true meaning of ﴿إِنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَأْتُونَنَا عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾ — and Allah knows best — is: you used to come to us from the direction that is the strongest of directions, namely the direction of religion, and make us doubt it.
This has also been said about His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَالسَّمَواتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ﴾; and it is well known in the speech of the Arabs — and Allah knows best what He intended. The poet said:
* "تَلَقَّاهَا عَرَابَةُ باليَمِينِ" *
(ʿArāba received it [the banner of glory] with the right hand — i.e. with strength.)
So they answered them that they themselves had been astray, and said: ﴿بَلْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ. وَمَا كَانَ لَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ﴾.
Al-Suddī said: that is, of proof.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿بَلْ كُنتُمْ قَوْماً طَاغِينَ﴾ — that is, astray; ﴿فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنَا قَوْلُ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا لَذَآئِقُونَ﴾ — that is, all of us are in the punishment; ﴿فَأَغْوَيْنَاكُمْ إِنَّا كُنَّا غَاوِينَ﴾ [verse 32].
That is, by whispering and enticement.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوۤاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لاَ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾.
That is, [too proud to accept] the oneness of Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِكَأْسٍ مِّن مَّعِينٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, of flowing wine. ﴿بَيْضَاءَ لَذَّةٍ للشَّارِبِينَ﴾ — al-Ḥasan said: the wine of Paradise is whiter than milk.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لاَ فِيهَا غَوْلٌ وَلاَ هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنزَفُونَ﴾.
Ibn [Abī] Najīḥ related from Mujāhid: ﴿لاَ فَيهَا غَوْلٌ﴾ — he said: there is no stomach-ache in it; ﴿وَلاَ هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنْزَفُونَ﴾: their minds do not go.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda: ﴿لاَ فِيهَا غَوْلٌ وَلاَ هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنْزَفُونَ﴾ — he said: their heads do not ache and their minds do not go.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿لاَ فِيهَا غَوْلٌ﴾ — he said: He says: there is no headache in it; ﴿وَلاَ هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنْزَفَونَ﴾ — he said: their minds do not go.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: ﴿لاَ يُنْزَفُونَ﴾: their minds are not drained away. He said: and al-ghawl is disagreeable harm.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the most comprehensive and most fitting of them. One says "ghālathu ghawlun", i.e. something carried him off; and "the drink ghālahu and ightālahu", i.e. it carried off his mind or harmed him. From it is "so-and-so assassinated (ightāla) so-and-so", and from it "he killed him by treachery (qatl ghīla)" — the wāw changed into yāʾ because of the kasra before it. The root sense of "nuzifa" is "was diminished"; the meaning is: no diminution overtakes them, through drunkenness or anything else. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, denied drunkenness of them, because of the falsehood and foolishness it involves.
Its sum is diminution. And it is read ﴿وَلاَ هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنْزِفِونَ﴾, and there are two views on its meaning:
a- The better known of the two is that one says "anzafa the man" when his drink runs out, and the meaning is: his drink ran out.
b- The other view is that it is reported that one says "anzafa the man" when he becomes drunk. Abū ʿUbayda recited, from al-Ubayrid:
لَعْمِري لَئِنْ أَنْزَفْتُمُ أَوْ صَحَوْتُمُ * لَبِئْسَ النَّدَامَى كُنْتُمُ آلَ أَبْجَرَا
(By my life, whether you were drunk or sober, what wretched drinking companions you were, O family of Abjar!)
As for "nuzifa the man" when his mind goes from drunkenness, it is known and heard from the Arabs.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَعِندَهُمْ قَاصِرَاتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ عِينٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: they restrict their glances to their husbands.
Abū Yaḥyā related from Mujāhid, who said: [they restrict their glances to their husbands, and do not look at others].
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: they are not jealous over their husbands.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is the well-known one; its origin is from "qaṣartuhu", i.e. I confined it. [Translator's note: the source repeats «الأوَّلُ» twice.]
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿عِينٌ﴾ — Mujāhid said: that is, with beautiful eyes.
Al-Suddī said: ﴿عِينٌ﴾ — that is, with large eyes.
The lexicographers report that one says "a man aʿyan and a woman ʿaynāʾ", i.e. wide-eyed.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَّكْنُونٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, which hands have not touched; they resemble its whiteness.
By this Qatāda means: what is inside the shell.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says "kanantu the thing", i.e. I protected it. The Arabs liken a woman to the ostrich egg, as the poet said:
كَبِكْرِ المُقَانَاةِ البَيَاضِ بِصُفْرَةٍ * غَذَاهَا نَمِيرُ المَاءِ غَيْرَ مُحَلَّلِ
(Like the first egg [of the ostrich], whose whiteness is blended with yellow, nourished by pure water that has not been fouled.)

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ﴾.
He means the people of Paradise.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
﴿قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ إِنِّي كَانَ لِي قَرِينٌ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said: these are two men, brothers; one of them gave his wealth in charity, and his brother reproached him and said to him what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has narrated.
And it has been related from Ibn ʿAbbās: it is the idolater who had a believing companion; he said this to him.
Mujāhid said: ﴿قَرِينٌ﴾ — that is, a devil.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَقُولُ أَإِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُصَدِّقِينَ﴾.
The meaning: he says, "Are you indeed of those who affirm that we shall be requited?" Then "إِنَّ" was given kasra because of the coming of the lām.
Mujāhid said: ﴿مَدِينُونَ﴾ — that is, called to account.
﴿قَالَ هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُطَّلِعُونَ﴾ — that is, the one in Paradise said: will you look down? ﴿فَاطَّلَعَ فَرَآهُ﴾ — that is, he looked down and saw his companion ﴿فِي سَوَاء الجَحِيمِ﴾ — that is, in its midst.
The one in Paradise said: ﴿تَاللهِ إِنْ كِدْتَ لَتُرْدِينِ﴾ — that is, you were about to destroy me.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "لَتُغْوِينِ" (to lead me astray).

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ نِعْمَةُ رَبِّي لَكُنتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, of those brought into the Fire.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَفَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَيِّتِينَ. إِلاَّ مَوْتَتَنَا ٱلأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ؟ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ﴾.
Qatāda said: this is the end of his words. * Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لِمِثْلِ هَذَا فَلْيَعْمَلِ العَامِلُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُّزُلاً..؟﴾.
"Is that better as nuzul" — and nazl: that is, as provision. Al-nuzul also means yield and surplus.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَمْ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ. إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهَا فِتْنَةً لِّلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Abū Jahl said: we know zaqqūm only as dates with butter, so let us eat it greedily (natazaqqam).
Qatāda said: they were tried by this, and said: how can there be a tree in the Fire, when fire consumes trees? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ في أَصْلِ الجَحِيمِ﴾ — that is, its nourishment is from the Fire, and from it it was created.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿طَلْعُهَا كَأَنَّهُ رُءُوسُ ٱلشَّيَاطِينِ﴾.
﴿طَلْعُهَا﴾ — that is, its fruit, as it were the first of what emerges from it. Then He said: ﴿كَأَنَّهُ رُءُوسُ ٱلشَّيَاطِينِ﴾.
Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] said: it may be said: the devils have never been seen, so how can a comparison be made with them?
And is it permissible to say "Zayd is like so-and-so" when so-and-so is unknown?
The answer: what is intended is the meanings that are commonly recognised. When it is said "so-and-so is a devil", it is known that the meaning is "so-and-so is ugly and vile"; and from it is their saying "tashayṭana" when someone becomes vile. As the poet said:
أَيَقْتُلُنِي وَالمَشْرَفيُّ مُضَاجِعِي * وَمَسْنُونَةٌ زُرْقٌ كَأَنْيَابِ أَغْوَالِ
(Will he kill me, when the Mashrafī sword lies beside me, and sharpened blue[-gleaming arrowheads] like the fangs of ghouls?)
And the ghoul has never been seen, nor its fangs; but when the Arabs want to depict a female as ugly they liken her to the ghoul, and when they want to depict a male as ugly they liken him to the devil. This is a sound and clear answer.
And it has been said: it is a plant in Yemen of ugly appearance, to which it was likened, called al-astan and al-shayṭān; but that is not known among the Arabs.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and it has been said: the shayāṭīn are ugly kinds of snakes.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْهَا لَشَوْباً مِنْ حَمِيمٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, a mixture.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says "shubtu the thing with the thing", i.e. I mixed it with it.
And it has been said: what is meant here is the drinking of boiling water.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ أَلْفَوْاْ آبَآءَهُمْ ضَآلِّينَ. فَهُمْ عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿أَلْفَوْا﴾ is: they found.
Mujāhid said: ﴿يُهْرَعُونَ﴾ is like a fast trot; and Qatāda said: they hasten.
And it has been said: as though they are driven on in their haste.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ هُمُ ٱلْبَاقِينَ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda: all people are of the offspring of Noah, Allah bless him and grant him peace.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي ٱلآخِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that is, praise.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the meaning is: and We left for him among later generations [this:] it is said ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَى نُوحٍ فِي العَالَمِينَ﴾ — i.e. We left for him this phrase, remaining.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِ لإِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, on his way and his practice.
Qatāda said: on his religion.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: and among the party of Noah.
Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is: and among the party of Muḥammad, Allah bless him and grant him peace.
The first is more likely, because the mention of Noah has preceded.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِذْ جَآءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, sound, free of shirk (associating partners with Allah).
ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: he never cursed anything at all, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِذْ جَاءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَإِفْكاً آلِهَةً دُونَ ٱللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, a lie?

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَمَا ظَنُّكُم بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: that is, what do you think of the Lord of the worlds, when you have worshipped another than Him, when you meet Him?

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَنَظَرَ نَظْرَةً فِي ٱلنُّجُومِ﴾ [verse 88].
There are three views on its meaning:
Al-Ḥasan said: that is, he reflected on what he would do when they required him to go out.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning according to this view is: he looked into what had arisen (najama) for him of opinion, i.e. what had appeared to him. One says "najama the horn and the plant" when they emerge.
That is, he reflected and knew that every living being must fall ill, so he said: ﴿إِنِّى سَقِيمٌ﴾.
Al-Khalīl said: when a man reflects on a thing, how to manage it, it is said of him: he looked into the stars.
And Abū al-ʿAbbās said the same about the meaning of this verse.
The second view: the meaning is that he looked at the things that arise (najama), and knew that they have a Creator and Disposer, and that they change; and he knew that this would overtake him too, so he said: I am ill.
The third view: what Saʿīd related from Qatāda, that Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: he looked at a star and said "I am ill", using a stratagem on behalf of his religion.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning according to this view is: he did what they were familiar with — looking into the stars and taking them as indications.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿فَقَالَ إِنِّى سَقِيمٌ﴾ — that is, stricken with plague; and they used to flee from the plague. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَتَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ مُدْبِرينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:91-91.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰ آلِهَتِهِمْ فَقَالَ أَلاَ تَأْكُلُونَ﴾.
That is, he turned aside and veered; from it comes al-rawāgh (dodging). Then he said ﴿أَلاَ تَأْكُلُونَ﴾? in astonishment.
That is, he brought food near to them and said ﴿أَلاَ تَأْكُلُونَ﴾? And when he did not see them eating, he said: Will you not speak?
Abū Mālik said: he came to their gods, and they had placed food before them; when they did not speak to him, he said ﴿مَا لَكُمْ لاَ تَنْطِقُونَ﴾, then took an axe and struck their sides with it, then hung it on the neck of the biggest of them.

nahhas-meani:93-93.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَرَاغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْباً بِٱلْيَمِينِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of ﴿باليَمِينِ﴾ may be: with strength, as has preceded.
And He may intend the [right] hand.
And it has been said: by his oath, when he said ﴿وتَالله لأَكِيدَنَّ أصْنَامَكُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَأَقْبَلُوۤاْ إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, walking.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says "zaffa the ostrich, yaziffu" when it hastens, and that is at the beginning of its run.
And it is read ﴿يُزِفُّونَ﴾ with ḍamma on the yāʾ, and most lexicographers do not know it.
It may be that "azaffa" means "came upon [a state of] zafīf", in which case this is from it.
Al-Kisāʾī reported that it was read ﴿يَزِفُونَ﴾ with the fāʾ undoubled, and most lexicographers do not know this either.
And some reported that one says "wazafa, yazifu" when one hastens.

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayd said: that is, and what you make the idols from and carve — namely wood, stone and the like.
Qatāda said: and what you make with your hands.
It is possible that "ما" is negative, i.e. "and you do not make it, but Allah is its Creator".
It is possible that it is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun forming), i.e. "and your making".
And it is possible that it is interrogative, carrying the sense of rebuke.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَأَرَادُواْ بِهِ كَيْداً فَجَعَلْنَاهُمُ ٱلأَسْفَلِينَ﴾.
﴿ٱلأَسْفَلِينَ﴾: the most abased in argument.
Qatāda said: he did not debate them after that until He destroyed them.

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالَ إِنِّي ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ﴾.
He emigrated to the Holy Land.

nahhas-meani:102-102.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْيَ قَالَ يٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيۤ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ..؟﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْيَ﴾ — that is, work, i.e. he grew into a youth.
Others said: he reached thirteen years.
﴿قَالَ يٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيۤ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ؟﴾.
That is, I see in a dream that I am going to sacrifice you.
That is, I was commanded this in a dream, and it was made a sign: when I saw that, I was to sacrifice you.
And it is read ﴿مَاذَا تُرِي﴾? [explained by someone as] from patience. [Translator's note: the source is elliptical here; the person meant by «غيره» below is not named in the text.]
Abū Isḥāq said: no one other than him said this.
Rather, the scholars said the meaning is: what do you advise?
Ḥadīths have been related about the one to be sacrificed from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Some of the scholars said: the evidence that he was Ismāʿīl is that Ismāʿīl was in Mecca, and the sacrifice was at Minā.
But this does not follow: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: the sacrifice was in Syria (al-Shām).
And ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: it was in Syria — though Mujāhid said: it was at Minā.
And some said: in the Qurʾān there is what indicates that he was Ismāʿīl, Allah bless him and grant him peace. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَبَشَّرْنَاهَا بِإِسْحَاقَ، وَمِنْ وَرَاءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾; this indicates that Isḥāq would live until a child was born to him, so how could he be commanded to sacrifice him?
Abū Jaʿfar said: this too does not establish a proof, because it is possible that he be commanded to sacrifice him while knowing that a child would be born to him, since Allah, Majestic and Mighty, could bring him back to life after that.

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, they both submitted to the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty.
Abū Jaʿfar said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿فَلَمَّا سَلَّمَا﴾.
One says "sallama" when one gives one's hand [in submission] and is content.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ﴾ — that is, he laid him down; and there are two jabīns (sides of the forehead), with the forehead between them.
The jawāb (answer) of "لمَّا" according to the Basrans is omitted, as though He said: "he was happy".
And the wāw according to the Kufans is redundant (zāʾida), as though He said: "We called him".

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَفَدَيْنَاهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾.
Al-dhibḥ is what is sacrificed, and al-dhabḥ is the maṣdar (verbal noun).
Warqāʾ related from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid, who said: large, accepted.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ﴿عظيمٌ﴾ in the language is used for the large and for the noble.
And the people of tafsīr hold that here it is for the noble, i.e. the accepted.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَادَانَا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ ٱلْمُجِيبُونَ﴾.
It has been said: by his asking for the destruction of his people, when he said ﴿رَبِّ لا تَذَرْ عَلَى
الأَرْضِ مِنَ الكَافِرِينَ دَيَّارَاً﴾.
And it has been said: the meaning is that he prayed that We save him from drowning; ﴿وَنجَّيناه وأَهْلَهُ مِنَ
الكَرْبِ العَظِيمَ﴾ — that is, from drowning.

nahhas-meani:115-115.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ. وَنَجَّيْنَاهُمَا وَقَوْمَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلْكَرْبِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: from Pharaoh.

nahhas-meani:116-116.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَنَصَرْنَاهُمْ فَكَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ﴾.
He did not say "and We helped the two of them", because two is in origin a plural.
And it may be as when one reports about a single person with the verb of a group.
And it has been said: the meaning is: and We helped Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them both, and their people, against Pharaoh and his people. And this is the correct view, because before it is ﴿وَنَجَّيْنَاهُمَا وَقَوْمَهُمَا﴾.

nahhas-meani:117-117.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُمَا ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلْمُسْتَبِينَ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: the Torah.
He said: ﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُمَا الصِّرَاطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ﴾: Islam.

nahhas-meani:123-123.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾.
It has been said: Ilyās is Idrīs.
And it has been said: he is of the descendants of Aaron, Allah bless them both and grant them peace — and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.

nahhas-meani:125-125.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلاً وَتَذَرُونَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْخَالِقِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلاً﴾ — that is, a lord.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is an idol of theirs called Baʿl.
Ibn Zayd said: they were in Baalbek.
Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about this and remained silent. Then he heard a man calling out for a lost animal, and another said to him: "I am its baʿl", i.e. its owner. So Ibn ʿAbbās said to the questioner: this is like His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿أَتَدْعُونَ بَعْلاً﴾, i.e. a lord.
Ibn Isḥāq reported that ﴿بَعْلاً﴾ was a woman whom they worshipped.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says "this is the baʿl of the house", i.e. its owner.
So the meaning is: do you call upon a lord you have invented, and leave the best of creators?
The origin of this is that whatever is high and elevated is called baʿl; from it the husband is called baʿl al-marʾa, and from it what is watered by rain alone is called baʿl.

nahhas-meani:127-127.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, in the punishment.

nahhas-meani:130-130.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ إِلْ يَاسِينَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever reads ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَى إِلْيَاسِينَ﴾, there are two views about his reading:
One of them: that ﴿إلْيَاسِينَ﴾ and "إِلْيَاسَ" are one and the same, as one says Sīnāʾ and Sīnīn.
The second: it may be that He put him in the plural together with the people of his religion, as one says Mahāliba [for al-Muhallab and his family].

nahhas-meani:140-140.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ. إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ﴾.
That is, he fled.
Ṭāwūs said: when he boarded the ship it stood still, and they said: there is an ill-omened man on it. So they cast lots, and the lot fell on him three times; they threw him overboard and the whale swallowed him.

nahhas-meani:141-141.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُدْحَضِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُدْحَضِينَ﴾ — that is, of those who lost the lot.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the root sense of "adḥaḍtuhu" is "I made him slip".
Ibn ʿUyayna said: that is, of those defeated [in the lot].

nahhas-meani:142-142.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَٱلْتَقَمَهُ ٱلْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, a wrongdoer.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says "alāma the man" when he does something for which he is blamed.

nahhas-meani:144-144.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَبِّحِينَ. لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾.
Abū Razīn related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿مِنَ ٱلْمُسَبِّحِينَ﴾ — he said: of those who pray.
Mujāhid said: that is, in the belly of the whale.

nahhas-meani:145-145.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَنَبَذْنَاهُ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ﴾.
Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq said: al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿العَرَاءُ﴾ is the empty place; and from it is the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَنَبَذْنَاهُ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌ﴾.
He said: and Abū ʿUbayda said: al-ʿarāʾ is the face of the earth, and he recited for a man of Khuzāʿa:
رَفَّعْتُ رِجْلاً لا أَخَافُ عِثَارهَا * ونَبَذْتُ بالبَلَدِ العَرَاءِ ثِيَابِي
(I raised a foot whose stumbling I do not fear, and cast my garments down on the bare open land.)

nahhas-meani:146-146.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَأَنبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةً مِّن يَقْطِينٍ﴾.
ʿAmr ibn Maymūn related from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: it is the gourd.
Mujāhid said: it is every plant on the face of the earth that has no stem.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what Mujāhid said is what the Arabs know; it applies to the gourd, the colocynth, the melon and everything that is not on a stem. Its derivation seems to be from "qaṭana bi-l-makān", i.e. he stayed in the place. Sībawayh recited:
* "قَوَاطِناً مَكَّةَ مِنْ وُرْقِ الحَمِي" *
(Dwelling in Mecca, of the grey doves of the sanctuary.)
[Translator's note: the source spells the name «سيويه», a misprint for «سيبويه».]

nahhas-meani:147-147.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَىٰ مِئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: there are four views on the meaning of "أَوْ":
1- Abū ʿUbayda and al-Farrāʾ said: it is in the sense of "بَلْ" (rather).
This is an error according to most skilled grammarians; had it been as the two of them said, it would be "and We sent him to more than a hundred thousand", and "أَوْ" would be dispensed with.
2- Al-Qutabī [Ibn Qutayba] said: "أو" is in the sense of the wāw (and).
This too is an error, because it would nullify meanings.
3- And it has been said: "أو" is for permission (ibāḥa).
4- Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: "أَوْ" is in its proper function, and the meaning is: We sent him to a multitude such that, had you seen them, you would have said: a hundred thousand or more.
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: he was sent to a hundred and thirty thousand.
Abū Mālik said: he stayed in the belly of the whale forty days.
Ibn Ṭāwūs said: Allah caused a plant of gourd (yaqṭīn) to grow over him — it is "al-dubbāʾ" — and it used to shade him from the sun and he ate from it. When it fell, he wept over it, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed to him: Do you grieve over a plant, and not grieve over a hundred thousand or more? They repented, so I did not destroy them.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent termites against the plant, and they cut its roots, so he grieved over it — and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
Mujāhid said: the mission was before the whale swallowed him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafa narrated to us, saying: al-ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Nuʿmān Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us, saying: Abū Hilāl narrated to us, saying: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab narrated to us from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the mission of Jonah ﷺ was only after the whale cast him out. And he recited this verse ﴿وإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ until he reached His saying ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَىٰ مِئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾, and said: the mission was after that.

nahhas-meani:148-148.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَآمَنُواْ فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: until death.

nahhas-meani:149-149.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَٱسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَلِرَبِّكَ ٱلْبَنَاتُ وَلَهُمُ ٱلْبَنُونَ﴾.
That is, ask them a question of rebuke.
It is related from a group of the readers that they read ﴿اصّطَفَى البَنَاتِ
عَلَى البَنِينَ﴾ with the connecting alif (hamzat al-waṣl); Abū Ḥātim rejected this reading.
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is permissible, on the basis that it refers back to the saying [i.e. is part of what they say], and on the basis that rebuke may be expressed without the interrogative alif.

nahhas-meani:157-157.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَمْ لَكُمْ سُلْطَانٌ مُّبِينٌ. فَأْتُواْ بِكِتَابِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
Al-Suddī said: ﴿سُلْطَانٌ﴾ — that is, a proof. ﴿فَأْتُواْ بِكِتَابِكُمْ﴾ — he said: [bring] your proof that a book came to you with this.

nahhas-meani:158-158.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ نَسَباً﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿ٱلْجِنَّةِ﴾ here means the angels; i.e. they said: the angels are the daughters of Allah.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: they — meaning the unbelievers of Quraysh — said: the angels are the daughters of Allah. Abū Bakr said: then who are their mothers? They said: the secluded daughters of the jinn.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: they said Allah, Majestic and Mighty, married into the jinn, and they bore the angels.
Juwaybir related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ نَسَباً﴾: he said: they said: Iblīs is the brother of the All-Merciful, Majestic and Mighty. [Translator's note: the source spells the name «جوبير».]
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَتِ ٱلجِنَّةُ إِنَّهُمْ لَمُحْضَرُونَ﴾.
That is, the jinn know that those who said this will be brought to the punishment. So said al-Suddī, and it is correct; and likewise every "brought" (muḥḍarīn) in this sūra.
Mujāhid said: ﴿لَمُحْضَرُونَ﴾ — [brought to] the reckoning, meaning the jinn.

nahhas-meani:162-162.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ. مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفَاتِنِينَ﴾.
That is, you will not lead [anyone] astray by it.
﴿إلاَّ مَنْ هُوَ صَالِ الجَحِيمِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: that is, you will lead astray none but one whom it has gone before in My decree that he will go astray.
Al-Ḥasan, Ibrāhīm, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: this is the meaning of His saying ﴿مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفَاتِنِينَ﴾, i.e. you will not tempt anyone except one against whom I have decreed that.

nahhas-meani:164-164.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: Gabriel, or an angel, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: You stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it? The angels pray and glorify; there is no angel in heaven who is idle. [Translator's note: the source has «الملائكمة», a misprint for «الملائكة».]

nahhas-meani:166-166.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلصَّآفُّونَ. وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْمُسَبِّحُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: this is what the angels say.

nahhas-meani:168-168.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِن كَانُواْ لَيَقُولُونَ. لَوْ أَنَّ عِندَنَا ذِكْراً مِّنَ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
It is related that al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: this is what the idolaters of Mecca said. Then, when the remembrance of the former peoples and the knowledge of the later ones came to them, they disbelieved in it — so they will come to know.
Abū Isḥāq said: the unbelievers of Quraysh used to say: if a reminder came to us as it came to others among the former peoples, we would devote our worship purely to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then, when it came to them, they disbelieved in it; so they will come to know the outcome of their unbelief, and the punishment and vengeance that will befall them, in this world and the Hereafter.

nahhas-meani:171-171.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾.
That is, the word went forth from Us beforehand to Our messengers that they would be the ones helped; i.e. the decree and judgement have been settled by Us on this.
Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, happiness was preordained for them. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is ﴿وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا عَلَى عِبَادِنَا المُرْسَلَينَ﴾.
And it has been said: by "the word" He meant His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كتبَ اللهُ لأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا
وَرُسُلِي﴾.

nahhas-meani:177-177.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِذَا نَزَلَ بِسَاحَتِهِمْ فَسَآءَ صَبَاحُ ٱلْمُنْذَرِينَ﴾.
That is, the punishment descends on them. The meaning of ﴿بِسَاحَتِهِمْ﴾ is: on their abode; and al-sāḥa in the language is the wide courtyard of a house.
﴿فَسَآءَ صَبَاحُ ٱلْمُنْذَرِينَ﴾ — that is, wretched is the morning of those who were warned of the punishment. There is an implied element in it, i.e. "evil is the morning, their morning". And in the ḥadīth: "Allāhu akbar! Khaybar is ruined. When we descend on the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned."

nahhas-meani:180-182.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿سُبْحَانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ ٱلْعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ. وَسَلاَمٌ عَلَىٰ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ. وَٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [verses 180–182].
He, Glorified is He, declared Himself free of what the idolaters attributed to Him of a consort and a child.
﴿رَبِّ ٱلْعِزَّةِ﴾ is a badal (substitute). The accusative is also permissible, as praise (madḥ), and the nominative in the sense of "He is the Lord of might".
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the meaning of "Subḥān Allāh", and he said: "It is declaring Allah free of every evil."

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) the wāw of the oath, putting the noun in the genitive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم "I swear"; (صفّا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its governor being الصافّات; (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (زجرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, its governor being الزاجرات; (ذكرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its synonym [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) if الذكر is the Quran.]; (اللام) the lām of the oath, in compensation for the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).
The clause « (أقسم) بالصافّات..» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «إنّ إلهكم لواحد ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(الصافّات): plural of الصّافّة, the feminine of الصافّ, an active participle of the verb صفّ of the نصر class; its pattern is فاعل, its ʿayn and lām being of one letter. Its masculine plural is صافّون, صافّين.. and the feminine plural is صوافّ on the pattern فواعل [Note: See verse (36) of Sūrat al-Ḥajj.]. (الزاجرات): plural of الزاجرة, the feminine of الزاجر, an active participle of the three-letter verb زجر of the نصر class; its pattern is فاعل; its masculine plural is الزاجرون, الزاجرين.. and the feminine زواجر.
(زجرا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) known by hearsay (samāʿī) of the verb زجر; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(التاليات): plural of التالية, the feminine of التالي, an active participle of the three-letter verb تلا of the نصر class; its pattern is فاعل. It contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb): its original form is التالو with kasra on the lām; the wāw was changed into a yāʾ because the letter before it has kasra. Its masculine plural is التالون, التالين, and in both there is a weak-letter change by omission because of the meeting of two quiescent letters: the original form is التاليون, التاليين; the ḍamma and the kasra on the yāʾ were felt heavy, so they were transferred to the two letters before them, and when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ, the lām of the word, was omitted; its pattern is فاعون, فاعين.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) a badal (substitute) of واحد, nominative [Note: Or it is a second khabar (predicate) of the particle resembling the verb, or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هو, and the clause is resumptive.]; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a relative in the position of genitive, conjoined to السموات; (بينهما) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (الواو) conjunction; (ربّ) conjoined to the first ربّ, nominative like it.

safi-cedvel:6-10.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (بزينة) attached to (زيّنا); (الكواكب) a badal (substitute) of زينة — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it — genitive.
The clause «إنّا زيّنا..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «زيّنا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
(7) (حفظا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; (من كلّ) attached to the omitted verb..
The clause « (حفظناها) حفظا» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause زيّنا..
(8) (لا) negating; (إلى الملأ) attached to (يسّمّعون), by making it include the meaning of يصغون "they listen attentively"; (الواو) conjunction, and (الواو) in (يقذفون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (من كلّ) attached to (يقذفون).
The clause «لا يسّمّعون..» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: It is not valid for the clause to be a naʿt (adjective) of (كلّ شيطان), since it would then be described as not listening or not hearing, which is unsound; nor is it valid for it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), though al-ʿUkbarī permitted both.].
The clause «يقذفون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لا يسّمّعون.
(9) (دحورا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its synonym [Note: Or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl.]; (الواو) conjunction; (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) عذاب..
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لا يسّمّعون.
(10) (إلّا) for exception; (من) a relative in the position of nominative as a badal of the agent of يسّمّعون [Note: Or in the position of accusative as excepted.]; (الخطفة) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative; (الفاء) conjunction.
The clause «خطف» .. has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «أتبعه شهاب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خطف ...

* Morphology:
(7) مارد: an active participle of the three-letter verb مرد of the كرم class; its pattern is فاعل, and it means "insolent, rebellious".
(9) دحورا: maṣdar (verbal noun) of دحر of the فتح class; its pattern is فعول with two ḍammas.
(10) الخطفة: a maṣdar of once-ness (maṣdar marra) from the three-letter verb خطف of the فرح class; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.
(ثاقب): an active participle of the three-letter verb ثقب; its pattern is فاعل.

* Benefits:
His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِزِينَةٍ الْكَواكِبِ. وَحِفْظاً مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطانٍ مارِدٍ. لا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ الْأَعْلى. وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِنْ كُلِّ جانِبٍ — Ibn Hishām said, concerning the i'rab of the clause (لا يسّمعون): What first comes to mind is that it is an adjective (of لكل شيطان), or a ḥāl of it, and both are false, since there is no sense in guarding against a devil that does not hear. Rather it is for grammatical resumption (istiʾnāf naḥwī), and it cannot be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) because of the corruption of meaning. It has been said: it is possible that the original was «لئلا يسمعوا» "so that they would not hear", then the لام was omitted, as in your saying «جئتك أن تكرمني» "I came to you that you might honour me", then «أن» was omitted and the verb became nominative, as in the saying of Ṭarafa:
ألا أيّهذا الزاجري أحضر الوغى ... وأن أشهد اللذات هل أنت مخلدي
(O you who chide me for attending the battle and for witnessing pleasures — will you make me immortal?)
according to those who read أحضر in the nominative. But al-Zamakhsharī considered weak the combination of the two omissions (i.e. the omission of the لام and of أن). If you say: "I make it an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), i.e. 'and as a guard against every rebellious devil, its not hearing being anticipated', i.e. after the guarding", I say: the one who anticipates the existence of the meaning of the ḥāl is the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl), like the one passed by in your saying «مررت به معه صقر صائدا به غدا» "I passed by him with a falcon, hunting with it tomorrow", i.e. anticipating, at the time of being passed by, that he will hunt with it tomorrow; and the devils do not anticipate not hearing, nor do they want it.
After the Imam al-Nasafī cited the words of Ibn Hishām, he said:
In these words there is a forcedness from which the Quran must be protected. For each of the two particles (i.e. the لام and أن) is not rejected on its own, but their combination is objectionable. Then he mentioned the difference between our saying سمعت فلانا يتحدث "I heard so-and-so speaking" and سمعت إليه يتحدث "I listened to him speaking", or سمعت حديثه "I heard his speech" and سمعت إلى حديثه "I listened to his speech", and he said: the verb that is transitive by itself conveys perception, and the one that is transitive by إلى conveys listening attentively along with perception.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (خلقا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (أم) a conjunction; (من) a relative in the position of nominative, conjoined to the pronoun هم; (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (من طين) attached to (خلقناهم)..
The clause «استفتهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أهم أشدّ ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «خلقنا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «إنّا خلقناهم..» has no grammatical position: giving the reason.
The clause «خلقناهم..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(استفتهم): it contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) in keeping with its indeclinable (mabnī) form; its imperfect is يستفتي, and its pattern is استفعهم.
(لازب): an active participle of the three-letter verb لزب, meaning "sticking to the hand"; its pattern is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:12-17.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) before يسخرون..
The clause «عجبت..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يسخرون..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هم.. and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(13- 14) (الواو) conjunction in the six places, and (الواو) in (ذكّروا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (لا) negating..
The clause «ذكّروا ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «لا يذكرون..» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a condition that does not put the verb in the jussive.
The clause «رأوا ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يستسخرون» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(15) (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (سحر) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هذا.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «إن هذا إلّا سحر ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(16) (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation in both places; (ترابا) the khabar of كنّا, accusative; (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb and its ism; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
The clause «متنا ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كنّا ترابا» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause متنا.
The clause «إنّا لمبعوثون» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the implied apodosis [Note: This clause cannot validly be the apodosis of the condition, so that the adverb is not attached to the khabar of إنّ, since what comes after (إنّ) does not govern what comes before it; so the attachment is implied, i.e. أإذا متنا ... نبعث "When we have died ... shall we be raised?", and the clause mentioned is an explanation of this implied element.].
(17) (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation, and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (آباؤنا) is omitted, its implied form being مبعوثون ...
The clause «آباؤنا ... (مبعوثون)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّا لمبعوثون.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(نعم) a particle of response; (الواو) conjunction — or circumstantial (ḥāliyya). The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنتم داخرون ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the implied clause that is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), i.e. نعم تبعثون وأنتم داخرون "Yes, you will be raised, and you will be humbled" [Note: Or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of the implied تبعثون.].

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) giving the reason; (إنّما) a restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa); (هي) a pronoun referring to the notion of the resurrection, or the Hour, or the cry of the Hereafter evident in the context, and it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being زجرة; (الفاء) conjunction; (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya) ...
The clause «إنّما هي زجرة ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption giving the reason for an implied prohibition, i.e. لا تستصعبوا ذلك فإنّما هي ... "Do not deem that difficult, for it is only ...".
The clause «هم ينظرون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause هي زجرة.
The clause «ينظرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(زجرة): a maṣdar of once-ness (maṣdar marra) of the three-letter verb زجر of the نصر class; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (يا) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ويلنا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb that is not in use ...
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause هي زجرة [Note: In the preceding verse (19).].
The clause «يا ويلنا..» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) — or parenthetical. The clause «هذا يوم الدين....» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied saying, i.e. the angels said: هذا يوم الدين "This is the Day of Judgement" [Note: Or the object of their own saying after the parenthesis يا ويلنا.].
(21) (الذي) a relative in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of يوم الفصل; (به) attached to (تكذّبون)..
The clause «هذا يوم الفصل ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption [Note: Whether it is from the speech of the disbelievers to one another or from the speech of the angels.].
The clause «كنتم به تكذّبون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «تكذّبون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(الفصل): a maṣdar (verbal noun) known by hearsay (samāʿī) of the three-letter verb فصل of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:22-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (أزواجهم) conjoined to the relative noun, accusative [Note: Or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), accusative.. and Ibn Hishām denies that the wāw of accompaniment occurs in the Revelation at all.]; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to the relative الذين, and the referring pronoun is omitted.
The clause «احشروا ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied saying from the Creator, the Exalted, to the angels.
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «كانوا....» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يعبدون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا.
(23) (من دون) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied referring pronoun, i.e. يعبدونه من دون الله "they worship it besides Allah"; (الفاء) conjunction — or linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (إلى صراط) attached to (اهدوهم).
The clause «اهدوهم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause احشروا [Note: Or it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. إن تمّ حسابهم فاهدوهم "If their reckoning is complete, then lead them"..
And the clause of the condition and the apodosis is parenthetical between the two conjoined elements.].
The clause «قفوهم..» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause اهدوهم [Note: Or conjoined to the clause احشروا..].
The clause «إنّهم مسئولون» has no grammatical position: a resumption giving the reason.

* Morphology:
(قفوهم): it contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf); it is a weak verb of the mithāl type (first radical weak), whose fāʾ is dropped in the imperative because its ʿayn has kasra in the imperfect; its pattern is علوهم..

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (لكم) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (لا) negating; (تناصرون) an imperfect verb from which one of the two تاء's has been dropped.
The clause «ما لكم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied saying, i.e. that is said to them by way of rebuke.
The clause «لا تناصرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (اليوم) attached to the khabar (predicate) (مستسلمون).
The clause «هم اليوم مستسلمون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مستسلمون): plural of مستسلم, an active participle of the six-letter verb استسلم; its pattern is مستفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (على بعض) attached to (أقبل) ...
The clause «أقبل بعضهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يتساءلون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of أقبل.

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(عن اليمين) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent in (تأتوننا): swearing oaths..
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّكم كنتم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كنتم تأتوننا..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «تأتوننا ...» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(اليمين): a noun for an oath or for the well-known limb (the right hand); its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:29-32.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for nullifying digression (al-iḍrāb al-ibṭālī) ...
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لم تكونوا مؤمنين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) is implied, i.e. ما أضللناكم بل لم تكونوا مؤمنين ... "We did not lead you astray; rather you were not believers ...".
(30) (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negating; (لنا) attached to the khabar (predicate) of كان; (عليكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of سلطان; (بل) like the first ...
The clause «ما كان لنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لم تكونوا [Note: Or in the position of accusative, conjoined to the implied clause that is the object of the saying.].
The clause «كنتم قوما ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the saying.
(31- 32) (الفاء) conjunction carrying the meaning of cause; (علينا) attached to (حقّ); (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (اللام) for emphasis.
The clause «حقّ علينا قول ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّا لذائقون» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying [Note: In the verse there is a shift (iltifāt) from address to the first person, the original being: إنكم لذائقون "you will surely taste".. Or it is from the speech of those who led astray, giving the reason for what preceded, so it has no grammatical position.].
The clause «أغويناكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason.
The clause «كنّا غاوين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(طاغين): plural of طاغ, an active participle of the three-letter verb طغى; its pattern is فاع. It contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf), because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ) whose lām — the yāʾ — was omitted because it met, being quiescent, with the sukūn of the tanwīn; and likewise طاغين, on the pattern فاعين.

* Benefits:
- Giving the hamza of إن fatḥa or kasra:
1- Giving the hamza of إن fatḥa or kasra:
1- The hamza of (إن) takes fatḥa if it can validly be interpreted, together with its ism and khabar, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as in His saying, the Exalted, قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ, the implied sense being: "the listening of a group of jinn"; and our saying يعجبني أنك مخلص "It pleases me that you are sincere", the implied sense being: "your sincerity".
2- But if it cannot validly be interpreted, together with its ism and khabar, as a maṣdar, then it takes kasra, and the places where it takes kasra are in the following cases:
1- At the beginning of speech: as in His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّا أَعْطَيْناكَ الْكَوْثَرَ; or at the beginning of a resumed clause, as in His saying, the Exalted, فَلا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ ما يُسِرُّونَ وَما يُعْلِنُونَ. 2- After the verb of saying: as in the verse we are dealing with, which is His saying, the Exalted, قالُوا: إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ الْيَمِينِ, and His saying, the Exalted, قالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ.
3- After an oath: as in His saying, the Exalted, وَالْعَصْرِ إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ, يس وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ. 4- If it occurs at the head of the ṣila (relative clause), as in His saying, the Exalted, ما إِنَّ مَفاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوأُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ أُولِي الْقُوَّةِ, and our saying (هذا الذي إنه محسن للمساكين) "This is the one who is kind to the poor".
5- If the لام is joined to its khabar, it takes kasra after it had the right to fatḥa, e.g.:
(علمت أنك صادق) "I knew that you were truthful" becomes (علمت إنك لصادق).

safi-cedvel:33-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative, attached to the khabar (predicate) (مشتركون); (في العذاب) attached to (مشتركون).
The clause «إنّهم ... مشتركون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(34) - (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is نفعل; (بالمجرمين) attached to (نفعل).
The clause «إنّا ... نفعل» has no grammatical position: parenthetical — or giving the reason. (35) - (لهم) attached to (قيل); (إلّا) a particle of exception; (الله) the Name of Majesty, a badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun in the implied khabar.
The clause «إنّهم كانوا.. يستكبرون» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for what preceded.
The clause «كانوا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «قيل لهم ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «لا إله إلّا الله ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied saying, i.e. قولوا لا إله.. "Say: there is no god..", and the implied clause of saying is in the position of nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: Because it is the object of the saying in the active verb..].
The clause «يستكبرون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا [Note: This is if the adverb (إذا) is devoid of conditional meaning, and what lies between the verb and its khabar is parenthetical ...
If the adverb is made to include the meaning of a condition, then the clause يستكبرون is its apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the condition, its protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of كانوا.].
(36) - (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation; (إنّا) like the first; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (لشاعر) attached to (تاركو).
The clause «يقولون ...» is conjoined to the clause يستكبرون.
The clause «أإنا لتاركو» .. is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(مشتركون): plural of مشترك, an active participle of the five-letter verb اشترك; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for nullifying digression (al-iḍrāb al-ibṭālī); (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of جاء ...
The clause «جاء ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: It is in reality a resumption within the scope of an implied saying, i.e. He, the Exalted, said: «ليس بشاعر بل جاء بالحقّ» "He is not a poet; rather he has brought the truth".].
The clause «صدّق ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:38-40.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
The clause «إنّكم لذائقو ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: And it is within the scope of the implied saying preceding in verse (37).].
(39) - (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negating, and (الواو) in (تجزون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the referring pronoun being omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ...) is in the position of accusative as the direct object, its governor being تجزون [Note: Or in the position of [Translator's note: the source has «في محل حرف جرّ» "in the position of a preposition"; «في محل جرّ» "in the position of genitive" is evidently intended.] genitive by an omitted preposition, namely the باء, attached to (تجزون).].
The clause «ما تجزون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كنتم تعملون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كنتم.
(40) (إلّا) a particle of exception; (عباد) accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) from the agent pronoun in (تعملون) ...

* Rhetoric:
Shift of person (iltifāt): in His saying, the Exalted, «إِنَّكُمْ لَذائِقُوا الْعَذابِ الْأَلِيمِ».
He shifted from the third person to direct address, to show the fullness of anger against them, by confronting them face to face with this threat, and by paying no heed to them. And that is what befits the arrogant.

safi-cedvel:41-49.t:
* I'rab:
(لهم) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) رزق..
The clause «أولئك لهم رزق ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لهم رزق ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
(42- 44) - (فواكه) a badal (substitute) of رزق, nominative [Note: Or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, and the clause is an adjective.]; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (في جنّات) attached to (مكرمون) [Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (مكرمون); it may also be a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.]; (على سرر) attached to (مكرمون) [Note: Or attached to متقابلين.]; (متقابلين) a ḥāl, accusative, of the pronoun in (مكرمون) ...
The clause «هم مكرمون..» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in (لهم) [Note: It may be in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لهم رزق.].
(45) (عليهم) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb يطاف; (بكأس) attached to (يطاف); (من معين) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of كأس.
The clause «يطاف عليهم ...» is in the position of nominative as another khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك) [Note: It may be resumptive, so it has no grammatical position.].
(46- 47) (بيضاء) a second naʿt of كأس, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, a diptote; (لذّة) a third naʿt, genitive; (للشاربين) attached to لذّة; (لا) negating; (فيها) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ غول; (الواو) conjunction; the second (لا) is redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation, and the redundancy is obligatory; (عنها) attached to (ينزفون), and (عن) is causal ...
The clause «لا فيها غول ...» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of كأس..
The clause «هم عنها ينزفون ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause لا فيها غول.
The clause «ينزفون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(48- 49) (الواو) conjunction; (عندهم) an adverb, accusative, attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ قاصرات; (عين) a naʿt of قاصرات, nominative.
The clause «عند هم قاصرات ...» is conjoined to the clause يطاف عليهم.
The clause «كأنهنّ بيض ...» is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of قاصرات.

* Morphology:
(45) كأس: a noun for the vessel one drinks from, and it is feminine; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; the plural is كؤوس — with ḍamma on the kāf — and أكؤس — with fatḥa on the first hamza — and كاسات, and كئاس with kasra on the kāf.
(46) (لذّة): feminine of لذّ, on the pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the past verb لذّ of the فتح class.. or it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the aforementioned verb; and if it is the maṣdar it mostly keeps the masculine. لذّة is a noun meaning the opposite of pain, and the plural is لذّات.
(47) غول: a maṣdar known by hearsay (samāʿī) of the three-letter verb غاله يغوله meaning "destroyed him", or غالته الخمر, i.e. the wine took away his mind or the health of his body; and it may be a noun meaning headache, drunkenness or hardship ... Its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(ينزفون): a verb always used in the passive form while having an active meaning, meaning "his mind went" or "he became drunk", in the same way as يهرع, يغمى عليه, يجنّ ... etc.; its past is نزف with ḍamma then kasra.
(48) قاصرات: plural of قاصرة, the feminine of قاصر, an active participle of the three-letter verb قصر of the نصر class: قصر عن الشيء when one refrains from it, i.e. restraining their glances from other than their husbands ... or قصر على الشيء, i.e. one did not aspire to anything else and did not go beyond it to another.
(عين): plural of عيناء, a resembling adjective from عين يعين of the فرح class, i.e. the black of whose eye is large and wide; its pattern is فعلاء; and the pattern of عين is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn, its fāʾ having been given kasra to suit the yāʾ, for lightness; the masculine is أعين on the pattern أفعل.
(49) بيض: a generic noun (ism jins) for what females of animals and others produce (eggs); the singular is بيضة, on the pattern فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn, and the pattern of بيض is فعل with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(مكنون): a passive participle of the three-letter verb (كنّ); its pattern is مفعول.
