The loose simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in His saying, the Exalted, «كَأَنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَكْنُونٌ».
What is meant is likening them to eggs sheltered by feathers in the nest, which hands have not touched and dust has not reached, with a slight yellowness together with a lustre as in pearls. Most hold that it is specifically ostrich eggs in their nests in the sand, because they are finer in appearance than all other eggs, and further from the touch of hands and from anything reaching them that would change their colour. The Arabs liken women to eggs, and they call them "eggs of the curtained chambers"; from this is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وبيضة خدر لا يرام خباؤها ... تمتعت من لهو بها غير معجل
(Many an egg of the curtained chamber, whose tent none dared approach, have I enjoyed sporting with, unhurried.)

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (أقبل ... يتساءلون) the i'rab of this verse has passed [Note: See verse (27) of this sūra, words and clauses.].

safi-cedvel:51-53.t:
* I'rab:
(منهم) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of قائل; (لي) attached to the khabar (predicate) of كان..
The clause «قال قائل ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «إنّي كان لي قرين» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كان لي قرين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(52) The fāʿil (agent) of (يقول) is a pronoun referring to القرين; (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (من المصدّقين) attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يقول ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of قرين.
The clause «أإنّك لمن المصدّقين» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
(53) (أإذا متنا.. لمدينون) the i'rab of its counterpart has passed [Note: See verse (16) of this sūra, words and clauses.]..

safi-cedvel:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
The fāʿil (agent) of (قال) is a pronoun referring to the aforementioned speaker; (هل) a particle of interrogation.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنتم مطّلعون» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(مطّلعون): plural of مطّلع, an active participle of the five-letter verb اطّلع; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.. The word contains a substitution (ibdāl): its original form is مطتلع, taken from اطتلع.. the تاء came after the طاء, was changed into a طاء and assimilated into the first طاء..

safi-cedvel:55-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction in both places; (في سواء) attached to (رآه).
The clause «اطّلع ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال [Note: In the preceding verse (54).].
The clause «رآه....» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اطّلع.

safi-cedvel:56-59.t:
* I'rab:
(التاء) the tāʾ of the oath, putting the noun in the genitive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, genitive by (التاء), attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم "I swear"; (إن) lightened from the heavy (inna), necessarily inoperative (muhmala); (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), redundant (zāʾida); and (النون) in (تردين) is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and (الياء), omitted for lightness, is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the oath and its answer ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كدت لتردين» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.
The clause «تردين..» is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كدت.
(57) (الواو) conjunction; (لولا) a conditional particle that does not put the verb in the jussive; (نعمة) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and the khabar is obligatorily omitted; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لولا; (من المحضرين) attached to the khabar of كنت..
The clause «لولا نعمة ربّي ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer to the oath.
The clause «كنت من المحضرين» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(58) (الهمزة) for interrogation; (الفاء) conjunction; (ما) negating, operating like ليس; (ميّتين) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ما.
The clause «ما نحن بميّتين ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object of an implied saying, i.e. the people of Paradise said: «أنحن مخلّدون فما نحن بميّتين ...» "Are we immortal, so that we shall not die ...?"
(59) (إلّا) a particle of exception; (موتتنا) accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) [Note: It is said that (إلّا) is for restriction (ḥaṣr) and (موتتنا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is the resembling adjective (ميّتين).]; (الواو) conjunction; (ما نحن بمعذّبين) like ما نحن بميّتين.
The clause «ما نحن بمعذّبين ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause ما نحن بميّتين.

* Morphology:
(كدت): it contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf), because it is a hollow verb (ajwaf) to which a nominative pronoun is attached: when it was made indeclinable on the sukūn and two quiescent letters met, the alif and the dāl, the alif was omitted. Its pattern is فلت with kasra on the fāʾ; its class is فرح, the vowel of the omitted ʿayn having been transferred to the fāʾ; its original form is كود يكود, like خوف يخوف.
(موتتنا): a maṣdar of once-ness (maṣdar marra) from مات, on the pattern فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:60-61.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (لمثل) attached to (يعمل); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (اللام) the lām of command, and the verb (يعمل) was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters..
The clause «إنّ هذا لهو الفوز ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو الفوز ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «ليعمل العاملون ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. من أراد الفوز في الآخرة فليعمل له مثل ذلك في الدنيا "Whoever wants success in the Hereafter, let him work for it likewise in this world".

safi-cedvel:62-68.t:
* I'rab:
(نزلا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (أم) a conjunction counterbalancing the hamza of interrogation; (شجرة) conjoined to the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ذلك).
The clause «ذلك خير ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(63) - (للظالمين) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of فتنة — or to فتنة. The clause «إنّا جعلناها ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «جعلناها ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
(64- 65) - (في أصل) attached to (تخرج), by making it include the meaning of تنبت "it grows".
The clause «إنّها شجرة ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption.
The clause «تخرج ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of شجرة.
The clause «طلعها كأنّه رؤوس ...» is in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of شجرة.
The clause «كأنّه رؤوس ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ طلعها.
(66) (الفاء) resumptive; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis; (منها) attached to (آكلون), and the second is attached to (مالئون), which is conjoined to (آكلون) by (الفاء); (البطون) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle مالئون.
The clause «إنّهم لآكلون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(67) (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar; (عليها) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of حميم [Note: An adjective placed before what it qualifies, i.e. إنّ لهم لشوبا من حميم مصبوب على ما يأكلون من شجرة الزقّوم "they will have a mixture of scalding water poured over what they eat of the tree of Zaqqūm".]; (اللام) for emphasis; (شوبا) the ism of إنّ, accusative; (من حميم) attached to a naʿt of (شوبا)..
The clause «إن لهم.. لشوبا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّهم لآكلون.
(68) - (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis; (إلى الجحيم) attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّ مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّ لهم.. لشوبا.

* Morphology:
(62) الزقّوم: a noun for the fruit of a vile, bitter tree of loathsome taste; it is said to be a tree found in the land of Tihāma, among the vilest of trees; its pattern is فعّول with fatḥa, and ḍamma on the doubled ʿayn.
(64) أصل: a noun for the lowest part of a thing, or what is opposite to the branch, or it is the maṣdar (verbal noun); its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.. from the three-letter verb of the كرم class.
(66) مالئون: plural of مالئ, an active participle of the three-letter verb ملأ; its pattern is فاعل.
(67) شوبا: a maṣdar known by hearsay (samāʿī) of the verb شابه يشوبه, i.e. mixed with it; it may be intended as the passive participle, i.e. المشوب "mixed"; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metaphor (istiʿāra): in His saying, the Exalted, «طَلْعُها».
Al-ṭalʿ belongs to the date-palm, and it was borrowed for what emerges from the tree of Zaqqūm of its yield: either a verbal metaphor or a conceptual one.
2- The imaginative simile (al-tashbīh al-takhyīlī): in His saying, the Exalted, «طَلْعُها كَأَنَّهُ رُؤُسُ الشَّياطِينِ».
It is likened to the heads of devils as an indication of its utmost loathsomeness and ugliness of appearance, because the devil is loathed and considered ugly in people's natures, as they believe him to be pure evil unmixed with any good; so they say of one with an ugly form: "as if it were the face of a devil, as if it were the head of a devil". And when painters depict him, they bring his image in the ugliest and most terrifying form imaginable; just as they believed the angel to be pure good with no evil in it, so they likened a beautiful form to it. Allah the Exalted said: «ما هذا بَشَراً إِنْ هذا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ».
3- The secret of conjoining with «ثم»: in His saying, the Exalted, «ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْها لَشَوْباً مِنْ حَمِيمٍ» there is a secret, subtle in derivation and fine in its path, for in the meaning of delay (tarākhī) there are two aspects. The first: that they fill their bellies from the tree of Zaqqūm, which is hot, burning their bellies and making them thirsty, and they are not given drink until after a long while, as a torment by that thirst; then they are given to drink what is hotter, namely the drink mixed with scalding water. The second: that He mentioned the food with that loathsomeness and repulsiveness, then mentioned the drink with what is more loathsome and repulsive, so He brought ثم to indicate the remoteness of the state of the drink from the state of the food, and the difference of its description from that of the food in exceeding it.

safi-cedvel:69-70.t:
* I'rab:
(ألفوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (ضالّين) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «إنّهم ألفوا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption giving the reason.
The clause «ألفوا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
(70) - (الفاء) conjunction; (على آثارهم) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هم..
And (الواو) in (يهرعون) is the fāʿil [Note: It should be noted that this verb is used in the language only in the passive form, so the pronoun in it must be an agent, not a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil).].
The clause «هم على آثارهم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّهم ألفوا.
The clause «يهرعون..» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of "being settled" (istiqrār).].

* Morphology:
(ألفوا): it contains a weak-letter change by omission (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, the lām of the word and the (واو) of the plural; the letter before the wāw was given fatḥa as an indication of the omitted alif; its pattern is أفعوا — with fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:71-74.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قبلهم) an adverb, accusative, attached [Translator's note: the source reads «متعلّق لا متعلّق ب (ضلّ)», which appears garbled; the sense is "attached to (ضلّ)".] to (ضلّ) [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of أكثر.] ...
The clause «ضلّ ... أكثر» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath ...
The implied oath clause has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(72) (فيهم) attached to (أرسلنا), by making it include the meaning of بعثنا "We sent forth"..
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first implied oath clause.
(73) - (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (كيف) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كان..
The clause «انظر ...» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: إن عاقبنا المنذرين. فانظر ... "If We punished those who were warned, then look ...".
The clause «كان عاقبة ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. (74) - (إلّا) for exception; (عباد) accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) ...

safi-cedvel:75-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (الفاء) conjunction; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for the preceding implied oath; (نعم) a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; (المجيبون) fāʿil (agent), nominative ... and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, its implied form being نحن "We".
The clause «نادانا نوح ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath.
The clause «نعم المجيبون..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer to the oath [Note: Or the answer to another implied oath.].
(76) - (الواو) conjunction in the following four places; (أهله) conjoined to the third-person pronoun in (نجّيناه); (من الكرب) attached to (نجّيناه)..
The clause «نجّيناه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause that is the answer to the oath.
(77) - (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); (الباقين) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being جعلنا.
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجّيناه.
(78) - (عليه) attached to an omitted element which is the object of تركنا, i.e. تركنا ثناء عليه "We left praise of him"..
(في الآخرين) attached to (تركنا).
The clause «تركنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجّيناه.
(79) - (سلام) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative [Note: Beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible because it indicates a supplication.]; (على نوح) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ سلام; (في العالمين) attached to the "being settled" (istiqrār), which is the khabar.
The clause «سلام على نوح» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication [Note: Or it is an explanation of His saying تركنا ... or an explanation of the implied object, i.e. "We left something, which is these words" ... It may also be the object of an implied saying, i.e. قلنا سلام ... "We said: Peace ...".].
(80) - (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) and its ism; (كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is نجزي ...
The clause «إنّا ... نجزي ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for what preceded.
The clause «نجزي ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(81) - (من عبادنا) attached to an omitted khabar of إنّ..
The clause «إنّه من عبادنا ...» has no grammatical position: another reason.
(82) - (ثمّ) a conjunction ...
The clause «أغرقنا....» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجّيناه — or جعلنا.

* Morphology:
(75) المجيبون: plural of المجيب, an active participle of the four-letter verb أجاب; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. It contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb): its original form is مجوب — with kasra on the wāw, for it has wāw as its ʿayn — then the wāw was given sukūn and its vowel was transferred to the jīm, then the wāw was changed into a yāʾ because the letter before it has kasra, so it became (مجيب) [Note: And see verse (61) of Sūrat Hūd.].

safi-cedvel:83-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من شيعته) attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (اللام) for emphasis; (إبراهيم) the ism of إنّ, accusative.
The clause «إنّ من شيعته لإبراهيم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(84) (إذ) an adverb of past time, attached to an omitted element indicated by the word شيعته, i.e. شايعه إذ جاء ربّه "he followed him when he came to his Lord"; (بقلب) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent.
The clause «جاء ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
(85) - (إذ) an adverb, a badal (substitute) of the first; (لأبيه) attached to (قال); (ماذا) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being تعبدون [Note: Or (ما) is an interrogative, mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar being the relative noun (ذا), and the clause of the mubtadaʾ and khabar is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause تعبدون is a ṣila (relative clause), the referring pronoun being omitted.].
The clause «قال ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تعبدون..» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
(86) (الهمزة) for rebuking interrogation; (إفكا) a fronted direct object, accusative [Note: It is said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) whose governor is تريدون, and the direct object is آلهة.]; (آلهة) a badal of (إفكا) with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. عبادة آلهة "the worship of gods"; (دون) an adverb, accusative, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of آلهة [Note: Or attached to (تريدون).].
The clause «تريدون» is in the position of accusative as a badal of the clause تعبدون.

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {أُوْلَئِكَ} up to the end is an explanation of their condition.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {فَوَاكِهُ}: it may be a badal (substitute) for «رزق», and it may be the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "that provision is fruits."

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {على سُرُرٍ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ, while Abū al-Sammāl read it with fatḥa on it. This is the dialect of some of Kalb and Tamīm: they put fatḥa on the ʿayn of the pattern fuʿul when it is a doubled noun. As for an adjective such as «ذُلُل», there is disagreement about it; the sound view is that this is not permissible, because the attested usage occurred with inanimate nouns, not with adjectives.

His saying: «في جنات»: it may be attached (yataʿallaq) to «مُكْرَمون», it may be a second khabar, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial); likewise «على سُرُرٍ». And «متقابلين» is a ḥāl. It is also possible that «على سرر» is attached to «متقابلين», and «يُطافُ» is an adjective of «مُكْرَمُون», or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «متقابلين», or from the pronoun in one of the two prepositional phrases if we make it a ḥāl.

The kaʾs (cup) is made of glass so long as there is wine or nabīdh (date/raisin drink) in it; otherwise it is a qadaḥ (drinking vessel). The kaʾs may also be applied to the wine itself, which is a permissible figurative usage. It was recited:
3792 - Many a cup I drank for pleasure, and another with which I treated myself with it (i.e. with wine)
And «من مَعين» is an adjective of «كأس»; the discussion of «معين» has already preceded.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {بَيْضَآءَ}: an adjective of «كَأْس». The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "an adjective of kaʾs or of the wine." I say: the wine has not been mentioned, unless he means by «المَعين» the wine, which is very far-fetched.

ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] read «صفراءَ» (yellow), which contradicts the black [i.e. the opposite of white], except that describing it with this colour has been attested. A verse by one of the muwallad (post-classical) poets was recited:
3793 - Yellow; griefs never descend in her courtyard; if a stone touched her, a joy would touch it

And «لَذَّةٍ» is also an adjective. It is described by a maṣdar (verbal noun) for emphasis, or on the omission of the muḍāf, that is: "possessing delight"; or on the feminine form of laddh in the sense of ladhīdh (delightful), so that it is a description on the pattern faʿl, like ṣaʿb. One says: ladha l-shayʾu yaladhdhu ladhdhan, so it is ladhīdh and laddh. He recited:
3794 - With her delightful talk, which, were she to speak with it to the lions of the wilderness, they would come hurrying
And another said:
3795 - And a delight like the taste of the Ṣarkhadī wine, which I left in the land of enemies for fear of the misfortunes of fate

Al-ladhīdh is everything that is found pleasant. It was recited: 3796 - It delights by its taste, and you imagine in it, when you rouse her after sleep ...

And «للشاربين» is an adjective of «لَذَّةٍ».

semin-durr:47-47.t:
And {لاَ فِيهَا غَوْلٌ}: also an adjective. The operation of «لا» is void, and it is repeated because its khabar is fronted. The benefit of fronting a khabar like this, and the Shaykh's [Abū Ḥayyān's] rejection of it and the discussion with him, have already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara; so turn to it.

His saying: «يُنْزَفُون»: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «يُنْزِفون» here and in al-Wāqiʿa, with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the zāy. ʿĀṣim agreed with them only in what is in al-Wāqiʿa. The rest read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the zāy. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with fatḥa and kasra [yanzifūna]. Ṭalḥa read it with fatḥa and ḍamma [yanzufūna]. The first reading is from anzafa l-rajulu, when his reason goes from drunkenness, so he is nazīf and manzūf. Its analogical form would have been munzaf, like mukram. And nazafa l-rajulu l-khamrata, then he anzafa: the triliteral is transitive, and the quadriliteral with hamza is intransitive, like: kababtuhu so he akabba, and qashaʿat al-rīḥu l-saḥāba so it aqshaʿa, that is: they entered into the kabb and the qashʿ. Al-Aswad said:
3797 - By my life, if you have become drunk or sobered up, how wretched drinking companions you are, O house of Abjar
It is also said: anzafa, meaning his drink ran out. As for the second reading, it is from nuzifa l-rajulu, triliteral, in the passive, meaning: he became drunk and his reason went as well. It is also possible that this reading is from unzifa, in the sense given above. It was also said: it is from their saying: nazaftu l-rakiyya, that is: I drained its water. The meaning is: their wines do not run out but remain forever. And «يُنْزَفُوْن» is made to include the meaning of "they are turned away from it because of drunkenness." As for the last two readings, one says nazifa l-rajul and nazufa, with kasra and ḍamma, meaning: his reason went through drunkenness.

Al-ghawl: everything that destroys you (ightālaka), that is, ruins you. From it comes also al-ghūl with ḍamma: something the Arabs imagined, about which they have poems, like the ʿanqāʾ. One says: ghālanī kadhā ("such-and-such destroyed me"). From it also comes al-ghīla in killing and in suckling. He said:
3798 - Our predecessors passed on, all of them enjoying their lives, and a ghūl destroyed me in Mecca
And another said:
Wine never ceased to destroy us, and to carry off the first and then the first [of us]
So al-ghawl is a general noun for all harm.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
And {قَاصِرَاتُ الطرف}: it may be of the category of the ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective), that is: "those whose glances are restrained," like munṭaliq al-lisān; and it may be of the category of the active participle in its original sense. On the first, the muḍāf ilayhi is nominative in position; on the second, it is accusative, that is: "their glances are confined to their husbands," and this is great praise. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
3800 - Among those with restrained glances: were a tiny ant creeping over her garment's hem, it would leave a mark

Al-ʿīn: plural of ʿaynāʾ, the wide-eyed woman. The male is aʿyan. Al-bayḍ is the plural of bayḍa (egg), which is well known. What is meant by it here is the ostrich egg. Al-maknūn means "protected," from kanantuhu, that is: I put it in a kinn (shelter). The Arabs compare a woman to it in its colour, which is a white mixed with some yellow. The Arabs love it. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
3801 - And many an egg of a curtained chamber whose tent is not approached, I enjoyed pleasure with her unhurriedly
Like the first egg of the ostrich, white tinged with yellow, nourished by clear water not muddied

And Dhū al-Rumma said:
3802 - White in her excess, yellow in her coquetry, as if she were silver touched by gold

Some of them said: the woman is compared to it only in respect of her parts, for the egg, from whatever side you come to it, appears to the eye similar to the other, and this is the utmost praise. Some poets noticed this when he said:
3803 - Her limbs are proportionate, so you see no difference among them, but they come in due measure

Al-bayḍ is pluralised as buyūḍ. He said:
3804 - In a barren wasteland, the mounts being as if they were sandgrouse of al-Ḥazn whose eggs had become chicks

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {يَتَسَآءَلُونَ}: a ḥāl from the agent of «أَقْبَلَ», and «أقبل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يُطاف», that is: "they drink and converse." The same is the state of drinking, where they sit, as he said:
3805 - Nothing remains of the pleasures except conversation of the noble over the wine
He used «فأقْبَلَ» in the past tense because its occurrence is certain, like His saying: {ونادى أَصْحَابُ الجنة} [al-Aʿrāf: 44] {ونادى أَصْحَابُ النار} [al-Aʿrāf: 50].

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {لَمِنَ المصدقين}: the majority read the ṣād without tashdīd, from taṣdīq (affirmation), that is: "of those who affirm the meeting with Allah." It was also read with tashdīd, from ṣadaqa (almsgiving).

semin-durr:54-54.t:
The majority read «مُطَّلِعُوْنَ» with a doubled ṭāʾ with fatḥa and fatḥa on the nūn, and «فاطَّلَع» as an active past verb, of the pattern iftaʿala from ṭulūʿ (rising/appearing).

Ibn ʿAbbās, among others, read it (and it is also reported from Abū ʿAmr) with sukūn on the ṭāʾ and fatḥa on the nūn: «فأُطْلِعَ», with a hamzat qaṭʿ with ḍamma and kasra on the lām, as a passive past verb. On this reading «مُطْلِعُوْنَ» may be intransitive, that is: "approaching," from your saying: aṭlaʿa ʿalaynā fulān, that is: he approached; or it may be transitive, its object omitted, that is: "your companions."

Abū al-Burhasam and ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār read «مُطْلِعُوْنِ» with the ṭāʾ lightened and the nūn with kasra, and «فَأُطْلِعَ» in the passive. People, Abū Ḥātim and others, rejected this reading because of the combination of the nūn with the speaker's pronoun, since its analogical form would be muṭliʿiyya, the original being muṭliʿūya, in which [the wāw] was replaced and assimilated, as in: jāʾa muslimiyya l-ʿāqilūna, and the saying of him, peace be upon him, «أوَ مُخْرِجِيَّ هم». Ibn Jinnī gave it a directive by saying that the active participle was treated in it like the imperfect verb, meaning in retaining the nūn with the pronoun. Al-Ṭabarī recited as proof of this: 3806 - I do not know, though my opinion is every opinion: will Shurāḥ hand me over to my people?
Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to it, saying: "Or he likened the active participle in that to the imperfect because of their kinship, as if he had said: 'yuṭliʿūnī'. But it is weak and occurs only in poetry." He gave another directive for it, saying: "He meant muṭliʿūna iyyāya, so he put the attached [pronoun] in the place of the detached, as in his saying:
3807 - They are the doers of good and those who command it ... [verse incomplete in the source]

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected it: this is not one of the places for the detached pronoun so that he could claim that the attached one stood in its place. It is not permissible to say "Hind Zayd is one who strikes iyyāhā," nor "Zayd is one who strikes iyyāya." I say: what he mentioned is not permissible only because, when the attached pronoun can be used, one does not turn to the detached. Someone might say: we do not concede that the attached can be used when the nūn and the tanwīn are present before the pronoun; rather the place becomes the place of the detached pronoun, so what al-Zamakhsharī said is valid. The grammarians have two views about the tanwīn-bearing active participle before the speaker's yāʾ, like the verse above and the saying of another:
3808 - Is there a youth from the nobles of the people who will carry me, and none will carry me but the son of a carrier? And the saying of another:
3809 - He is not one who wearies me, while among people there is a friend who gives enjoyment, when a friend fails me
One: that it is tanwīn, and that its tanwīn with the pronoun is irregular, even if we say that the pronoun after it is in the accusative position. The other: that it is not tanwīn but a nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya). Ibn Mālik argued for this by his saying:
"wa-laysa bi-muʿyīnī ..." [incomplete in the source]
and also by his saying:
3810 - The one who comes to me is not to be given help while disappointed, for he has manifold what he hoped for
The point of the evidence from the first: if it were tanwīn, the yāʾ before it should be dropped, because it is a defective noun with tanwīn, and the defective noun with tanwīn loses its yāʾ in the nominative and genitive because of the meeting of two sukūns.
The point of the evidence from the second: the article al-, does not combine with the tanwīn (nūn). What favours the first view is the presence of the nūn in his saying «والآمِرُوْنَه» and in his saying:
3811 - And he did not lean back while the people were all present with him, and the hands of the seekers of gifts were his rain clouds
For the nūn stands in the place of tanwīn in the dual and the plural, in the same manner. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is also read with kasra on the nūn, which is very far-fetched, because if the nūn is for protection it does not attach to nouns, and if it is the nūn of the plural it does not remain in annexation (iḍāfa)." I say: this dilemma is correct were it not for the answer given above, though with some strain and departure from the rules; and were it not for fear of tedium, I would have exhaustively covered the views of the grammarians on this question.

It was also read «مُطَّلِعُوْن» with tashdīd like the majority, «فأَطَّلِعَ» as an imperfect in the accusative with an implied «أَنْ», in answer to the interrogative. It was also read «مُطْلِعون» lightened, «فَأَطْلَعَ» lightened as a past verb, and lightened as an imperfect in the accusative as before. One says: ṭalaʿa ʿalaynā fulān and aṭlaʿa, like akrama, and iṭṭalaʿa with tashdīd, with one meaning.

As for the reading of those who made the verb passive, the one standing in place of the agent has three possibilities. The first: that it is the maṣdar of the verb, that is: "the aṭlāʿ was aṭlaʿa'd." The second: the implied preposition [and its noun]. The third, and it is the sound one: that it is the pronoun of the one who said to his companions what he said; for one says ṭalaʿa Zayd and another made him ascend (aṭlaʿahu), so the hamza in it is for transitivity. As for the first two views, Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī held them in his «Lawāmiḥ», saying: "ṭalaʿa and iṭṭalaʿa mean he appeared and became visible, and aṭlaʿa iṭlāʿan when he came and approached. The meaning of that is: 'Are you approaching, so that I approach?' The maṣdar is set in it in place of the agent, by the estimation: 'the iṭlāʿ was iṭlāʿa'd', or by the estimation of an omitted preposition, that is: 'it was aṭlaʿa by him', because aṭlaʿa is intransitive just as aqbala is."

The Shaykh rejected these two views, saying: "We have mentioned that aṭlaʿa with hamza is a transitive form of the intransitive ṭalaʿa. As for his saying 'or the omitted preposition, that is: aṭlaʿa bihi', this is not permissible, because the object of what is not named for its agent (the passive) cannot be omitted since it is a deputy for it; just as the agent cannot be omitted without its governor, so too this. If you said 'Zayd is mamrūr or maghḍūb,' meaning 'by him' or 'at him,' it would not be permissible." I say: Abū al-Faḍl does not claim that the deputy for the agent is omitted; he only said "by estimation of the omitted preposition." The meaning of that: when the preposition was omitted by extension, the pronoun turned nominative and became latent in the verb, as is claimed in the omission of the returning pronoun of a relative when it is in the genitive when the conditions of omission are absent; and this is called omission by gradation.

semin-durr:55-55.t: His saying: {فَرَآهُ}: conjoined to «فاطَّلَعَ». Sawāʾ al-jaḥīm is its middle. The best of what was said about it is what Ibn ʿAbbās said: it was so called because the distance from it to the sides is equal. It is related from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar that he said to Abū ʿUbayda: "I used to write until my sawāʾ ran out" [i.e. until the middle of my ink-pot ran out].

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {تالله}: an oath carrying the sense of wonder. «إنْ» is either the lightened [inna] or the negative; and the lām is either the distinguishing lām or has the meaning of «إلاَّ». On both estimations it is the answer to the oath, I mean inna and what falls within its scope.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {بِمَيِّتِينَ}: Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «بمائِتين»; the two are like ḍayyiq and ḍāʾiq. This has already preceded.

And his saying: «أفما»: there is the well-known disagreement in it. Al-Zamakhsharī estimated it: "Are we immortal and in bliss, so are we not dead?" Others make the hamza fronted from the fāʾ.

semin-durr:59-59.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ مَوْتَتَنَا}: accusative as a maṣdar. The governor in it is the adjective [participle] before it, and it is a mufarragh (emptied) exception. It was also said: it is a disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) exception, that is: "but the first death was ours in the world." This is close in meaning to the saying of Allah the Exalted: {لاَ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الموت إِلاَّ الموتة الأولى} [al-Dukhān: 56]; there is a fine discussion about it, and its verification will come there, Allah willing.

semin-durr:60-60.t: And his saying: {إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ} up to his saying: «العامِلون» may be the speech of the speaker, and it may be the speech of the Creator, the Exalted.

semin-durr:62-62.t: His saying: {نُّزُلاً}: a tamyīz (specification) of «خَيْرٌ». The "betterness" is relative to what the disbelievers chose over others. The zaqqūm is a poisonous tree from which milk comes out; whenever it touches anyone's body, it swells and he dies. Tazaqqum is swallowing hateful things with force and effort. The saying of Abū Jahl, who was a pure Arab: "We know zaqqūm only as dates with butter," is sheer obstinacy and lying.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {رُءُوسُ الشياطين}: there are two views about it. The first: that it is literal, and that the "heads of the devils" are a particular tree in the region of Yemen called al-Astan, which al-Nābigha mentioned:
3812 - She shies from an astan, its lower parts black, like maidservants going out in the morning carrying bundles
It is a bitter tree of repulsive appearance; the Arabs named it so by likening it to the heads of devils in ugliness, then it became a base to which things are likened. It was also said: the shayāṭīn are a kind of snakes that have crests. He said:
3813 - A little old woman swears when I swear, like the crested devil of the ḥamāṭ tree
And it was said: it is a tree called al-ṣawm, and from it is the saying of Sāʿida ibn Juʾayya:
3814 - Assigned to the heights of the ṣawm, watching them from the places of sunset, with shrunken belly, thin-waisted
On this basis the Arabs were addressed with what they know, and this tree exists, so the speech is literal.
The second: that it is of the category of imagery and similitude. That is because everything that is disliked and judged ugly in natures and form is likened to what the imagination pictures, even if it has not seen it. The devils, though they exist, are not seen by the Arabs, yet He addressed them with the imaginative figures to which they were accustomed, as in the saying:
3815 - ... [the first half is missing in the source] and sharp blue [spears] like the fangs of ghouls
and he did not see their fangs; indeed, they do not exist at all.

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying: {لَشَوْباً}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the shīn, and it is a maṣdar in its original sense. It was also said that the passive participle is meant by it, and the reading of Shaybān the grammarian «لَشُوباً» with ḍamma indicates this. Al-Zajjāj said: "The one with fatḥa is a maṣdar and the one with ḍamma is a noun meaning mashūb (mixed)," like al-naqḍ in the sense of al-manqūḍ. He conjoined with «ثمَّ» for one of two reasons: either because He delays what they think will quench their thirst, to add to their torment, so He used «ثم», which indicates a delay; or because custom decrees that drinking comes after eating, so He acted on that pattern. As for filling the belly, it follows eating immediately, so He conjoined it to what precedes with fāʾ. And «مِنْ حميمٍ» is an adjective of «شَوْباً». Al-shawb: mixing and blending; from it: shāba l-labana yashūbuhu, that is: he mixed and blended it.

semin-durr:74-74.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ عِبَادَ الله}: a disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) exception from those who were warned, because it is a threat and they did not enter into this threat.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying: {فَلَنِعْمَ}: the answer to an implied oath, that is: "by Allah." Like it is the saying:
3816 - By my life, how excellent are the two masters you were both found to be ... [incomplete in the source]
The specified object of praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, that is: "we."

semin-durr:79-79.t: His saying: {سَلاَمٌ على نُوحٍ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and there are several views on it. One: that it explains «تَرَكْنا». The second: that it explains its object, that is: "We left praise upon him, namely these words." It was said: there is an implied saying, that is: "so We said: peace." It was said: «تَرَكْنا» was made to include the meaning of "We said." It was said: «تَرَكْنا» was given power over what follows. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And We left upon him among the later generations this phrase, namely {سَلاَمٌ على نُوحٍ}, meaning: they greet him with a greeting and pray for him; and it is of the quoted speech, as you say: 'I recited a sūra We sent down.'" What he said is the view of the Kufans: they made the clause accusative in position as an object of «تَرَكْنا», not that it is made to include the meaning of saying, but it is on its own meaning, unlike the view before it, which is also among their views. ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] read «سَلاماً», which is a direct object of «تَرَكْنا», and «كذلك» is an adjective of a maṣdar, or a ḥāl from its pronoun, as has been explained more than once.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
His saying: {وَإِنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِ}: the pronoun in it has two views, the more apparent being that it refers to Nūḥ, that is: of those who followed him (yushāyiʿuhu), that is, followed him in his religion and firmness in the command of Allah. The second: that it refers to Muḥammad ﷺ. The shīʿa may be applied to the one who came earlier, as in the saying:
3817 - I have no partisans except the family of Aḥmad, and I have no path except the path of truth
He made the family of Aḥmad, who came before him while he is a follower of theirs, his shīʿa. Al-Farrāʾ said this. But the well-known usage is that the shīʿa comes later.

semin-durr:84-84.t: His saying: {إِذْ جَآءَ}: there are two views on what governs it. One: an implied "remember," which is the customary one. The second: al-Zamakhsharī said: "the sense of partisanship (mushāyaʿa) in «الشِّيْعَةِ», meaning: 'and among those who followed him in his religion and piety when he came to his Lord.'" The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is not permissible, because it involves separating the governor and the governed by a foreigner, namely «لإِبْراهيمَ», because it is foreign to his shīʿa and to «إذ». The prohibition increases because he estimated it 'from those who followed him when he came,' [because he estimated 'from those who followed him', making the governor before it the ṣila of a relative noun and separating it from «إذ» by a foreigner, namely «لإِبراهيمَ»]. Also the lām of ibtidāʾ prevents what precedes it from operating in what follows it. If you said 'inna ḍāriban la-qādimun ʿalaynā Zaydan', its estimation being 'inna ḍāriban Zaydan la-qādimun ʿalaynā', it would not be permissible."

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying: {إِذْ قَالَ}: a badal from the first «إذ», or an adverbial of «سليم», that is: "he was safe from it at the time of his saying such and such," or an adverbial of «جاء»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is not clear. The like of what follows has preceded.

semin-durr:86-86.t: His saying: {أَإِفْكاً}: there are several views on it. One: that it is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), that is: "Do you want gods besides Allah, as a falsehood?" So «آلهةً» is the direct object, and «دونَ» is an adverbial of «تُرِيْدون». The complements of the verb were fronted for the sake of emphasis, and it was made good by the governor being the end of a verse-ending. He fronted the object of purpose before the direct object for emphasis, because it confronts them with the fact that they are in falsehood and error. Al-Zamakhsharī began with this view. The second: that it is a direct object of «تُريدون», and «آلهةً» is a badal of it; he made them the very falsehood, for emphasis, so he substituted it and explained it by it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned only this. The third: that it is a ḥāl from the agent of «تُريدون», that is: "Do you want gods while lying, or possessing falsehood?" Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to it. The Shaykh said: "Making the maṣdar a ḥāl is not regular except after «أمَّا», as in: ammā ʿilman fa-ʿālimun."

semin-durr:91-91.t: His saying: {فَرَاغَ}: that is: he turned aside secretly. Its root is from the rawaghān of the fox, which is its going back and forth and not staying in one place.

semin-durr:93-93.t: And «ضَرْباً» is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, that is: "he turned upon them striking"; or a maṣdar of a verb, that verb being a ḥāl, its estimation: "he turned upon them, striking a blow"; or «راغ» was made to include the meaning of "he strikes," which is far-fetched. And «باليمينِ» is attached to «ضَرْباً» if we do not make it an emphatic, otherwise to its governor. Al-yamīn: it may mean one of the two hands, which is the apparent sense; it may mean strength, and the bāʾ on this is for the state, that is: "accompanied by strength"; and it may mean the oath, in fulfilment of His saying {وتالله لأَكِيدَنَّ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 57], and the bāʾ on this is causal. He made the second «راغ» transitive with «على» because it was with striking that overpowered them from above to below, unlike the first, which was with rebuke of them; and He used the pronoun of rational beings in His saying «عليهم», following the assumption of its worshippers that they are like rational beings.

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying: {يَزِفُّونَ}: a ḥāl from the agent of «أَقْبَلوا», and «إليه» may be attached to what precedes it or to what follows it. Ḥamza read «يُزِفُّون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from azaffa, which has two meanings. One: from azaffa yuzifffu, that is: he entered into the zafīf, which is hurrying, or the zifāf of the bride, which is walking in her manner, because the people were at ease about their affair. This second was thus said, but it is nothing, since the meaning is that when they heard of it they hastened, hurrying; the hamza on this is not for transitivity. The second: that it is from azaffa baʿīrahu, that is: he made it go at the zafīf, which is hurrying, or at the zifāf, and what is in it has preceded. The rest of the Seven read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ, from zaffa l-ẓalīmu yazifffu, that is: the male ostrich ran swiftly. The origin of zafīf is for ostriches.
Mujāhid, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «يَزِفُون» from wazafa yazifu, that is: he hurried. However, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: "We do not know it in the sense of zaffa," though others knew it. Mujāhid, one of those who read it so, said: "al-wazīf is al-nasalān (scurrying)."
It was also read «يُزَفُّون» in the passive and «يَزْفُوْن» like yarmūn, from zafāhu in the sense of ḥadāhu (he drove him), as if some of them drove others because of their haste toward him. Between His saying «فأَقْبَلُوا» and His saying «فراغ عليهم» there are omitted sentences which the context indicates, that is: "the news reached them, so they returned from their festival," and the like.

semin-durr:96-96.t:
His saying: {وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ}: there are four views on this «ما». The best: that it means "that which," that is: "and He created that which you make"; the "work" here is shaping and carving, as in: ʿamila l-ṣāʾighu l-siwāra, that is: the goldsmith fashioned the bracelet. What favours its being "that which" is that what precedes it is also "that which," that is: "Do you worship that which you carve, while Allah created you and created that which you work by carving?"
The second: that it is maṣdarī (verbal-noun forming), that is: "He created you and your deeds." The Ashʿarites made it evidence for the creation of the servants' acts by Allah the Exalted, and that is the truth; however, the evidence for this from here is not strong, because of the clarity, mentioned above, that it means "that which." Makkī said: "It must be that «ما» and the verb are a maṣdar, brought to show that Allah is the creator of all things." He also said: "This is more fitting to His saying {مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ} [al-Falaq: 2]: the reciters agreed on the iḍāfa, which indicates that He is the creator of evil. ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd departed from the people and read «مِنْ شرٍّ» with tanwīn to affirm a creator alongside Allah the Exalted." Al-Zamakhsharī took up this statement here regarding its being maṣdarī and denounced whoever said it.
The third: that it is interrogative, an interrogative of rebuke and belittling of their affair, that is: "and what is it that you do?" The fourth: that it is negative, that is: "the deed is in truth not yours, so you do nothing." The sentence «والله خَلَقكم» is a ḥāl, and its meaning then: "Do you worship idols in a state that contradicts that, namely that Allah is the creator of you and of them all?" It may also be resumptive.

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His saying: {فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ}: «معه» is attached to an omitted element by way of clarification, as if someone said: "With whom did he reach the age of striving?" and it was said: with his father. It is not permissible to attach it to «بَلَغَ», because that would require that both reached the limit of striving together. It is not permissible to attach it to «السَّعْيِ», because the ṣila of a maṣdar does not precede it, so what was said is settled. Al-Zamakhsharī said the meaning of this. Whoever is lenient with adverbials permits its attachment to al-saʿy.
His saying: «ماذا ترى»: «ماذا» may be compound with the interrogative predominating, so it is accusative by «تَرَى», and it and what follows are in the accusative position by «انْظُر», because it suspends it (muʿallaqa); and «ما» may be interrogative and «ذا» a relative, so they are a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the sentence is also suspended; and «ماذا» may mean "that which," so it is governed by «انْظُرْ». The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «تُري» with ḍamma and kasra; the two objects are omitted, that is: "you show me it of your patience and endurance." The rest of the Seven read «تَرَى» with two fatḥas, from ra'y (opinion). Al-Aʿmash and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «تُرَى» with ḍamma and fatḥa, meaning: what appears to you and occurs to your mind.
And his saying: «ما تُؤْمَرُ»: «ما» may mean "that which," the returning pronoun being implied, that is: tuʾmaruhu; the original is tuʾmaru bihi, but omitting the preposition is regular, so the returning pronoun is omitted only when it is accusative in position, so its omission here is not like its omission in your saying «جاء الذي مَرَرْتُ». It may also be maṣdarī. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "or 'your command', by annexing the maṣdar to the object and calling the thing commanded an 'amr'." By "the object" he means the one whose agent is not named (the passive); however, there is the well-known disagreement about estimating a maṣdar by a verb in the passive.

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying: {فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا}: there are three views on its jawāb (apodosis). The first, and it is the apparent one: that it is omitted, that is: "the angels called out to him," or "their patience appeared," or "We magnified their reward for them." Some estimated it as: after the vision, that is: "what happened happened, of what the state and description speak, whose essence is not grasped." Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported that the estimation is: "fa-lammā aslamā aslamā wa-tallahu" ("when they submitted, they submitted and he laid him down"), saying: like the saying:
3818 - And when we had passed through the courtyard of the tribe ... [incomplete in the source]
that is: "when we passed, we passed and he turned aside." This is ascribed to Sībawayh and his teacher al-Khalīl. There is a consideration in it: the identity of the two verbs that stand in the position of protasis and apodosis; unless it is said that the difference in the verse is made by conjunction to the verb, while in the line the second operates on «ساحة» and also by conjunction to it. The apparent view is that the like of this does not suffice for difference.
The second: that the apodosis is «وتَلَّه للجبين» and the wāw is redundant; this is the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash. The third: that it is «وناديناه», with the wāw also redundant.
ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh and Ibn ʿAbbās read «سَلَّما». It was also read «اسْتَسْلَما».
And «تَلَّه», that is: he threw him down and laid him on his side. It was said: it is throwing with force, and its origin is from "he threw him on the tall," which is a raised place, or from al-talīl, which is the neck, that is: he threw him on his neck; then it was said of every throwing down, even if not on a hill or on a neck. And al-mitall: the spear with which one throws down. Al-jabīn: what flanks the forehead on this side and that; and its plural aḥbun is irregular. Its analogical form in the paucal is ajbina like arghifa, and in the plural of multitude: jubun and jubnān, like raghīf, rughfān and rughuf.

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying: {نَبِيّاً مِّنَ الصالحين}: accusative as a ḥāl, and it is a muqaddara (anticipated) ḥāl. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "If the sacrificed one is Isḥāq, it is apparent that it is an anticipated ḥāl; and if Ismāʿīl is the sacrificed one, and this glad tiding was a glad tiding of the birth of Isḥāq, then al-Zamakhsharī made that a place of a question. He said: 'If you say: there is a difference between this and His saying {فادخلوها خَالِدِينَ} [al-Zumar: 73]: that is, the thing entered exists along with the existence of the entering, while eternity does not exist with them, so you estimated "estimating eternity," and it was sound; but it is not so for the one given glad tidings, for he is non-existent at the time of the glad tidings, and the non-existence of the one given glad tidings necessitates the non-existence of his ḥāl, because the ḥāl is an adornment that stands only by what is adorned. And this one given glad tidings, who is Isḥāq, when he came into being, prophethood did not come into being with his existence either; rather it was delayed from him for a long time. So how is "nabiyyan" made an anticipated ḥāl, when the ḥāl is a description of the agent or the object at the time of the action from him or on him? For eternity, though it is not their description at the time of entering Paradise, you estimate it as their description, because the meaning is "estimating eternity"; but prophethood is not so, for there is no way for it to exist or be anticipated at the time of the glad tidings of Isḥāq, because Isḥāq does not yet exist.' I say: this is a question of subtle approach. What resolves the difficulty: an omitted muḍāf must be estimated, namely His saying: 'We gave him glad tidings of the existence of Isḥāq as a prophet,' that is, 'of his being brought into existence with the anticipated state of his prophethood.' So the governor of the ḥāl is the existence, not the verb of glad tidings, and by that it returns to the like of His saying {فادخلوها خَالِدِينَ} [al-Zumar: 73]." End [of the quotation]. It is fine speech.
His saying: «من الصالحين»: it may be an adjective of «نَبِيَّاً», and it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «نبيَّاً», so it is a nested ḥāl. It may also be a second ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its occurrence is by way of praise and commendation, because every prophet must be among the righteous."

semin-durr:116-116.t:
His saying: {وَنَصَرْنَاهُمْ}: the pronoun refers to Mūsā and Hārūn and their people. It was also said: it refers to the two with the wording of the plural, for magnification, as in his saying:
3819 - If you wish, I will forbid women other than you ... [incomplete in the source]
{ياأيها النبي إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ} [al-Ṭalāq: 1].
His saying: «فكانوا هم»: «هم» may be tawkīd (emphasis), may be a badal, and may be a faṣl (separating pronoun), and this is the most apparent.

semin-durr:123-123.t: His saying: {وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ}: the majority read it with a hamza with kasra, hamzat qaṭʿ. Ibn Dhakwān read it as a hamzat waṣl; the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] did not report it from him but reported it from a group other than him. The reason for the two readings is that it is a foreign name which the Arabs played with, cutting its hamza at one time and connecting it at another, and they said of it: Ilyāsīn, like Jibrāʾīn. It was also said: the connected reading may mean that his name is Yāsīn, and then the definite article al- was added to it, as it was added to al-Yasaʿ, which has preceded. This Ilyās was said to be the son of the Ilyāsīn mentioned later, of the descendants of Hārūn, the brother of Mūsā. It was also said: rather, Ilyās is Idrīs. The reading of ʿAbd Allāh, al-Aʿmash and Ibn Wathāb «وإنَّ إدْريس» indicates this. It was also read «إدْراس», like Ibrāhīm and Ibrāhām. In the codex of Ubayy and his reading is his saying «وإن إيْليسَ»: a hamza with kasra, then a yāʾ with sukūn with two dots below, then a lām with kasra, then a yāʾ with two dots below with sukūn, then a sīn with fatḥa.

semin-durr:124-124.t: His saying: {إِذْ قَالَ}: an adverbial for His saying «لمن المرسلين».

semin-durr:125-125.t:
His saying: {بَعْلاً}: the reciters read it with tanwīn in the accusative, and it is "the Lord" in the language of Yemen. Ibn ʿAbbās heard a man of theirs seeking a stray animal, and another said: "I am its baʿl," so he said: "Allāhu akbar," and recited the verse. It was also said: it is a proper name of a particular idol, with a story in tafsīr. It was also said: it is a proper name of a particular woman who came to them with misguidance and they followed her, as it came in tafsīr. The holder of this view is supported by the reading of those who read «بَعْلاءَ» on the pattern of ḥamrāʾ.
His saying: «وتَذَرُوْنَ»: it may be a ḥāl with an implied mubtadaʾ, and it may be conjoined to «تَدْعُون», so it enters into the scope of the denunciation.

semin-durr:126-126.t: His saying: {الله رَبَّكُمْ وَرَبَّ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read the three in the accusative, from three possibilities: the accusative of praise, or badal, or explication if we say that the annexation of afʿal is a pure annexation. The rest read in the nominative: either as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "He is Allah," or on the basis that the name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ and what follows is the khabar. It is reported from Ḥamza that when he connected [the verses] he put it in the accusative, and when he paused he put it in the nominative. This is very good, and in it is a combination of the two reports.

semin-durr:128-128.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ عِبَادَ الله}: a connected (muttaṣil) exception from the agent of «فكذَّبوه»; it indicates that among his people there were some who did not call him a liar, and so they were excepted. It is not permissible that they be excepted from the pronoun of «لَمُحْضَرون», because it would necessarily mean that they were included among those who called him a liar, but they would not be brought forth because they are sincere servants of Allah. This is clearly invalid. It is not to be said that it is excepted from it as a disconnected exception, because the meaning would become: "but the sincere servants of Allah, other than these, will not be brought forth." There is no need for this in any way, since by it the structure of the speech is spoiled.

semin-durr:130-130.t:
His saying: {على إِلْ يَاسِينَ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read {على آلِ يَاسِينَ}, annexing «آل», meaning the family, to «ياسينَ». The rest read it with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the lām, connected to «ياسين», as if he had pluralised «إلياس» with a sound plural. As for the first: he meant by the āl Ilyās, son of Yāsīn as mentioned above, and his companions. It was also said: what is meant by this Yāsīn is the aforementioned Ilyās, so he would have two names. His āl: his clan and his believing people. It was also said: what is meant by Yāsīn is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ﷺ.
As for the second reading, it was said that it is the plural of the aforementioned Ilyās. It was pluralised with regard to his companions, like al-Mahālaba and al-Ashāʿitha for al-Muhallab and his sons, and al-Ashʿath and his people; and it is in origin the plural of those attributed to Ilyās, the original being Ilyāsī like Ashʿarī. Then the doubling of the two [yāʾs] was found heavy, so one of the two yāʾs of attribution was dropped; when it was pluralised with a sound plural, two sukūns met: one of the two yāʾs and the yāʾ of the plural, so the first of them was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, and it became Ilyāsīn as you see. Like it: al-Ashʿarūn and al-Khubaybūn. He said:
3820 - Enough for me of the support of the two Khubaybs, enough!
A part of this has already preceded at the end of al-Shuʿarāʾ at «الأَعْجَمِيْن». However, al-Zamakhsharī rejected this: that if it were as mentioned, it would have to be made definite by al-, and it would be said: ʿalā l-Ilyāsīn. I say: because whenever a proper name is pluralised with a sound plural or dualised, the article al- is necessarily attached, since its proper-name status disappears, so one says al-Zaydān, al-Zaydūn, al-Zaynabāt; and no attention is paid to their saying Jumādayān and ʿAmāyatān, names of two months and two mountains, because of their rarity.
Al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read «على إلياسينَ» with a connected hamza, on the basis that it is the plural of Ilyās and his people attributed to him by the way mentioned. This one is clear because of the presence of the definite article in it, like al-Zaydīn. ʿAbd Allāh read «على إدْراسين» because he read in the first place «وإنَّ إدْريَس». Ubayy read «على إيليسِيْنَ» because he read in the first place «وإنَّ إيليسَ», as I have verified from him. These two indicate that Ilyāsīn is a plural of Ilyās.

semin-durr:137-137.t: His saying: {مُّصْبِحِينَ}: a ḥāl. It is from the complete (tāmma) aṣbaḥa, meaning "entering into the morning." From it: «إذا سَمِعْتَ بسُرى القَيْنِ فاعلَمْ أنه مُصْبِح» (when you hear of the night journey of the smith, know that he is one who stays on into the morning), that is: staying in the morning. This has already preceded in Sūrat al-Rūm.

semin-durr:138-138.t: His saying: {وباليل}: conjoined to the preceding ḥāl, that is: "and accompanied by the night."

semin-durr:140-140.t:
His saying: {إِذْ أَبَقَ}: an adverbial of «المرسلين», that is: "he was of the messengers even in this state." Abaqa means he fled. One says: abaqa l-ʿabdu yaʾbiqu ibāqan, so he is ābiq, and the plural is ubbāq like ḍurrāb. There is a second dialect form: abiqa with kasra, yaʾbaqu with fatḥa. The man is "yaʾbiqu," likened to it in hiding. And the saying of the poet:
3821 - ... the knots of the rope and the abaq were made firm
It was said: it is hemp.

semin-durr:141-141.t: His saying: {فَسَاهَمَ}: that is: he contended with them in drawing lots (musāhama), which is casting lots. Its origin is that the arrow comes out for the one who wins.

semin-durr:142-142.t:
His saying: {وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ}: a ḥāl. Al-mulīm: the one who has done what he is blamed for. He said:
3822 - Many a blameworthy one has not been blamed, and many a pursued for a sin has no sin
One says: alāma fulān, that is: he did what is blameworthy. It was also read «مَليم» with fatḥa on the mīm, from lāma yalūmu, and it is very irregular since its analogical form would be malūm, because it is from the roots with wāw, like maqūl and maṣūn. It was said: but it is taken from līma ʿalā kadhā in the passive. Like it in that: shubtu l-shayʾa, so it is mashīb, and duʿiya, so it is madʿiyy, while the analogical forms are mashūb and madʿuww, because they are from yashūbu and yadʿū.

semin-durr:144-144.t: His saying: {فِي بَطْنِهِ}: apparently it is attached to «لَبِثَ». It was also said: it is a ḥāl, that is: "settled."

semin-durr:145-145.t:
His saying: {بالعرآء}: that is: "in the open land," like: Zayd bi-Makka (Zayd is in Mecca). Al-ʿarāʾ is the wide land in which there is no vegetation and no landmark, derived from ʿurī, which is the absence of covering; the barren land was so called because it is not covered by anything. Al-ʿurā, short, is the side; from it comes iʿtarāhu, that is: he made for its side. As for the lengthened [al-ʿarāʾ], it is, as preceded, the spacious land. He said:
3823 - I lifted a foot whose stumbling I do not fear, and cast my garments on the open ground of the back

semin-durr:146-146.t:
His saying: {مِّن يَقْطِينٍ}: it is of the pattern yafʿīl from qatana bi-l-makān, when one stays in it and does not leave. It was said: al-yaqṭīn is everything that has no stem of wood, like cucumber, gourd and melon. In His saying «شجرةً» is what refutes the saying of some that the "tree" in their speech is what has a stem of wood; rather the sound view is that it is more general. For that reason it was specified by His saying «مِنْ يَقْطِين». As for His saying {والنجم والشجر} [al-Raḥmān: 6], there is no evidence in it, because it is the use of a general word for one of its denotations. It was also said: rather Allah caused this particular yaqṭīn to grow on a stem as a miracle for him, so it came on its basic sense.
And if you built from al-waʿd a pattern like yaqṭīn you would say yawʿīd. It is not to be said that the wāw is dropped because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra, like yaʿidu, the imperfect of waʿada; because the condition of that yāʾ is that it be the yāʾ of the imperfect. This is among the things by which the morphologists test one another.

semin-durr:147-147.t: His saying: {أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ}: there are seven views on this «أو»; their verification and evidence have preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara at His saying {أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ} [verse 19], so turn to them there: doubt in relation to the addressees, that is: the one who sees them is in doubt when he sees them; vagueness (ibhām) in relation to the fact that Allah the Exalted left their number vague; permission (ibāḥa), that is: whoever looks at them is permitted to estimate them at this number or at this number; likewise choice (takhyīr), that is: he is free to estimate them as so much or so much; and "bal" (iḍrāb) and the meaning of "wāw" are both clear.

semin-durr:149-149.t: His saying: {فاستفتهم}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is conjoined to its like at the beginning of the sūra, though they are far apart." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "When they have counted separation by one sentence, such as 'Eat meat and strike Zayd and bread,' among the ugliest constructions, how then with many sentences and diverse stories?" I say: someone might say: the separation, however much between the conjoined sentences, is tolerated. As for the example he mentioned, it is of the category of single words. Do you not see how he conjoined «خبزاً» to لحماً?

semin-durr:150-150.t: His saying: {وَهُمْ شَاهِدُونَ}: a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya) from the angels. The link is the wāw, and here it is obligatory because there is no other link.

semin-durr:152-152.t: The majority read «وَلَدَ اللَّهُ» as a past verb attributed to the Name of Majesty, that is: "He brought a child"; exalted is Allah far above what they say. It was also read «وَلَدُ اللَّهِ» by annexing al-walad to Him, that is: they say: the angels are His child. The mubtadaʾ was omitted because it is known, and its khabar retained. Al-walad is of the pattern faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl, like al-qabaḍ; for this reason it occurs as a khabar of the singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine. You say: hādhī waladī and hum waladī.

semin-durr:153-153.t:
His saying: {أَصْطَفَى}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the hamza, being an interrogative hamza in the sense of denial and rebuke; the hamzat waṣl was omitted with it as unnecessary.
Nāfiʿ in one report, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and al-Aʿmash read with a hamzat waṣl, which stays when beginning and drops in continuous speech. There are two views on it. One: that it is with the intention of the interrogative, and was omitted only because it is known. From it is the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
3824 - Then they said: "Do you love her?" I said: "Immensely! The number of the sand and the pebbles and the dust" (that is: "Do you love her?")
The second: that this sentence is a badal for the sentence quoted by "saying," namely «وَلَدَ اللَّهُ», that is: they say so and so, and they say: "He chose this kind over this kind." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash have read it so. This reading, even though this is its construal, is weak. What weakens it is that denial surrounds this sentence on both sides, namely His saying «وإنهم لَكاذبون» and {مَالَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ}; whoever makes it an affirmation has made it an intruder between two kinsmen." The Shaykh said: "It is not an intruder between two kinsmen, because it has an evident connection with their saying «وَلَدَ اللَّهُ». As for His saying «وإنهم لَكاذبون», it is a parenthetical sentence between two sayings of the disbelievers, brought for denunciation and emphasis that their saying is from their falsehood."
Abū al-Baqāʾ reported that it was read «آصْطفى» with a lengthened hamza. He said: "It is very far-fetched."

semin-durr:154-154.t: His saying: {مَالَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ}: two interrogative sentences, neither of which is connected to the other in terms of i'rab. He asks first about what has settled and been established for them, an interrogative of denial; and second an interrogative of wonder at their making this unjust judgment, namely that they ascribed to their Lord the baser of the two sexes, which they take as an ill omen, and one of them hides from his people at the glad tidings of it, and [ascribed] the better of the two sexes to themselves.

semin-durr:160-160.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ عِبَادَ الله}: a disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) excepted. The one excepted from: either the agent of «جَعَلُوا», that is: "they made a kinship between Him and the jinn, except the servants of Allah." The second: that it is the agent of «يَصِفُوْن», that is: "but the servants of Allah describe Him with what befits Him, the Exalted." The third: that it is the pronoun of «مُحْضَرون», that is: "but the servants of Allah are saved." On this the sentence of glorification is parenthetical. The apparent meaning of Abū al-Baqāʾ's words is that it may be a connected exception, because he said: "excepted from «جَعَلُوا» or «مُحْضَرون». It may also be disconnected." The apparent meaning of this expression is that in the first two views it is connected, not disconnected. It is not far-fetched, as if it were said: "and the people made [a kinship]," then these were excepted from them; and everyone who did not make a kinship between Allah the Exalted and the jinn is, with Allah, sincere, free from shirk.

semin-durr:161-161.t:
His saying: {وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is conjoined to the ism of «إنَّ»; «ما» is negative, and «أنتم» is its ism or a mubtadaʾ; in «أنتم» the addressee is given precedence over the absent, since the original is: "fa-innakum wa-maʿbūdakum mā antum wa-huwa," so the address was given precedence. «عليه» is attached to His saying «بفاتِنين». The pronoun refers to «ما تعبدون», with an omitted muḍāf estimated, and «فاتنين» is made to include the meaning of "bringing under temptation"; the estimation is: "You and your gods, you and they will not bring anyone under temptation to worship Him except those whom it was foreknown in His knowledge are of the people of burning in Hell." So «مَنْ» is the object of «فاتِنين», and the exception is mufarragh. The second: that it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); on this it is fine to stop at «تعبدون», as it is fine in your saying: "inna kulla rajulin wa-ḍayʿatahu" (every man and his estate); al-Kisāʾī related: "kullu thawbin wa-thamanahu." The meaning: you are joined with your objects of worship, as one estimates in "kullu rajulin wa-ḍayʿatuhu muqtarinān." And His saying: {مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفَاتِنِينَ} is resumptive, that is: "You, over what you worship, will not bring under temptation, or bring to temptation, except he who is going to burn among you." Al-Zamakhsharī said it. But Abū al-Baqāʾ weakened the second, and likewise the Shaykh, following him, in weakening it because it does not come readily to the understanding.
I say: the apparent view is that it is conjoined, and the resumption of {مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفَاتِنِينَ} is not clear; and the truth is more deserving to be followed. Al-Zamakhsharī permitted the pronoun in «عليه» to refer to Allah the Exalted, saying: "If you say: how do they tempt them against Allah? I say: they corrupt them against Him by their misleading, from your saying: fatana fulānun ʿalā fulānin imraʾatahu (so-and-so alienated his wife against him), as you say: he corrupted her against him and made her disappointed against him."

semin-durr:163-163.t:
And «مَنْ هو»: it may be a relative or an indefinite noun with a description.
The majority read «صالِ الجحيم» with kasra on the lām, because it is a defective noun in annexation whose final letter was dropped due to the meeting of two sukūns, and it is construed according to the wording of «مَنْ», so it is singular as it is singular. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read with ḍamma on the lām followed by a wāw, in what al-Hudhalī reported from them, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya from al-Ḥasan. They also read with ḍamma without a wāw, in what Ibn Khālawayh reported from them and from al-Ḥasan only, in what al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Faḍl reported. As for with the wāw, it is a sound plural with wāw and nūn, and it is construed first on the wording of «مَنْ», so it is singular in His saying «هو», and secondly on its meaning, so it is pluralised in His saying «صالُو», and the nūn is dropped because of annexation. Among what is construed on both wording and meaning in one sentence which is the ṣila of a relative is the saying of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مَن كَانَ هُوداً أَوْ نصارى} [al-Baqara: 111]: it is singular in «كان» and plural in «هوداً». Like it is his saying:
3825 - ... and woke up those of you who were asleep
As for without the wāw, it is possible that it is also plural, and the wāw was dropped in writing as it was dropped in pronunciation. They often do this: they drop in writing what drops in pronunciation. From it is «يَقُضُّ الحق» in the reading of those who read it with the dotted ḍād, which is written without a yāʾ, and likewise {واخشون، اليوم} [al-Māʾida: 3]. It is also possible that it is singular, and its due on this is only kasra on the lām because it is the ʿayn of a defective noun, and the ʿayn of a defective noun is always with kasra; and the lām, which is the yāʾ, is dropped due to the meeting of two sukūns, like: hādhā qāḍi l-balad.
They mentioned two directions for it. One: that it is inverted (maqlūb); the original is ṣāliy then ṣāyil: they moved the lām to the place of the ʿayn, so the i'rab falls on the ʿayn, then the lām of the word was dropped after the inversion, so the word became as you see, and its pattern on this is fāʿ. So one says on this: jāʾa ṣāl, raʾaytu ṣālan, marartu bi-ṣālin, and it becomes in pronunciation like your saying: hādhā bābun, raʾaytu bāban, marartu bi-bābin. Its parallel in mere inversion: shākin and lāthin for shāʾik and lāʾith; but shāʾik and lāʾith before inversion are sound, and became by it weak, defective; unlike «صال», which was before the inversion weak, defective, and became by it sound. The second: that the lām was dropped for heaviness without inversion. This, to me, is easier than the former, and we have seen them ignore the dropped lām and put the i'rab on the ʿayn. It has been read «وله الجوارُ» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and {وَجَنَى الجنتين دَانٌ} with ḍamma on the nūn, likening it to janāḥ and jānn. They also said: mā bālaytu bihi bālatan, the original being bāliya like ʿāfiya. A part of this has preceded at His saying {وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٌ} for those who read it with ḍamma on the shīn.

semin-durr:164-164.t:
His saying: {وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ}: there are two views on it. One: that «منَّا» is a description of an omitted described noun that is the mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the sentence of His saying {إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ}; its estimation: "there is none among us but has a station." Omitting the mubtadaʾ with «مِنْ» is good and eloquent. The second: that the mubtadaʾ is also omitted, and {إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ} is its description whose described noun was omitted, and the khabar on this is the preceding prepositional phrase. The estimation: "and there is none among us but has a station." Al-Zamakhsharī said: he omitted the described and put the description in its place, as in the saying:
3826 - I am the son of Jalā, climber of the mountain passes ... [incomplete in the source]
[and the saying]:
3827 - She shoots with the two hands of one who was the best of men at shooting
The Shaykh rejected it, saying: "This is not an omission of the described and substitution of the description in its place, because what is omitted is a mubtadaʾ, and {إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ} is its khabar; and because no speech is formed from His saying «وما منَّا أحد», and His saying {إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ} is the point of the benefit. Even if one imagines that {إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} is in the position of a description, they have stated that «إلاَّ» cannot be a description when its described noun is omitted, and that it differs from «غير» when it is a description in that, because «غير» is firmly established in description and «إلاَّ» is not firmly established in it. He made that like His saying 'I am the son of Jalā,' that is, 'I am the son of a man who disclosed,' and 'bi-kaffay kāna,' that is, 'a man who was.' The grammarians have counted it among the ugliest poetic necessities [in that he omitted the described while the description is a sentence not preceded by «مِنْ», unlike the saying 'minnā ẓaʿana wa-minnā aqāma', by which they mean 'among us a group who departed, and among us a group who stayed']." Something like this has preceded in al-Nisāʾ at His saying {وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب إِلاَّ لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ} [al-Nisāʾ: 159]. The apparent meaning of this speech and what follows is that it is the speech of the angels. It was also said: it is the speech of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The object of «الصافُّون» and «المُسَبِّحون» may be intended, that is: "those who set in rows our feet or our wings, and those who glorify Allah the Exalted"; and it may not be intended at all, that is: "we are of the people of this act."

semin-durr:172-172.t: His saying: {إِنَّهُمْ لَهُمُ المنصورون}: an explanation of the word (al-kalima), so it may have no position in i'rab; it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, or accusative with an implied verb, that is: "it is: 'They are the ones helped,'" or "I mean by the word this expression," and that is by way of quotation; for if you stated the verb before it, quoting the sentence after it, it would be sound, as if you said: "I meant this expression," as you say "I wrote: Zayd is standing" and "inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «كلماتنا» in the plural.

semin-durr:177-177.t:
His saying: {نَزَلَ بِسَاحَتِهِمْ}: the majority read «نَزَلَ» in the active; ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] in the passive, the prepositional phrase standing in place of its agent. Al-sāḥa is the courtyard free of buildings; its plural is sūḥ, so its alif is from wāw, and it is diminutivised as suwayḥa. The poet said:
3828 - It was all one whether they did not send out the livestock to graze, or sent them out, while the courtyards were dust-covered
By this the weakness of al-Rāghib's saying becomes clear, that it is from the roots with yāʾ, since he counted it under the root s-y-ḥ, then said: "Al-sāḥa: the wide place; from it sāḥat al-dār. Al-sāʾiḥ: water flowing in the courtyard. Sāḥa fulān fī l-arḍ: he passed as the wanderer passes; a man sāʾiḥ and sayyāḥ." End. It is possible that it has two roots, but he should have mentioned which is better known, or mentioned both. The second object of «أبْصر» is omitted, either for brevity because the first indicates it, or by restriction. The specified object of censure is omitted, that is: "their morning."

semin-durr:180-180.t: His saying: {رَبِّ العزة}: Rabb is annexed to al-ʿizza because of His specification with it, as if it were said "possessor of might," as you say ṣāḥib ṣidq because of his specification with it. It was also said: what is meant is the created might that exists among His creation. On the two views follows the issue of the oath: on the first, an oath is validly made by it, because it is one of His attributes, the Exalted; unlike the second, for an oath is not validly made by it.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
His saying: {والصافات صَفَّا}: Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza read with assimilation of the tāʾ of «الصافَّاتِ», «الزَّاجراتِ» and «التاليات» into the ṣād of «صَفَّاً», the zāy of «زَجْراً» and the dhāl of «ذِكْراً»; and they did likewise in {والذاريات ذَرْواً} [al-Dhāriyāt: 1], in {فالملقيات ذِكْراً} [al-Mursalāt: 5] and in {العاديات ضَبْحاً} [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 1], with a divergence from Khallād in the last two. Abū ʿAmr runs on his principle of assimilating close-sounding letters, as is known of his principle, while Ḥamza departs from his principle; and the difference between their two doctrines is that Abū ʿAmr permits rawm (partial vowel) and Ḥamza does not. This is as they agreed in assimilating {بَيَّتَ طَآئِفَةٌ} in [Sūrat] al-Nisāʾ [v. 81], even though assimilating the like of it is not part of Ḥamza's principle. The rest read with all of that pronounced clearly.
The object of «الصَّافَّات» and «الزَّاجراتِ» is not intended, for the meaning is "the doers of that". Abū l-Baqāʾ parsed «صَفَّاً» as a direct object, in that it may apply to the thing arrayed. I say: this is weak.
