It was also said that it is intended, and the meaning: "those who array themselves", namely the angels, or the fighters, or the worshippers; or "those who array their wings", namely the birds, as in {والطير صَآفَّاتٍ} [al-Nūr: 41]; and "those who drive off the clouds", or "the disobedient", if the scholars are meant by them. Al-zajr is repelling with force, and is strength of voicing. He recited:
3789 - زَجْرَ أَبي عُرْوَةَ السِّباعَ إذا ... أشْفَقَ أَنْ يَخْتَلِطْنَ بالغَنَم
(Like the driving off of the beasts of prey by Abū ʿUrwa, when he feared they would mix with the flock.)
And زَجَرْتُ الإِبِلَ والغنمَ is said when they were frightened by your voice. As for «والتاليات», «ذِكْراً» may be its object, the "remembrance" meaning the Qur'an and other than it of glorification and praise; and «ذِكْراً» may also be a maṣdar from the meaning of «التاليات», which accords better with what precedes. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The fāʾ in «فالزَّاجراتِ» and «فالتالياتِ» either indicates the sequence of their meanings in existence, as in his saying:
3790 - أيا لَهْفَ زَيَّابةَ للحارثِ الصَّا ... بحِ فالغانِمِ فالآيِبِ
(Alas for Zayyāba, for al-Ḥārith who raided at dawn, then took spoils, then returned.)
as though he said: the one who made a dawn raid, then took spoils, then returned; or on their sequence in degree in some respects, as in: 'Take the better, then the more complete', and 'Do the finer, then the more beautiful'; or on the sequence of those they qualify in that, as you say: 'May Allah have mercy on those who shave their heads, then on those who shorten.' Here, if you take the qualified as one, it indicates the sequence of the attributes in merit. If the single one is the angels, the merit is for the array, then the driving, then the recitation, or the reverse. If you take the qualified as three, they are ordered in merit, so the arrayers possess merit, the drivers greater merit, and the reciters a more brilliant merit, or the reverse." By "the reverse" in both places he means that you rise from the excellent to the more excellent to the preferred, or you begin with the lowest, then the excellent, then the most excellent.
The wāw in these is of oath, and the answer is His saying: {إِنَّ إلهكم لَوَاحِدٌ}. You know the discussion of the second and third wāw: whether it is of oath or of conjunction.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {رَّبُّ السماوات}: it may be a second khabar, a badal from «لَواحدٌ», or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. The plural of "easts" and "wests" is with regard to the whole year, for the sun has three hundred and sixty risings and three hundred and sixty settings. As for His saying «المَشْرِقَيْن والمغربين», it is with regard to summer and winter.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {بِزِينَةٍ الكواكب}: Abū Bakr read «زينة» with tanwīn and «الكواكب» accusative. It has two aspects. One: that «الزينة» is a maṣdar, with its agent omitted, its estimation being: "by Allah's adorning the stars, in their being luminous and beautiful in themselves". Two: that «الزينة» is a noun for that with which adornment is made, like al-līqa, a noun for what the inkwell is stuffed with; so «الكواكبُ» on this is accusative by the implied «أَعْني» ("I mean"), or is a badal ishtimāl from «سماء الدنيا», i.e. its stars, or from the position of «بزينة».
Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ likewise, except that they put «الكواكب» in the genitive, with «زينة» meaning that with which adornment is made, and «الكواكب» a badal or a clarification (bayān) of «الزينة».
The rest read with annexation of «زينة» to «الكواكب». It admits three aspects. One: that it is the annexation of the more general to the more specific, so it is for clarification, like "a garment of silk" (ثوبُ خَزّ). Two: that it is a maṣdar annexed to its agent, i.e. "by the stars' adorning the heaven with their light". Three: that it is annexed to its object, i.e. "by Allah's adorning it by making it radiant and luminous in itself".
Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd read it with tanwīn and «الكواكب» nominative. If you make it a maṣdar, «الكواكب» is nominative by it; and if you make it a noun for that with which adornment is made, then on this «الكواكبُ» is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are the stars", which is in force a badal. Al-Farrāʾ forbade the governing of a maṣdar with tanwīn and claimed it was not heard. That is an error, because of His saying {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ} [al-Balad: 14], as will come, Allah willing.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {وَحِفْظاً}: accusative as a maṣdar by an implied verb, i.e. "We guarded it with a guarding"; or as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, with the wāw redundant, the governor in it being «زيَّنَّا»; or with an implied governor, i.e. "for its guarding We adorned it"; or by carrying it over to the preceding meaning, i.e. "We created the lowest heaven as adornment and guarding". And «من كلِّ» is attached to «حِفْظاً» if it is not a confirming maṣdar, and to the omitted verb if it is made a confirming maṣdar. It may also be an adjective of «حِفْظاً».

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لاَّ يَسَّمَّعُونَ}: the two brothers and Ḥafṣ read it with doubled sīn and mīm. The origin is يَتَسَمَّعون, assimilated. The rest read both lightened. Abū ʿUbayd preferred the first and said: "If it were lightened, it would not be made transitive with «إلى»." This was answered: the meaning of the speech is "they do not listen attentively to the Highest Assembly". Makkī said: "Because it runs in the course of its reciprocal, which is يتَسَمَّعُون; so just as تَسَمَّع is made transitive with «إلى», سَمِع is made transitive with «إلى»; and فَعِلْتُ and افتعلْتُ are the same in transitivity; so تَسَمَّع is the reciprocal of سمع, and استمع is also the reciprocal of سَمِع, so سَمِعَ is made transitive as its reciprocal is."
This clause is cut off from what precedes it, and it cannot be an adjective of «شيطان» in meaning, since the estimation would become "of every rebellious devil that does not hear or listen", which is corrupt. Nor can it be an answer to the question of a questioner, "Why is it guarded from the devils?", since the meaning of that would be corrupted. Some said: the origin of the speech is "لئلا يَسْمَعوا", with the lām and «أَنْ» omitted, so the verb became nominative. There is strain in that. Abū l-Baqāʾ erred in allowing it to be an adjective, a ḥāl, or resumptive: the first two are plainly corrupt, and the third, if he meant by it the explanatory resumption (al-istiʾnāf al-bayānī), is also corrupt, and if he meant disconnection, as I set out, it is correct.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {دُحُوراً}: the majority read ḍamma on the dāl. It has several aspects. One: mafʿūl lahu, i.e. "for the sake of repulsion". Two: that it is a maṣdar of «يُقْذَفُون», i.e. "they are repelled with repulsion" or "they are cast with casting"; so the figurative looseness is in the first or in the second. Three: that it is a maṣdar of an implied verb, i.e. "they are repelled with a repulsion". Four: that it is in the position of ḥāl, i.e. "possessing repulsion" or "repelled". And it was said: it is a plural of dāḥir, like qāʿid and quʿūd, so it is a ḥāl by itself, without interpretation. It was reported from Abū ʿAmr that he read «ويَقْذِفُون» in the active.
ʿAlī, al-Sulamī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «دَحورا» with fatḥa on the dāl. It has two aspects: one, that it is an adjective of an implied maṣdar, i.e. "a casting that repels", like al-ṣabūr and al-shakūr. The second: that it is a maṣdar like al-qabūl and al-walūʿ. It has been stated that it is restricted to a few words.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَنْ خَطِفَ}: two aspects. One: that it is in the position of the nominative as a badal from the pronoun of «لا يَسَّمَّعون», and it is the better, since it is non-affirmative. The second: that it is accusative on the basis of exception. The meaning: that the devils do not hear the angels except one who snatches. I say: «مَنْ» may be conditional, its answer «فَأَتْبَعَه»; or a relative with its khabar «فَأَتْبَعَه»; and it is a disconnected exception. They stated that such a clause is a disconnected exception, as in His saying: {لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُصَيْطِرٍ * إِلاَّ مَن تولى وَكَفَرَ} [al-Ghāshiya: 22-23]. And «الخَطْفَةُ» is a maṣdar made definite by the generic or the familiar al-.
The majority read «خَطِفَ» with fatḥa on the khāʾ and kasra on the ṭāʾ, lightened. Qatāda and al-Ḥasan read both with kasra and doubled ṭāʾ, which is the dialect of Tamīm ibn Murr and Bakr ibn Wāʾil. From them also, and from ʿĪsā, with fatḥa on the khāʾ and kasra on the ṭāʾ doubled. From al-Ḥasan also, خَطِفَ like the majority. The origin of the two readings is اخْتَطَفَ; when assimilation was intended, the tāʾ was made sākin with the khāʾ before it sākin, so the khāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns, then the ṭāʾ was given kasra by assimilation to the vowel of the khāʾ. This is clear. As for the second, it is very problematic, because the kasra on the ṭāʾ was only for the kasra of the khāʾ, which is absent. It was explained as imagination (tawahhum): when they wanted assimilation they transferred the vowel of the tāʾ to the khāʾ, so it was given fatḥa, while they imagined it to be kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns as stated, so they made the ṭāʾ follow the imagined vowel of the khāʾ. If they did that in what inflection requires, then doing it elsewhere is more fitting. In sum, it is an explanation of an irregularity.
Ibn ʿAbbās read «خِطِفَ» with kasra on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ, lightened, which is assimilation, like their saying نِعِمَ with kasra on the nūn and the ʿayn. «فاتَّبَعَه» was also read with doubling.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {أَم مَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ}: the majority read with doubled mīm, the origin being «أم مَنْ», which is the connected «أم», «مَنْ» being conjoined to «هم». Al-Aʿmash read it lightened, which is a second interrogative; the hamza is also interrogative, «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is omitted, i.e. "Are those We created stronger?" So they are two independent clauses, and what has intellect is given preference over what has not, which is why «مَنْ» was used. Lāzib and lāzim have the same meaning ("clinging"); «لازم» was also read.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {بَلْ عَجِبْتَ}: the two brothers read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa. The fatḥa is clear; it is the pronoun of the Messenger, or of anyone from whom that is sound. As for the ḍamma, it is by turning it to the speaker, i.e. "Say, O Muḥammad: Nay, I marvel", or by ascribing it to the Creator the Exalted in the way that befits Him; the verification of this was given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara, with what occurs of it in the Book and the Sunna. It is reported of Shurayḥ that he denied it and said: "Allah does not marvel." It reached Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, who said: "Shurayḥ was pleased with his own opinion; it was read by one who is more knowledgeable than he," meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.
His saying: «ويَسْخَرون» may be resumptive, which is the more evident, or a ḥāl. Jannāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read «ذُكِروا» lightened.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {أَوَ آبَآؤُنَا}: Ibn ʿĀmir and Qālūn read it with sukūn on the wāw, as the conjunctive «أو» that implies doubt. The rest read it with fatḥa, as an interrogative hamza that entered upon the conjunctive wāw. This disagreement also runs in [Sūrat] al-Wāqiʿa. A parallel was given in [Sūrat] al-Aʿrāf in His saying: {أَوَ أَمِنَ أَهْلُ القرى} [al-Aʿrāf: 98]. For whoever gives the wāw fatḥa, two aspects are allowed in «آباؤنا». One: that it is conjoined to the position of «إنَّ» and its subject. The second: that it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in «لَمبعوثون», being sufficed by the separation made by the interrogative hamza. For whoever gives it sukūn, the first is the only one, and not the second, on the view of the majority, for lack of a separator.
Al-Zamakhsharī made this clear when he said: "«آباؤنا» is conjoined to the position of «إنَّ» and its subject, or to the pronoun in «مَبْعوثون»; and what permitted conjunction upon it is the separation by the interrogative hamza." The Shaykh said: "As for his saying 'conjoined to the position of «إنَّ» and its subject', the doctrine of Sībawayh is the opposite; for in your saying 'إن زيداً قائمٌ وعمروٌ', «عمرٌو» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted. As for his saying 'or to the pronoun in «مبعوثون»' to the end, that is also not permissible, because the interrogative hamza does not enter except on clauses and not on a singular; for if conjoined to a singular, the verb would govern the singular by means of the conjunction, and the interrogative hamza is not governed by what precedes it. So His saying «أو آباؤنا» is a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, the estimation being: 'or our fathers will be raised', indicated by what precedes it. So if you say 'أقام زيدٌ أو عمرٌو', «عمرٌو» is a mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, for what we have said.'" [Translator's note: the source text reads «أو علىلضميرِ في "مبعوثون"», a typographical slip for «أو على الضمير».]
I (al-Samīn) say: as for the first refutation, it is not binding, because he (al-Zamakhsharī) does not adhere to the doctrine of Sībawayh. As for the second, the hamza is an emphasis of the first, so it in truth enters upon the clause, except that «إنَّ» with its subject and khabar separated the two hamzas. Evidence for this is what he himself said in [Sūrat] al-Wāqiʿa, for he said: "The interrogative hamza entered upon the conjunctive particle. If you say, how is the conjunction upon the pronoun of «لَمبعوثون» good without emphasis by «نحن»? I say: it is good because of the separator, which is the hamza, as it was good in His saying {مَآ أَشْرَكْنَا وَلاَ آبَاؤُنَا} [al-Anʿām: 148] because of the separation by the emphasizer of the negation." End. So he did not mention here other than this aspect, with his likening it to his saying "by the separation of the emphasizer of the negation", because «لا» is an emphasis of the negation preceded by «ما». But this is problematic, in that a particle, when repeated for emphasis, is not in the general case repeated except by repeating what was connected with it first, or its pronoun. The discussion of it has gone before. Three aspects are derived for the nominative of «آباؤنا»: conjunction upon the position of «إن» and its subject; conjunction upon the latent pronoun in «لَمبعوثون»; and the nominative as a mubtadaʾ with an implied khabar. The governor of «إذا» is omitted, i.e. "shall we be raised when we have died?" This is if you make it an adverb not including the sense of condition; but if you make it conditional, its answer is the governor in it, i.e. "when we have died, shall we be raised or gathered?"
«إذا» was also read without interrogative. The discussion of it went before in [Sūrat] al-Raʿd.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {وَأَنتُمْ دَاخِرُونَ}: a ḥāl clause. The governor in it is the clause that stands in place of it, «نعم», i.e. "you will be raised while you are abased, humbled". The Shaykh said: "Ibn Wathāb read «نَعِمْ» with kasra on the ʿayn." I say: it was given in [Sūrat] al-Aʿrāf that al-Kisāʾī read it so wherever it occurs, and his saying here gives the impression that Ibn Wathāb is alone in it.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "«فإنما هي» is the answer of an implied condition, its estimation being: 'If that is so, it is only a single cry.'" The Shaykh said: "The conditional clause is often implied before a fāʾ when its estimation is allowable, but no necessity calls for that here; and the condition is not omitted with its answer remaining, except where the verb is jussive in what is called the answer to the imperative, the prohibition and what is mentioned with them. At the outset, its omission is not permissible."
His saying: «هي» is the pronoun of the resurrection, indicated by the context; since their being raised arises from the cry, it was made the cry itself figuratively. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is vague (mubhama), clarified by its khabar." The Shaykh said: "He and Ibn Mālik often say that the pronoun is explained by its khabar."

semin-durr:20-20.t: Abū Ḥātim paused at «وَيْلَنا» and made what follows from the words of the Creator the Exalted. Some made {هذا يَوْمُ الدين} from the speech of the disbelievers, and pause at it; and His saying {هذا يَوْمُ الفصل} from the words of the Creator the Exalted. It was also said: all of it is from their speech; on this, His saying «تُكَذِّبون» is either an iltifāt from the first person to the second, or the addressing of some of them to others.

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ}: the majority read it accusative. It has two aspects: one, conjunction on the relative; two, that it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is stronger in meaning." I say: he said "in meaning" only because it is weak in technical terms; for since conjunction is possible, one does not turn away from it. ʿĪsā ibn Sulaymān al-Ḥijāzī read it nominative, conjoined to the pronoun of «ظَلموا», which is weak for lack of a governor. As for His saying {وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعْبُدُونَ}, this is not permissible in it, because wrongdoing is not ascribed to them, if the devils are not meant by them; and if that is meant by them, the nominative is also permissible in it, as stated.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {إِنَّهُمْ مَّسْئُولُونَ}: the majority read it with kasra, as a resumptive that gives the reason. It was also read with fatḥa on the omission of the lām of cause, i.e. "stop them for the sake of Allah's questioning them".

semin-durr:25-25.t: His saying: {مَا لَكُمْ}: it may be cut off from what precedes it, with the thing asked about not being mentioned, for which reason some estimated it: "about their deeds". It may also be the thing asked about in meaning, so it suspends the question. And «لا تَناصَرون» is a ḥāl clause. The governor in it is the settledness in «لكم». And it was said: rather it is on the omission of the preposition and the subjunctive «أنْ»; when «أن» was omitted, the verb became nominative; the original is: في أنْ لا. The reading of al-Bazzī «لا تَّناصرون» with doubled tāʾ was given earlier. «تَتَناصرون» was also read, on the original.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {عَنِ اليمين}: a ḥāl from the agent of «تَأْتُوننا». And al-yamīn is either the limb, by which strength is expressed, or the oath, because two parties to a contract by oath each wipe the right hand of the other; so the estimation on the first is "you come to us strong", and on the second "swearing, taking oaths".

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {إِنَّا لَذَآئِقُونَ}: the apparent sense is that it is from the report of the disbelievers who were followed, or the jinn, that they will taste the punishment. There is no deviation in this speech. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "'So the word of our Lord became binding upon us: we shall surely taste.' He means Allah's threat that we shall surely taste His punishment without fail. Had he related the threat as it is, he would have said: 'You will surely taste'; but he turned it into the first-person wording, because they are speaking of themselves. Like it is the saying of the speaker:
3790 - ب لقد عَلِمَتْ هوازِنُ قَلَّ مالي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Hawāzin surely knew that my wealth was little ...)
and had he related her speech he would have said: 'your wealth is little.' From it also is the saying of the one administering an oath to the one swearing: 'Swear: «لأَخْرُجَنَّ»' and «لَتَخْرُجَنَّ»: the hamza is for relating the swearer's words, and the tāʾ for the administrator's turning to the one sworn." [Translator's note: the source numbers this verse 3790, the same number as the verse in entry 37:1, and prefixes it with a stray «ب»; it is rendered as it stands.]

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: i.e. the day when they ask and go back over the speech among themselves.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {وَصَدَّقَ المرسلين}: i.e. Muḥammad ﷺ confirmed them. ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) read «صَدَقَ» with the dāl lightened, and «المُرْسلون» as its agent, i.e. "they spoke truly in what they brought of their glad tidings of him, peace be upon him".

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {لَذَآئِقُو العذاب}: the majority drop the nūn and read the genitive. Some read it with the nūn kept and the accusative, which is the original. Abān ibn Taghlib, from ʿĀṣim, and Abū l-Sammāl in one report, read it with the nūn dropped and the accusative, treating the nūn like the tanwīn in its omission because of the meeting of two sukūns, as in His saying {أَحَدٌ الله الصمد} [al-Ikhlāṣ: 1-2], [and as in his saying]:
3791 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا ذاكرَ اللَّهَ إلاَّ قليلا
(... nor one who remembers Allah save a little.)
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It was read irregularly in the accusative, which is a slip of its reciter, because the nūn is dropped from the active participle and it is put in the accusative only if it has the alif and lām." I say: it is not a slip, for what I have told you. Abū l-Sammāl also read «لَذائِقٌ» in the singular with tanwīn, and «العذابَ» accusative. Its explanation is on the omission of a collective noun that has this description, i.e. "you are a group, or an assemblage, tasting", so that the subject and the khabar agree in plurality.

semin-durr:39-39.t: And His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا كُنْتُمْ}: i.e. "except the recompense of what you used to do".

semin-durr:40-40.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ عِبَادَ الله}: a disconnected exception.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالصَّافَّاتِ صَفًّا (١) فَالزَّاجِرَاتِ زَجْرًا (٢)).
The wāw is for the oath, and the answer to the oath is: إِنَّ إِلَهَكُمْ.
And (صَفًّا) is an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun), and likewise «زَجْرًا». It has been said: «صَفًّا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because الصَّفّ (the row) may apply to what is set in rows.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ الْمَشَارِقِ (٥)).
(رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ): a badal (substitute) from وَاحِدٌ [Translator's note: in the preceding verse, إِنَّ إِلَهَكُمْ لَوَاحِدٌ], or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is the Lord" (هُوَ رَبُّ).

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ الْكَوَاكِبِ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِزِينَةٍ الْكَوَاكِبِ): it is read with annexation (iḍāfa) [Translator's note: i.e. بِزِينَةِ الْكَوَاكِبِ]. There are two views on it. The first: it is the annexation of the species to the genus, as in your saying "a door of iron" (بَابٌ حَدِيدٌ) [Translator's note: so in the source, without annexation]; so the adornment is the stars. The second: الزِّينَة is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent; and it has been said: to its object, i.e. "We adorned the heaven by Our adorning the stars" (زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ بِتَزْيِينِنَا الْكَوَاكِبَ).
It is also read with tanwīn on the first and the accusative on الْكَوَاكِب, and there are two views on it: the first, that the maṣdar with tanwīn governs its object. The second: [it is read] with tanwīn on the first and the genitive on the second as a badal (substitute); and with the nominative on the second by the maṣdar [Translator's note: i.e. as its agent], meaning "in that its adornment is the stars" (بِأَنَّ زِينَتَهَا الْكَوَاكِبُ), or on the implied form "they are the stars" (هِيَ الْكَوَاكِبُ).

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَحِفْظًا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَارِدٍ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَحِفْظًا), i.e. "and We guarded it with a guarding" (وَحَفِظْنَاهَا حِفْظًا).
And (مِنْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted verb.

ukberi-tibyan:8-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَا يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَى الْمَلَأِ الْأَعْلَى وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ (٨) دُحُورًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ وَاصِبٌ (٩) إِلَّا مَنْ خَطِفَ الْخَطْفَةَ فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَسَّمَّعُونَ): it is put in the plural according to the meaning of كُلّ; the position of the clause is genitive as an adjective (ṣifa), or accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or it is resumptive.
It is read with the sīn undoubled [Translator's note: i.e. لَا يَسْمَعُونَ]; and it was made transitive with إِلَى by construing it on the meaning of يَصِفُونَ [Translator's note: so in the source; probably يُصْغُونَ "they incline their ears" is meant].
And with it doubled; and the meaning is one.
And (دُحُورًا): it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the meaning of يَقْذِفُونَ [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has يُقْذَفُونَ], or a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); and it may be the plural of دَاحِر, like قَاعِد and قُعُود, in which case it is a ḥāl.
(إِلَّا مَنْ): an exception from the same genus, i.e. "they do not listen to the angels except stealthily, and then they are pursued by the meteors."
And on (خَطِفَ) there is a discussion mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara.
And (الْخَطْفَةُ) is a maṣdar; the alif and lām in it are for the genus, or for what is known among them.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (بَلْ عَجِبْتَ وَيَسْخَرُونَ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَلْ عَجِبْتَ): with a fatḥa on the tāʾ, as address; and with a ḍamma on it [Translator's note: i.e. عَجِبْتُ]: it has been said that it is a report about the Prophet ﷺ; and it has been said that it is about Allah the Exalted, the meaning being: His servants marvelled.
And it has been said: the meaning is that it reached a degree at which one would say about the like of it: "I marvelled."

ukberi-tibyan:22-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ (٢٢) مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ (٢٣) وَقِفُوهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ مَسْئُولُونَ (٢٤) مَا لَكُمْ لَا تَنَاصَرُونَ (٢٥) بَلْ هُمُ الْيَوْمَ مُسْتَسْلِمُونَ (٢٦) وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ (٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَزْوَاجَهُمْ): the majority read the accusative, i.e. "and gather their spouses" (وَاحْشُرُوا أَزْوَاجَهُمْ); or it [Translator's note: the wāw] has the meaning of "with" (مَعَ), which is stronger in meaning.
It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, in the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun in ظَلَمُوا.
(لَا تَنَاصَرُونَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It has been said: the implied form is "in that you do not help one another" (فِي أَنْ لَا تَنَاصَرُونَ).
And (يَتَسَاءَلُونَ) is a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّكُمْ لَذَائِقُو الْعَذَابِ الْأَلِيمِ (٣٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَذَائِقُو الْعَذَابِ): the correct way is the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with the accusative [Translator's note: i.e. لَذَائِقُو الْعَذَابَ], and this is a slip by its reader, because the nūn is dropped from the active participle and it governs the accusative [only] when it has the alif and lām.

ukberi-tibyan:41-47.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ رِزْقٌ مَعْلُومٌ (٤١) فَوَاكِهُ وَهُمْ مُكْرَمُونَ (٤٢) فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ (٤٣) عَلَى سُرُرٍ مُتَقَابِلِينَ (٤٤) يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِكَأْسٍ مِنْ مَعِينٍ (٤٥) بَيْضَاءَ لَذَّةٍ لِلشَّارِبِينَ (٤٦) لَا فِيهَا غَوْلٌ وَلَا هُمْ عَنْهَا يُنْزَفُونَ (٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَوَاكِهُ): it is a badal (substitute) from «رِزْقٌ», or on the implied form "it is" (هُوَ).
And (مُكَرَمُونَ): with the undoubled consonant, and with the doubled one for intensity.
And (فِي جَنَّاتٍ): it may be an adverbial (ẓarf), or a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a second khabar (predicate).
And likewise «عَلَى سُرُرٍ»; and عَلَى may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مُتَقَابِلِينَ», with مُتَقَابِلِينَ being a ḥāl from «مُكْرَمُونَ» or from the pronoun in the preposition-phrase.
And (يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ): it may be resumptive, or like what precedes it, or an adjective (ṣifa) of «مُكْرَمُونَ».
And (مِنْ مَعِينٍ) is a naʿt (adjective) of كَأْس, and likewise «بَيْضَاءُ».
And (عَنْهَا) is attached to «يُنْزَفُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُطَّلِعُونَ (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُطَّلِعُونَ): it is read with the doubled consonant, on the pattern مُفْتَعِلُونَ. It is also read with the undoubled one [Translator's note: i.e. مُطْلِعُونَ], i.e. "causing your companions to look" (مُطْلِعُونَ أَصْحَابَكُمْ). And it is read with a kasra on the nūn [Translator's note: i.e. مُطْلِعُونِ]; this is very far-fetched, because if the nūn is the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya), it is not attached to nouns, and if it is the nūn of the plural, it does not remain in annexation.

ukberi-tibyan:58-67.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَيِّتِينَ (٥٨) إِلَّا مَوْتَتَنَا الْأُولَى وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ (٥٩) إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ (٦٠) لِمِثْلِ هَذَا فَلْيَعْمَلِ الْعَامِلُونَ (٦١) أَذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُزُلًا أَمْ شَجَرَةُ الزَّقُّومِ (٦٢) إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهَا فِتْنَةً لِلظَّالِمِينَ (٦٣) إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ فِي أَصْلِ الْجَحِيمِ (٦٤) طَلْعُهَا كَأَنَّهُ رُءُوسُ الشَّيَاطِينِ (٦٥ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَآكِلُونَ مِنْهَا فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ (٦٦) ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْهَا لَشَوْبًا مِنْ حَمِيمٍ (٦٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا مَوْتَتَنَا): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the active participle [Translator's note: i.e. governed by the sense of بِمَيِّتِينَ, as an absolute object]. It has been said: it is an exception.
And (نُزُلًا) is a tamyīz (specification).
And (شَوْبًا): it may have the meaning of مَشُوب (mixed), or be a maṣdar in its proper sense.

ukberi-tibyan:73-80.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ (٧٣) إِلَّا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ الْمُخْلَصِينَ (٧٤) وَلَقَدْ نَادَانَا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ الْمُجِيبُونَ (٧٥) وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ (٧٦) وَجَعَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ هُمُ الْبَاقِينَ (٧٧) وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرِينَ (٧٨) سَلَامٌ عَلَى نُوحٍ فِي الْعَالَمِينَ (٧٩) إِنَّا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٨٠)
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ): it has been dealt with in al-Naml.
(فَلَنِعْمَ الْمُجِيبُونَ): the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. "We" (نَحْنُ).
And «هُمْ» is a separating pronoun (faṣl).
And (سَلَامٌ عَلَى نُوحٍ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of an accusative by تَرَكْنَا. It has been said: it is the explanation of an omitted object, i.e. "We left upon him a praise, which is: peace" (تَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ ثَنَاءً هُوَ سَلَامٌ).
It has been said: the meaning of «تَرَكْنَا» is "We said" (قُلْنَا). And it has been said: the saying is implied.
It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, in the accusative, as the object of «تَرَكْنَا»; and likewise the [similar] verses in this sura.
And (كَذَلِكَ) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a recompense like that" (جَزَاءً كَذَلِكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:84-86.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ جَاءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ (٨٤) إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَاذَا تَعْبُدُونَ (٨٥) أَئِفْكًا آلِهَةً دُونَ اللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ (٨٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ جَاءَ), i.e. "remember when he came" (اذْكُرْ إِذْ جَاءَ); and it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) whose governor is (مِنْ شِيعَتِهِ).
And (إِذْ قَالَ) is a badal (substitute) from the first إِذْ; and it may be an adverbial for سَلِيم, or for جَاءَ.
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَاذَا تَعْبُدُونَ): it is like «مَاذَا تُنْفِقُونَ», and it has been dealt with in al-Baqara.
(أَئِفْكًا): it is accusative by «تُرِيدُونَ», and «آلِهَةً» is a badal (substitute) from it; the implied form is: "and the worship of gods" (وَعِبَادَةُ آلِهَةٍ), because الْإِفْك is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so the badal from it is implied likewise; and the meaning rests on that.
It has been said: «إِفْكًا» is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and «آلِهَةً» is the object of تُرِيدُونَ.

ukberi-tibyan:93-94.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَرَاغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْبًا بِالْيَمِينِ (٩٣) فَأَقْبَلُوا إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ (٩٤)).
(ضَرْبًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) from «فَرَاغَ», because its meaning is "he struck" [Translator's note: the source vowels it ضُرِبَ, passive]; and it may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (يَزِفُّونَ) is with the doubled consonant and the kasra, with a fatḥa on the yāʾ; and it is read with a ḍamma on it [Translator's note: i.e. يُزِفُّونَ]; they are two dialectal forms.
It is also read with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, a kasra on the zāy and the undoubled consonant [Translator's note: i.e. يَزِفُونَ]; its past tense is وَزَفَ, like وَعَدَ. The meaning of the doubled and undoubled forms is: hastening.

ukberi-tibyan:96-97.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ (٩٦) قَالُوا ابْنُوا لَهُ بُنْيَانًا فَأَلْقُوهُ فِي الْجَحِيمِ (٩٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ): it is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar). It has been said: it has the meaning of الَّذِي. It has been said: it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. And it has been said: it is interrogative, expressing contempt for their work.
And (مَا) [Translator's note: on the interrogative view] is accusative by تَعْمَلُونَ.
And (بُنْيَانًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ السَّعْيَ قَالَ يَا بُنَيَّ إِنِّي أَرَى فِي الْمَنَامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فَانْظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَى (١٠٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَاذَا تَرَى): «مَاذَا» may be a single noun in the accusative by «تَرَى», i.e. "what thing do you think?" (أَيَّ شَيْءٍ تَرَى).
And (تَرَى) is from الرَّأْي (opinion), not from seeing with the eye, nor the one transitive to two objects; rather it is as in your saying "he holds the opinion of the Khārijites" (هُوَ يَرَى رَأْيَ الْخَوَارِجِ); so it is transitive to one object.
It has been read «تُرِي» with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and a kasra on the rāʾ [Translator's note: the source prints «تَرَى»]; this too is from opinion, except that it was made causative with the hamza and so became transitive to two objects: «مَاذَا» is one of them, and the second is omitted, i.e. "you show me" (تُرِينِي).
It is also permissible that «مَا» be interrogative and «ذَا» have the meaning of الَّذِي; so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. "what is it that you think?" (أَيُّ شَيْءٍ الَّذِي تَرَاهُ), or "that you show me" (الَّذِي تُرِينِيهِ).

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ (١٠٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَمَّا): its apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, its implied form being "the angels called him" (نَادَتْهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ), or "its merit became manifest" (ظَهَرَ فَضْلُهَا).
The Kufans said: the wāw is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "he laid him down" (تَلَّهُ), or "We called him" (نَادَيْنَاهُ).

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَبَشَّرْنَاهُ بِإِسْحَاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (١١٢)).
And (نَبِيًّا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إِسْحَاق.

ukberi-tibyan:123-124.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ (١٢٣) إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ (١٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ): it is an adverbial (ẓarf) for «مُرْسَلِينَ».
It has been said: it is by an implied «أَعْنِي» (I mean).

ukberi-tibyan:126-126.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ وَرَبَّ آبَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (١٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ وَرَبَّ): the three are read in the accusative, as a badal (substitute) from «أَحْسَنَ» [Translator's note: in the preceding verse, أَحْسَنَ الْخَالِقِينَ], or by an implied «أَعْنِي» (I mean).

ukberi-tibyan:130-130.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (سَلَامٌ عَلَى إِلْ يَاسِينَ (١٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلْ يَاسِينَ): it is read آلْ [يَاسِين], with a long vowel, i.e. "his family".
It has been read with a short vowel, a sukūn on the lām and a kasra on the hamza, the implied form being إِلْيَاسِيِّين, the singular of which is إِلْيَاسِيّ; then the plural was lightened, just as they said الْأَشْعَرُونَ [Translator's note: the source prints «إِلْيَاسِينَ» for the implied full form].
It is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, إِدْرَاسِينَ, people related to إِدْرِيس.

ukberi-tibyan:138-138.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَبِاللَّيْلِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (١٣٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَبِاللَّيْلِ): pausing on it is a complete pause.

ukberi-tibyan:143-144.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَوْلَا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ (١٤٣) لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلَى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ (١٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي بَطْنِهِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial), or an adverbial (ẓarf).
(إِلَى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to لَبِثَ, or a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a remaining until the day" (لُبْثًا إِلَى يَوْمِ).

ukberi-tibyan:147-147.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَى مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ (١٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ), i.e. one who saw them would say: "They are a hundred thousand or more."
It has been said: some of them say "a hundred thousand" and some of them say "more". We have dealt with this at His saying (أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ), and in another place (وُجُوهًا) [Translator's note: so in the source].

ukberi-tibyan:153-153.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَصْطَفَى الْبَنَاتِ عَلَى الْبَنِينَ (١٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَصْطَفَى): with a fatḥa on the hamza, which is for the interrogative; the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was dropped, the interrogative hamza making it unnecessary.
It is read with a long vowel [Translator's note: i.e. آصْطَفَى], and this is very far-fetched.
It has been read with a kasra on the hamza [Translator's note: i.e. اصْطَفَى, with hamzat al-waṣl], in the form of a statement, with the interrogative intended, as ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
ثُمَّ قَالُوا تُحِبُّهَا قُلْتُ بَهْرًا ... عَدَدَ الرَّمْلِ وَالْحَصَى وَالتُّرَابِ
("Then they said: You love her? I said: Exceedingly — as many as the sand, the pebbles and the dust.")
i.e. "Do you love her?" (أَتُحِبُّهَا). This is irregular in usage and in analogy, so it should not be read thus.

ukberi-tibyan:154-154.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ (١٥٤)).
(مَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ): an interrogative after an interrogative.

ukberi-tibyan:160-160.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِلَّا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ الْمُخْلَصِينَ (١٦٠)).
(إِلَّا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ): it may be excepted from the pronoun in (جَعَلُوا) and from (مُحْضَرُونَ); or it may be disconnected (munfaṣil) [Translator's note: i.e. a disconnected exception].

ukberi-tibyan:161-164.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ (١٦١) مَا أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفَاتِنِينَ (١٦٢) إِلَّا مَنْ هُوَ صَالِي الْجَحِيمِ (١٦٣) وَمَا مِنَّا إِلَّا لَهُ مَقَامٌ مَعْلُومٌ (١٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; it is weak to take it as having the meaning of "with" (مَعَ), since there is no verb here. And (مَا أَنْتُمْ) is a negation.
And (مَنْ) is in the position of an accusative by فَاتِنِين; it has the meaning of الَّذِي, or is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective.
And (صَالِ) is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with a ḍamma on the lām [Translator's note: i.e. صَالُو]; it may then be a plural according to the meaning of «مَنْ»; or it may have undergone metathesis, becoming صَائِل, after which the yāʾ was dropped, leaving «صَالِ».
It may also be without metathesis, on the pattern فَعْل [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the examples given, رَوِح and صَوِف, are on the pattern فَعِل], as they said "a windy day" (يَوْمٌ رَاحٌ) and "a woolly ram" (كَبْشٌ صَافٌ), i.e. رَوِحٌ and صَوِفٌ. (وَمَا مِنَّا إِلَّا لَهُ), i.e. "and there is not one of us but…" (أَحَدٌ إِلَّا); and it has been said: "except one who has" (إِلَّا مَنْ لَهُ). It has been dealt with in al-Nisāʾ.

zajjaj:174-174.t: ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهم حَتّى حِينٍ﴾: that is, until the term for which they were granted respite comes to an end.

zajjaj:177-177.t:
﴿فَإذا نَـزَلَ بِساحَتِهِمْ﴾: that is, when the punishment descends upon them; and the punishment of these people in this world was being killed.
And His saying: ﴿فَساءَ صَباحُ المُنْذَرِينَ﴾, that is: "how evil is the morning (فَبِئْسَ صَباحُ)".

zajjaj:180-180.t: ﴿سُبْحانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ العِزَّةِ﴾: there are three ways (wujūh) of reading it. Whoever reads it in the accusative (naṣb) does so as praise (madḥ) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; whoever reads it in the nominative (rafʿ) also does so as praise, in the sense of "He is the Lord of Might (هو رَبُّ العِزَّةِ)"; and whoever reads it in the genitive (khafḍ) does so following His saying "رَبِّكَ رَبِّ العِزَّةِ". The accusative may also be [understood as] "I mean the Lord of Might (أعْنِي رَبَّ العِزَّةِ)" and "I mention the Lord of Might (أذْكُرُ رَبَّ العِزَّةِ)".

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt
﷽
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والصّافّاتِ صَفًّا﴾ ("by those ranged in ranks"). Most readers pronounce the tāʾ distinctly, and it has also been read with assimilation of the tāʾ into the ṣād. Likewise ﴿فالزّاجِراتِ زَجْرًا﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 2] ("and those who drive with a driving"): if you wish you assimilate the tāʾ into the zāy, and if you wish you pronounce it distinctly; and likewise ﴿فالتّالِياتِ ذِكْرًا﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 3] ("and those who recite a Reminder").
﴿إنَّ إلَهَكم لَواحِدٌ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 4] ("your God is indeed One"): He — Mighty and Majestic is He — swore by these things that He is One. It has also been said that its meaning is: "by the Lord of these things, He is One". The interpretation of “اَلصّافّاتِ” is that they are the angels, that is: they are obedient in heaven, glorifying Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He. “فالزّاجِراتِ”: it is related that the angels drive the clouds; and it has been said: “فالزّاجِراتِ زَجْرًا” is everything that restrains from disobedience to Allah. ﴿فالتّالِياتِ ذِكْرًا﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 3]: it has been said: "the angels"; and it is possible that it is the angels and others as well, among those who recite the remembrance of Allah.
﴿وَرَبُّ المَشارِقِ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 5] ("and Lord of the points of sunrise"), and the points of sunset. It has been said: the points of sunrise are three hundred and sixty, and likewise the points of sunset.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿إنّا زَيَّنّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِزِينَةٍ الكَواكِبِ﴾ ("We have adorned the lowest heaven with an adornment, the stars"), [read] with “زِينَة” in iḍāfa (genitive construct) to “اَلْكَواكِبِ” [i.e. بِزِينَةِ الكَواكِبِ, "with the adornment of the stars"], and most readers read it this way. It has also been read with tanwīn and the genitive of “الكَواكِبِ”, the meaning being that “اَلْكَواكِبِ” is a badal (substitute) for “الزِّينَة”; the meaning is: "We have adorned the lowest heaven with the stars". “بِزِينَةٍ الكَواكِبَ” is also permissible — and it is the least common in reading — in the sense: "by Our adorning the stars"; and it is possible that “اَلْكَواكِبِ” in the accusative is a badal for His saying “بِزِينَةٍ”, because “بِزِينَةٍ” is in the position of an accusative. “بِزِينَةٍ الكَواكِبُ” is also permissible, but I do not know anyone who read it so; so do not read it so unless a transmission of it is established, because reading is a sunna (followed practice). The nominative of “اَلْكَواكِبُ” is in the sense: "We have adorned the lowest heaven in that its adornment is the stars", and "in that the stars have been adorned".

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿وَحِفْظًا مِن كُلِّ شَيْطانٍ مارِدٍ﴾ ("and as protection against every rebellious devil"), in the sense: "and We protected it with a protection from every rebellious devil"; they are pelted with them [the stars] when they try to eavesdrop.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
“لا يَسْمَعُونَ إلى المَلَإ الأعْلى” ("they cannot listen to the exalted assembly"); it is also read with shadda: “يَسَّمَّعُونَ”, in the sense of “يَتَسَمَّعُونَ” ("they strain to listen").
﴿وَيُقْذَفُونَ مِن كُلِّ جانِبٍ﴾ ﴿دُحُورًا﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 9] ("and they are pelted from every side, repelled"), that is: they are driven off, that is: they are kept far away. ﴿وَلَهم عَذابٌ واصِبٌ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 9] ("and theirs is a wāṣib punishment"): it has been said: "constant", and it has been said: "painful".

zajjaj:10-10.t:
﴿إلا مَن خَطِفَ﴾ ("except one who snatches [a word]"), with fatḥa and kasra on the ṭāʾ; one says: “خَطِفْتُ، أخْطَفُ” and “خَطَفْتُ أخْطِفُ”, when I take a thing quickly. “إلّا مَن خَطَّفَ”, with shadda on the ṭāʾ and fatḥa on the khāʾ, is also permissible; and “خِطَّفَ”, with kasra on the khāʾ and fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, is permissible. The meaning is “اِخْتَطَفَ”: the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ, and the alif dropped because the khāʾ now had a vowel. Whoever gives the khāʾ fatḥa casts onto it the fatḥa of the tāʾ which was in “اِخْتَطَفَ”; and whoever gives it kasra does so because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the ṭāʾ. As for whoever transmitted “خِطِفَ الخَطْفَةَ”, with kasra on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ, it has no justification except a very weak one: that the ṭāʾ is made to follow the kasra of the khāʾ (itbāʿ).
﴿فَأتْبَعَهُ شِهابٌ ثاقِبٌ﴾ ("and a piercing flame pursues him"): one says “تَبِعْتُهُ”, “أتْبَعْتُهُ” and “اِتَّبَعْتُهُ”, when I go on his track. “شِهابٌ ثاقِبٌ” is a shining star.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
﴿فاسْتَفْتِهِمْ﴾ ("so ask them"), that is: ask them a question that makes them acknowledge: ﴿أهم أشَدُّ خَلْقًا أمْ مَن خَلَقْنا﴾ ("are they stronger in creation, or those whom We have created?") — of the bygone nations before them, and others besides them, of the heavens and the earths?!
﴿مِن طِينٍ لازِبٍ﴾ ("from sticky clay"), and “لازِمٍ”; the meaning of both is one, that is: “لازِقٍ” ("adhesive").

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿بَلْ عَجِبْتَ ويَسْخَرُونَ﴾ ("nay, you wonder, while they mock"). It is also read “عَجِبْتُ”, with ḍamma on the tāʾ ("I wonder"). Its meaning with the fatḥa is: "nay, you wonder, O Muḥammad, at the revelation coming down upon you, while they mock"; and it may mean: "nay, you wonder at their denial of the resurrection". Whoever reads “عَجِبْتُ” — it is a report about Allah. Some people rejected this reading and said: Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — does not wonder. This rejection of theirs is a mistake, because the reading and the transmission [of it] are abundant, and wonder on the part of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — is unlike that of human beings, just as He said: ﴿وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 30], ﴿سَخِرَ اللَّهُ مِنهُمْ﴾ [al-Tawba: 79] and ﴿وَهُوَ خادِعُهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 142]; and plotting and outwitting on the part of Allah are unlike those of human beings. The origin of “اَلْعَجَبُ” (wonder) in the language is that when a person sees something he disapproves of and whose like is rare, he says: "I wonder at such-and-such". Likewise, when human beings do something that Allah disapproves of, it is permissible for Him to say about it: "I wonder"; Allah knew the thing before it came to be, but the disapproval — and the wonder by which the proof becomes binding — only occurs when the thing takes place.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَإذا رَأوْا آيَةً يَسْتَسْخِرُونَ﴾ ("and when they see a sign they ridicule it"), that is: when they see an inimitable sign they ridicule and mock.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿وَقالُوا إنْ هَذا إلا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ ("and they say: This is nothing but manifest magic"): so they made what indicates the oneness [of Allah], of the things they are incapable of [producing], into magic — such as the splitting of the moon and the like.

zajjaj:16-16.t: And His saying: ﴿أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا وعِظامًا أإنّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ ("when we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised?"); “إنّا” is also permissible: whoever reads “إنّا” is content with the alif of interrogation [already in أإذا]. The meaning in both ways is: "shall we be raised when we have become dust and bones?!"; and its interpretation is: “لَمَبْعُوثُونَ” ("shall we indeed be raised").

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿قُلْ نَعَمْ وأنْتُمْ داخِرُونَ﴾ ("say: Yes, and you will be humbled"). The meaning is: "say: yes, you will be raised while you are abased".

zajjaj:19-19.t: Then He explained that their raising will happen by a single shout, by His saying: ﴿فَإنَّما هي زَجْرَةٌ واحِدَةٌ فَإذا هم يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ ("it will be only a single shout, and at once they will be looking"), that is: they will come to life and be raised seeing, looking.

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿وَقالُوا يا ويْلَنا هَذا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾ ("and they will say: Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgement"). “اَلْوَيْلُ” is a word a speaker says at the time of destruction. The meaning of ﴿هَذا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾ is: the day of recompense, that is: a day in which we are recompensed for our deeds. When they said: "This is the Day of Judgement", it was said to them: Yes, ﴿هَذا يَوْمُ الفَصْلِ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 21] ("this is the Day of Decision which you used to deny"), that is: this is a day on which a decision is made between the doer of good and the doer of evil, and everyone is recompensed according to his deeds, and according to what Allah bestows by His favour on the Muslim.

zajjaj:22-22.t: ﴿احْشُرُوا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وأزْواجَهُمْ﴾ ("gather those who did wrong and their azwāj"): its meaning is: "and their peers and their likes". You say: “عِنْدِي مِن هَذا أزْواجٌ” ("I have azwāj of this"), that is: likes; and likewise “زَوْجانِ مِنَ الخِفافِ” ("a pair of khuffs"), that is: each one is the counterpart of the other. Likewise “اَلزَّوْجُ” is the woman and “اَلزَّوْجُ” is the man, the two having become matched through the marriage contract. And likewise His saying: ﴿وَآخَرُ مِن شَكْلِهِ أزْواجٌ﴾ [Ṣād: 58].

zajjaj:23-23.t: ﴿فاهْدُوهم إلى صِراطِ الجَحِيمِ﴾ ("and guide them to the path of Hellfire"). One says: “هَدَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ” ("I guided the man") when I have shown him the way; and “هَدَيْتُ العَرُوسَ إلى زَوْجِها” ("I conducted the bride to her husband"); and “أهْدَيْتُ الهَدِيَّةَ” ("I presented the gift"). Likewise you say of the bride: “أهْدَيْتُها”, when you have made her like a gift.

zajjaj:24-24.t: And His saying: ﴿وَقِفُوهم إنَّهم مَسْؤُولُونَ﴾ ("and stop them; they are to be questioned"), that is: detain them.

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿ما لَكم لا تَناصَرُونَ﴾ ("what is the matter with you that you do not help one another?"). His saying ﴿لا تَناصَرُونَ﴾ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "what is the matter with you, not helping one another?!"

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿وَأقْبَلَ بَعْضُهم عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ ("and they will turn to one another, questioning"), that is: some of them will question others.

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿قالُوا إنَّكم كُنْتُمْ تَأْتُونَنا عَنِ اليَمِينِ﴾ ("they will say: You used to come at us from the right"). This is the saying of the unbelievers to those who led them astray: "you used to deceive us by the strongest of means", that is: you used to come at us from the direction of religion, and make us think that religion and truth were what you were leading us astray with.

zajjaj:29-29.t: ﴿قالُوا بَلْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ ("they will say: Rather, you were not believers"), that is: the disbelief came only from your side.

zajjaj:31-31.t: ﴿فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنا قَوْلُ رَبِّنا﴾ ("so the word of our Lord has come true against us"): the word of punishment has come true against us. ﴿إنّا لَذائِقُونَ﴾ ("we shall surely taste [it]"), that is: the whole group, the one who leads astray and the one led astray, is in the Fire.

zajjaj:32-32.t: ﴿إنّا كُنّا غاوِينَ﴾ ("we were ourselves astray"), that is: we led you astray; we were ourselves astray, erring.

zajjaj:34-34.t: ﴿إنّا كَذَلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِالمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ ("thus do We deal with the criminals"): “اَلْمُجْرِمُونَ” are the polytheists specifically.

zajjaj:35-35.t: ﴿إنَّهم كانُوا إذا قِيلَ لَهم لا إلَهَ إلا اللَّهُ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ ("when it was said to them: There is no god but Allah, they used to be arrogant"), meaning: [too arrogant to accept] the oneness of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — and not to take the idols as gods.

zajjaj:40-40.t: And His saying: ﴿إلا عِبادَ اللَّهِ المُخْلَصِينَ﴾ ("except the purified servants of Allah"): “اَلْمُخْلَصِينَ” are those whom Allah has purified and chosen for His worship. It is also read “اَلْمُخْلِصِينَ” ("the sincere"), that is: those who affirm His oneness.

zajjaj:45-45.t: ﴿يُطافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِكَأْسٍ﴾ ("a cup will be passed around among them"). “اَلْكَأْسُ”: the vessel, when there is wine in it, is a kaʾs; and kaʾs applies to any vessel together with its drink. ﴿مِن مَعِينٍ﴾ ("from a flowing spring"), that is: of wine that flows as water flows on the face of the earth from springs.

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿بَيْضاءَ لَذَّةٍ﴾ ("white, delicious"), that is: possessing delight.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
﴿لا فِيها غَوْلٌ﴾ ("no ghawl is in it"): it does not steal away their minds, does not take them away, nor does any pain afflict them from it. ﴿وَلا هم عَنْها يُنْـزَفُونَ﴾ ("nor will they be intoxicated by it"): “يُنْزِفُونَ”, with fatḥa and with kasra on the zāy. Whoever reads “يُنْزَفُونَ”, the meaning is: "their minds will not go by drinking it"; the drunkard is called “نَزِيفٌ” and “مَنزُوفٌ”. Whoever reads “يُنْزِفُونَ”, its meaning is: "they will not exhaust their drink", that is: it is everlasting for them; and it is possible that “يُنْزِفُونَ” means: they become drunk. The poet said:
؎لَعَمْرِي لَئِنْ أنْزَفْتُمُ أوْ صَحَوْتُمُ ∗∗∗ لَبِئْسَ النَّدامى كُنْتُمْ آلَ أبْجَرا
(By my life, whether you got drunk or stayed sober, you were the worst of drinking companions, O family of Abjar!)

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿وَعِنْدَهم قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ عِينٌ﴾ ("and with them will be those of restrained gaze, wide-eyed"), that is: with them will be houris who have restrained their glances — that is, their eyes — to their husbands. “عِينٌ”: large-eyed, with beautiful eyes; the singular is “عَيْناءُ”.

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿كَأنَّهُنَّ بَيْضٌ مَكْنُونٌ﴾ ("as though they were sheltered eggs"), that is: as though their colours were the colours of ostrich eggs. “مَكْنُونٌ” is that which the ostrich's head shelters. It is also possible that “مَكْنُونٌ” means: guarded; one says: “كَنَنْتُ الشَّيْءَ”, when I have covered it and guarded it, so it is “مَكْنُونٌ”; and “أكْنَنْتَهُ”, when you have concealed it within yourself.

zajjaj:52-52.t: ﴿أإنَّكَ لَمِنَ المُصَدِّقِينَ﴾ ("are you indeed among those who believe?"), [with the ṣād] light, from “صَدَّقَ، فَهو مُصَدِّقٌ” ("he believed, so he is a believer"). Doubling the ṣād is not permissible here, because “اَلْمُصَّدِّقِينَ” are those who give charity, while “اَلْمُصَدِّقِينَ” are those who do not deny. So the meaning is: "I had a companion who used to say: Are you among those who believe in the resurrection after you have become dust and bones?" Then his Muslim companion wished to see him, after it was said to him: ﴿هَلْ أنْتُمْ مُطَّلِعُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 54] ("will you look down?"), that is: would you like to look down and know where your station is relative to the station of the people of the Fire?

zajjaj:55-55.t:
﴿فاطَّلَعَ فَرَآهُ في سَواءِ الجَحِيمِ﴾ ("so he looked down and saw him in the midst of Hellfire"): the Muslim looked down and saw his companion who used to deny the resurrection in the sawāʾ of Hellfire, that is: in the middle of Hellfire; the sawāʾ of everything is its middle. It is also read: “هَلْ أنْتُمْ مُطْلِعُونَ”, with fatḥa and with kasra on the nūn, and with the ṭāʾ light. Whoever gives the nūn fatḥa with the light form, saying “مُطْلِعُونَ”, it means “طالِعُونَ” and “مُطَّلِعُونَ”; one says “طَلَعْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ”, “اِطْلَعْتُ” and “اِطَّلَعْتُ” with one meaning. Whoever reads “مُطْلِعُونِ”, with kasra on the nūn, reads “فَأُطْلِعَ”; and whoever reads “مُطْلِعُونَ” with fatḥa on the nūn must read “فَأُطْلَعَ”; and “فَأُطْلِعَ” is permissible in the sense: "will you make anyone look down?" As for the kasra on the nūn, it is anomalous (shādhdh) according to the Basrans and the Kufans alike, and according to all of them it has a weak justification. The like of it has come in poetry:
؎هُمُ القائِلُونَ الخَيْرَ والآمِرُونَهُ ∗∗∗ إذا ما خَشَوْا مِن مُحْدَثِ الأمْرِ مُعْظَما
(They are the ones who speak good and command it, whenever they fear something grave from a new turn of affairs.)
And they recited:
؎وَما أدْرِي وظَنِّي كُلُّ ظَنِّي ∗∗∗ أمُسْلِمُنِي إلى قَوْمِي شَراحِ
(I do not know — and my supposition is all I have — whether Sharāḥi will hand me over to my people.)
What Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] recited to me is: “أيُسْلِمُنِي إلى قَوْمِي” ("will he hand me over to my people"). The [correct] speech is only “أمُسْلِمِي” and “أيُسْلِمُنِي”, and likewise “هُمُ القائِلُونَ الخَيْرَ والآمِرُوهُ”. With all active participles, when you mention a pronoun after them, you do not mention the nūn nor the tanwīn: you say “زَيْدٌ ضارِبِي” ("Zayd is striking me") and “هُما ضارِباكَ” ("the two of them are striking you"); and “هو ضارِبُنِي” is not permissible, nor “هم ضارِبُونَكَ”; “هم ضارِبُونَكَ” is not permissible according to them except in poetry. However, it has been read with the kasra: “هَلْ أنْتُمْ مُطَّلِعُونِ”, in the sense of “مُطْلِعُونِي” ("will you let me look down?"): the yāʾ was dropped, as it is dropped at verse-endings, and the kasra remained as an indication of it. In grammar — I mean the kasra of the nūn — it is as I have told you, and the reading with it is rare. The best and most common reading is “مُطَّلِعُونَ”, with shadda on the ṭāʾ and fatḥa on the nūn; then, next to it, “مُطْلِعُونِ”, with the ṭāʾ light and fatḥa on the nūn. [Translator's note: the word is printed here with a kasra on the nūn (مُطْلِعُونِ) although the text describes it as having fatḥa; the intended form is evidently مُطْلِعُونَ.]

zajjaj:56-56.t: ﴿قالَ تاللَّهِ إنْ كِدْتَ لَتُرْدِينِ﴾ ("he said: By Allah, you almost ruined me"). “تاللَّهِ” means “واللَّهِ” ("by Allah"); the tāʾ is a substitute for the wāw. “لَتُرْدِينِ”, that is: you would destroy me; one says: “رَدِيَ الرَّجُلُ، يَرْدى، رَدًى”, when he perishes, and “أرْدَيْتُهُ”: I destroyed him.

zajjaj:57-57.t: ﴿لَكُنْتُ مِنَ المُحْضَرِينَ﴾ ("I would have been among those brought [to punishment]"), that is: I would be brought to the punishment as you have been brought.

zajjaj:62-62.t: ﴿أذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُـزُلا أمْ شَجَرَةُ الزَّقُّومِ﴾ ("is that better as hospitality, or the tree of Zaqqūm?"). The meaning is: "Are the bliss of Paradise and its food better as hospitality, or is the tree of Zaqqūm better as hospitality?" “اَلنُّزُلُ” here means: yield and surplus; you say: “هَذا طَعامٌ لَهُ نُزُلٌ” ("this is food that has yield"), and “نُزْلٌ”, with sukūn and with ḍamma on the zāy, and “نَزَلٌ”. And “أذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُزُلًا” may mean: "Is that better in the category of provisions (anzāl) by which one is sustained and with which residing is possible, or the provision of the people of the Fire?" It is said of the provisions that are set up for people: “أقَمْتُ لَهم نُزُلَهم” ("I set up their nuzul for them"), that is: "their nourishment and what makes it suitable for them to stay with it".

zajjaj:63-63.t: The meaning of ﴿إنّا جَعَلْناها فِتْنَةً لِلظّالِمِينَ﴾ ("We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers") is: "a lesson for the wrongdoers", that is: a piece of information by which they were tried and which they denied, so it became a trial for them. That is because when they heard that it is a tree that comes out at the bottom of Hellfire, they said: trees are burnt by fire, so how can a tree grow in fire? So they were tried, and they denied that.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
﴿طَلْعُها كَأنَّهُ رُءُوسُ الشَّياطِينِ﴾ ("its spathes are as though they were the heads of devils"). There are three views on it. It has been said: “اَلشَّياطِينُ” are snakes that have [ugly] heads, so its spathes were likened to the heads of those snakes. It has been said: “رُؤُوسُ الشَّياطِينِ” is a known plant. And it has been said — and this is the well-known view — that when a thing is considered ugly it is likened to the devil, so it is said: "as though it were the face of a devil" and "as though it were the head of a devil"; the devil is not seen, but it is felt that he is the ugliest of things — if he were seen, he would be seen in the ugliest form. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
؎أيَقْتُلُنِي والمَشْرَفِيُّ مُضاجِعِي ∗∗∗ ومَسْنُونَةٌ زُرْقٌ كَأنْيابِ أغْوالِ؟
(Will he kill me, when the Mashrafī sword lies beside me, and sharpened blue [spearheads] like the fangs of ghouls?)
The ghoul has never been seen, nor its fangs; but likening to what is considered ugly is more effective: in the category of the masculine, it is likened to the devil, and in the category of what is considered ugly in the feminine, it is likened to the ghoul.

zajjaj:67-67.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إنَّ لَهم عَلَيْها لَشَوْبًا مِن حَمِيمٍ﴾ ("then on top of it they will have a mixture of boiling water"), that is: a blend and a mixture. It is also read: “لَشُوبًا مِن حَمِيمٍ”. “اَلشَّوْبُ” is the maṣdar (verbal noun) and “اَلشُّوبُ” is the noun; and “اَلْخَلْطُ” [here] is that which is mixed.

zajjaj:70-70.t: ﴿فَهم عَلى آثارِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ﴾ ("so they are hastening in their footsteps"), that is: they follow their footsteps, following in haste. And it is said “يُهْرَعُونَ” as though they are driven on from haste to follow their forefathers. One says “هُرِعَ” and “أُهْرِعُ” with one meaning: when he is urged on and hastens.

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نادانا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ المُجِيبُونَ﴾ ("and Noah called upon Us, and how excellent are the Answerers!"), that is: he called upon Us to save him from drowning. The meaning is: "how excellent are the Answerers — Us".

zajjaj:76-76.t: ﴿وَنَجَّيْناهُ وأهْلَهُ مِنَ الكَرْبِ العَظِيمِ﴾ ("and We saved him and his family from the great distress"), meaning the distress of drowning, which is a punishment.

zajjaj:77-77.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ هُمُ الباقِينَ﴾ ("and We made his offspring the ones who remained"): when the Flood came, none remained but Noah and his offspring, and the rest of creation is from the offspring of Noah.

zajjaj:78-78.t: ﴿وَتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ ("and We left for him among later generations"), that is: We left for him good remembrance until the Day of Resurrection; and that remembrance is His saying: ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى نُوحٍ في العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 79]. The meaning of "We left for him among later generations" is: that blessings be invoked upon him until the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:83-83.t: ﴿وَإنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِ لإبْراهِيمَ﴾ ("and among his partisans was Abraham"), that is: among the partisans of Noah, among the people of his creed — meaning Noah.

zajjaj:84-84.t: ﴿إذْ جاءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ﴾ ("when he came to his Lord with a sound heart"). It has come in the exegesis: "sound from polytheism"; and it is sound from polytheism and from every defilement.

zajjaj:87-87.t: ﴿فَما ظَنُّكم بِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ("then what do you think of the Lord of the worlds?"). Abraham said to his people — while they were worshipping idols —: "What is it that you think of the Lord of the worlds, while you worship other than Him?!" The position of “ما” is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is “ظَنُّكم”.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
﴿فَنَظَرَ نَظْرَةً في النُّجُومِ﴾ ﴿فَقالَ إنِّي سَقِيمٌ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 89] ("then he cast a glance at the stars and said: I am sick"). He said to his people — having seen a star —: "I am sick", and he gave them the impression that he had the plague, so they turned away from him, departing, fleeing lest the plague be passed on to them. He said "I am sick" only because everyone, even if healthy, must inevitably fall sick and die. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وإنَّهم مَيِّتُونَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 30], that is: you will die in the future; and likewise His saying ﴿إنِّي سَقِيمٌ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 89], that is: I will inevitably fall sick. It has been related in the ḥadīth: «”لَمْ يَكْذِبْ إبْراهِيمُ إلّا في ثَلاثٍ“» ("Abraham did not lie except in three [things]"). We have explained that, and that in these three there was an indirect expression (muʿāraḍa): in his saying ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهم هَذا﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 63] ("rather, this biggest of them did it"), in the sense: "if they can speak, then their biggest did it"; and his saying: "Sarah is my sister", that is: my sister in Islam;
and his saying ﴿إنِّي سَقِيمٌ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 89], according to what we have explained.

zajjaj:93-93.t: ﴿فَراغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْبًا بِاليَمِينِ﴾ ("then he turned upon them, striking with the right hand"). The meaning of “راغَ عَلَيْهِمْ” is: he turned upon them. “ضَرْبًا” is a maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is: "he turned upon the idols, striking them a striking with the right hand". [بِاليَمِينِ] admits two ways: with his right hand, or with strength and might. He said “عَلَيْهِمْ” [with the masculine plural pronoun] although they are idols, because they had made them objects of worship, in the position of beings that discern, just as He said: ﴿وَكُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 40].

zajjaj:94-94.t:
﴿فَأقْبَلُوا إلَيْهِ﴾ ("then they came towards him"), meaning Abraham's people, ﴿يَزِفُّونَ﴾: hastening towards him. It is read in three ways: “يَزِفُّونَ”, with fatḥa on the yāʾ; “يُزِفُّونَ”, with ḍamma on it; and “يَزِفُونَ”, with the fāʾ light. The most correct Arabic of them all is “يَزِفُّونَ”, with fatḥa on the yāʾ and shadda on the fāʾ. Its origin is from the zafīf of ostriches, which is the beginning of their running; one says: “زَفَّ النَّعامُ، يَزِفُّ”. It is also read “يُزِفُّونَ”, that is: they come to be running [zafīf]; and similar to it is the saying of the poet:
؎تَمَنّى حُصَيْنٌ أنْ يَسُودَ جِذاعَهُ ∗∗∗ فَأمْسى حُصَيْنٌ قَدْ أُذِلَّ وأُقْهِرا
(Ḥuṣayn wished to lord it over the young men of his clan, but Ḥuṣayn ended up humiliated and brought to subjugation.)
The meaning of “أُقْهِرَ” is: he came to be subjugated; and likewise “يُزِفُّونَ”. As for “يَزِفُونَ” with the light form, it is from “وَزَفَ، يَزِفُ”, meaning "he hastened"; al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī did not know it, but others knew it.

zajjaj:97-97.t: And His saying: ﴿فِي الجَحِيمِ﴾ ("into the blazing fire"): every fire piled one part upon another is a jaḥm.

zajjaj:100-100.t: ﴿رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ ("my Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous"): he is saying: "grant me a righteous child from among the righteous".

zajjaj:101-101.t: ﴿فَبَشَّرْناهُ بِغُلامٍ حَلِيمٍ﴾ ("so We gave him the glad tidings of a forbearing boy"). This glad tiding indicates that he is a boy and that he will live until he is described with forbearance.

zajjaj:102-102.t:
﴿فَلَمّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ السَّعْيَ﴾ ("and when he reached the age of working with him"), that is: he attained [the age of] working with him; it is said that he had reached, at that time, thirteen years. ﴿قالَ يا بُنَيَّ إنِّي أرى في المَنامِ أنِّي أذْبَحُكَ فانْظُرْ ماذا تَرى﴾ ("he said: O my son, I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so consider what you think"). It is read without imāla (inclination of the vowel), and “تَرِى” with imāla, and “تُرِي” without imāla, and “تُرِى” with imāla, and “ماذا تُرى”. So there are five ways in it: “تَرى” with fatḥa and with kasra [i.e. imāla], and likewise in “تُرِي” and “تُرى”. There are five other ways in it with which no one has read, so do not read with them: namely, that the five we have mentioned, with and without imāla, which come without hamza, you give all of them a hamza; so whatever had imāla, he gave it hamza and imāla, and whatever did not have imāla, he gave it imāla and did not give it hamza. [Translator's note: the last clause appears garbled in the source; as written it reads "gave it imāla and did not give it hamza", whereas the sense requires "gave it hamza without imāla".] It is permissible: “ماذا تَرْأى” with imāla, “ماذا تُرْئِي”, “ماذا تُرْأى”, “ماذا تَرى” and “ماذا تُرى”. The meaning of “ماذا تَرْأى” and “تُرْئِي” is from “اَلرَّأْيُ” (opinion), and the meaning of “ماذا تُرى” is: what do you advise? Al-Farrāʾ claimed that its meaning is: "what will you show me of your patience?" — but I do not know anyone who said this; in all the exegesis, “ما تُرِي” means: what do you advise?
﴿قالَ يا أبَتِ افْعَلْ ما تُؤْمَرُ﴾ ("he said: O my father, do as you are commanded"). The dream-vision of the prophets is revelation, in the position of revelation to them in the waking state. We have explained “يا أبَهْ” and its i'rab earlier in the book.
﴿سَتَجِدُنِي إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصّابِرِينَ﴾ ("you will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient"): he is saying: [patient] with Allah's command.

zajjaj:103-103.t: ﴿فَلَمّا أسْلَما وتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ﴾ ("then when they had both submitted and he had laid him on his forehead"). “أسْلَما”: they both surrendered to Allah's command; Abraham was content to sacrifice his son, and his son was content to be sacrificed, in confirmation of the dream and in obedience to Allah. People have differed about who the one he was commanded to sacrifice was. Some said: Isaac, and some said: Ishmael. As for those who said it was Isaac: ʿAlī — Allah's mercy be upon him — Ibn Masʿūd, Kaʿb al-Aḥbār and a group of the Successors. As for those who said it was Ishmael: Ibn ʿUmar, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and a group of the Successors. The argument of those who said it was Ishmael is His saying: ﴿وَبَشَّرْناهُ بِإسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 112] ("and We gave him the glad tidings of Isaac, a prophet among the righteous"). The argument of those who said it was Isaac: he said there were two glad tidings concerning Isaac: the first, ﴿فَبَشَّرْناهُ بِغُلامٍ حَلِيمٍ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 101]; then when he surrendered himself to be sacrificed, and Abraham surrendered himself to sacrificing him, he was given glad tidings of him as a prophet among the righteous. There is much said about the two of them, and Allah knows best which of them was the one to be sacrificed. As for the apodosis (jawāb) of “فَلَمّا أسْلَما وتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ” — [تَلَّهُ] meaning: he threw him down — people have differed about it. Some said: its apodosis is “ونادَيْناهُ” ("We called to him"), the wāw being redundant (zāʾida). Others said that the apodosis is omitted, because there is in the speech an indication of it; the meaning is: "when he did that, he attained happiness, Allah gave his son prophethood, and He made his reward abundant in the Hereafter".

zajjaj:107-107.t: ﴿وَفَدَيْناهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ ("and We ransomed him with a great sacrifice"). “اَلذِّبْحُ”, with kasra on the dhāl, is the thing that is sacrificed, and “اَلذَّبْحُ” is the maṣdar (verbal noun); you say: “ذَبَحْتُهُ، أذْبَحُهُ، ذَبْحًا” ("I slaughtered it"). It has been said that it was the ram that was accepted from the son of Adam when he offered it; it has been said that it grazed in Paradise for forty years; and it has been said that it was one of the mountain goats (awʿāl) — the awʿāl being the mountain he-goats.

zajjaj:115-115.t: ﴿وَنَجَّيْناهُما وقَوْمَهُما مِنَ الكَرْبِ العَظِيمِ﴾ ("and We saved the two of them and their people from the great distress"): it has been said: from drowning, as was done to Pharaoh and his people.

zajjaj:123-123.t: ﴿وَإنَّ إلْياسَ لَمِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ ("and Ilyās was among the messengers"). It has come in the exegesis that he is Idrīs; and it has been related from Ibn Masʿūd that he read: “وَإنَّ إدْرِيسَ”, and it has been related [that he read]: “سَلامٌ عَلى إدْراسِينَ”.

zajjaj:125-125.t: ﴿أتَدْعُونَ بَعْلا وتَذَرُونَ أحْسَنَ الخالِقِينَ﴾ ﴿اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 126] ("do you call upon Baʿl and forsake the Best of creators — Allah, your Lord"). It has been said that Baʿl was something they used to worship, an idol of gold; and it has been said that baʿl means: "a lord". It has been read “اَللَّهَ رَبَّكم” [in the accusative], as a qualification of “أحْسَنَ الخالِقِينَ اللَّهَ”, and it has been read “اَللَّهُ رَبُّكم” [in the nominative], as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

zajjaj:130-130.t: ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى إلْ ياسِينَ﴾ ("peace be upon Il Yāsīn"), and it has also been read: “إلْياسَ”. Whoever reads it joined, then the status of “إلْ ياسِينَ” is a plural: he and his believing community. Likewise what is attributed to a thing is pluralised with the wording of the thing: you say “رَأيْتُ المَسامِعَةَ، والمَهالِبَةَ” ("I saw the Masāmiʿa and the Mahāliba"), meaning the sons of al-Muhallab and the sons of Misma'; and likewise: “رَأيْتُ المُهَلَّبِينَ، والمِسْمَعِينَ”. There is another way in it, in which there are two dialectal forms: “إلْياسُ” and “إلْياسِينُ”, just as one says “مِيكالُ” and “مِيكائِيلُ”.

zajjaj:135-135.t: And His saying: ﴿إلا عَجُوزًا في الغابِرِينَ﴾ ("except an old woman among those who remained behind"), meaning: among those who remained.

zajjaj:140-140.t: And His saying: ﴿إذْ أبَقَ إلى الفُلْكِ المَشْحُونِ﴾ ("when he ran away to the laden ship"): “أبَقَ” means: he fled to the laden ship; and “اَلْمَشْحُونُ” is: filled.

zajjaj:141-141.t: ﴿فَساهَمَ﴾ ("then he cast lots"): he drew lots. “اَلْمُدْحَضِينَ” ("the losers"): those overcome. When Jonah was in the ship, it would not move, so the people of the ship drew lots with him, and the lot fell upon him; so he went out of it and threw himself into the sea.

zajjaj:142-142.t: ﴿فالتَقَمَهُ الحُوتُ﴾ ("then the whale swallowed him") — that is, the fish — and when he had left the ship, it moved. ﴿وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ﴾ ("while he was blameworthy"): he had done something for which he is blamed. One says: “قَدْ ألامَ الرَّجُلُ”, so he is “مُلِيمٌ”, when he has done what he deserves to be blamed for.

zajjaj:143-143.t: ﴿فَلَوْلا أنَّهُ كانَ مِنَ المُسَبِّحِينَ﴾ ("and had he not been among those who glorify"): among those who pray.

zajjaj:144-144.t: ﴿لَلَبِثَ في بَطْنِهِ إلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ ("he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised"). It has come in the exegesis that he remained forty days; and al-Ḥasan said: he remained only a little, and was brought out of its belly shortly after the time at which he was swallowed.

zajjaj:145-145.t:
﴿فَنَبَذْناهُ بِالعَراءِ وهو سَقِيمٌ﴾ ("then We cast him onto the bare shore while he was ill"), meaning: in the empty place. “اَلْعَراءُ” is of two kinds, with the short ending (maqṣūr) and with the long ending (mamdūd): the maqṣūr [al-ʿarā] is the side [of something], and “اَلْعَراءُ”, the mamdūd, is the empty place. Abū ʿUbayda and others said: it is called “اَلْعَراءُ” only because there are no trees in it, nor anything that covers it. It has also been said that al-ʿarāʾ is the face of the earth, its meaning being the empty face of the earth. And they recited:
؎وَرَفَعْتُ رِجْلًا لا أخافُ عِثارَها ∗∗∗ ونَبَذْتُ بِالبَلَدِ العَراءِ ثِيابِي
(I lifted a foot whose stumbling I do not fear, and cast off my garments in the bare land.)

zajjaj:146-146.t: ﴿وَأنْبَتْنا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةً مِن يَقْطِينٍ﴾ ("and We caused to grow over him a plant of yaqṭīn"). Every plant that does not grow on a stem, but only spreads over the face of the ground — such as the gourd, the melon and the colocynth — is “يَقْطِينٌ”. I reckon its derivation is from “قَطَنَ بِالمَكانِ” ("he dwelt in the place"), when he stays in it; all these plants lie on the face of the ground, and that is why it is called “يَقْطِينٍ”.

zajjaj:147-147.t: ﴿وَأرْسَلْناهُ إلى مِائَةِ ألْفٍ أوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾ ("and We sent him to a hundred thousand or more"). More than one [scholar] said its meaning is: "nay, more"; al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayda said that. Others said: its meaning is: "or more, in your own estimation: when an observer sees them he says: these are a hundred thousand, or more than a hundred"; and this is according to the original sense of “أوْ”. Some said: its meaning is the meaning of the wāw ("and"). But “أوْ” does not have the meaning of the wāw, because the wāw means combination, and there is no indication in it that one of the two things is before the other; whereas “أوْ” means singling out one of two things or of several things.

zajjaj:149-149.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فاسْتَفْتِهِمْ﴾ ("so ask them"), that is: ask them a question of rebuke and of making them acknowledge, because they claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah — Allah is exalted far above that.

zajjaj:150-150.t: ﴿أمْ خَلَقْنا المَلائِكَةَ إناثًا﴾ ("or did We create the angels female"): its meaning is: "Rather, did We create the angels female?" ﴿وَهم شاهِدُونَ﴾ ("while they were witnesses?").

zajjaj:151-151.t: ﴿ألا إنَّهم مِن إفْكِهِمْ لَيَقُولُونَ﴾ ﴿وَلَدَ اللَّهُ وإنَّهم لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 152] ﴿أصْطَفى البَناتِ عَلى البَنِينَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 153] ("indeed it is of their falsehood that they say: Allah has begotten — and they are liars. Has He chosen daughters over sons?"). This alif has fatḥa; this is the preferred view, because the meaning is: "ask them: has He chosen daughters over sons?" — so the alif is the alif of interrogation. “اِصْطَفى” [with a connecting alif] is also permissible, as a quotation of their saying: "they say: He has chosen". But giving the alif fatḥa and making it a disjunctive hamza is better, on [the basis of] “أاصْطَفى”, then the connecting alif is dropped.

zajjaj:158-158.t:
﴿وَجَعَلُوا بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ الجِنَّةِ نَسَبًا﴾ ("and they have set up a kinship between Him and the jinna"): “اَلْجِنَّةُ” here are the angels.
﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَتِ الجِنَّةُ إنَّهم لَمُحْضَرُونَ﴾ ("and the jinna have known that they will be brought [to punishment]"), that is: the jinna — and they are the angels — have known that those who said "Allah has begotten" will be brought to the punishment.

zajjaj:159-159.t: ﴿سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمّا يَصِفُونَ﴾ ("glory be to Allah above what they describe"): declaring Allah free of evil, above their description.

zajjaj:161-161.t: ﴿فَإنَّكم وما تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ ﴿ما أنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفاتِنِينَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 162] ("for you and what you worship cannot tempt [anyone] away from Him"), that is: you cannot lead [anyone] astray against Him, except one whom Allah has led astray.

zajjaj:163-163.t: ﴿إلا مَن هو صالِ الجَحِيمِ﴾ ("except one who is to burn in Hellfire"), that is: you lead none astray but the people of the Fire. Al-Ḥasan read: “إلّا مَن هو صالُ الجَحِيمِ”, with ḍamma on the lām; but the reading is with kasra on the lām, in the sense of “صالِي”; the pause on it ought to be with the yāʾ, but it is omitted in the muṣḥaf. Al-Ḥasan's reading has two justifications. One of them is that he meant “صالُونَ الجَحِيمَ” ("those who burn in Hellfire"): the nūn was dropped because of the iḍāfa (genitive construct), and the wāw was dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the lām of “اَلْجَحِيمِ”; and “مَن” is taken in the sense of a genus, that is: the genus of those who burn in Hellfire. And it is possible that “صالُ” is in the sense of “صائِلُ”, reshaped (maqlūb) from “صالى”, like “جُرُفٍ هارٍ” ("a crumbling bank"), that is: “هائِرٍ”. [Translator's note: the source text reads «مَفْعُولٍ مِن صالى»; this is translated as "reshaped (maqlūb)" on the assumption that مَقْلُوبٌ is intended, as the comparison with هارٍ / هائِرٍ (metathesis) suggests.] The reading on which there is consensus is the kasra of the lām.

zajjaj:164-164.t: ﴿وَما مِنّا إلا لَهُ مَقامٌ مَعْلُومٌ﴾ ("and there is none of us but has a known station"). This is the saying of the angels, and there is something implied here; the meaning is: "there is no angel among us but has a known station".

zajjaj:165-165.t: ﴿وَإنّا لَنَحْنُ الصّافُّونَ﴾ ("and indeed we are those who range in ranks"), that is: we are those who pray.

zajjaj:166-166.t: ﴿وَإنّا لَنَحْنُ المُسَبِّحُونَ﴾ ("and indeed we are those who glorify"): those who extol Allah, who declare Him free of evil.

zajjaj:167-167.t: ﴿وَإنْ كانُوا لَيَقُولُونَ﴾ ﴿لَوْ أنَّ عِنْدَنا ذِكْرًا مِنَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 168] ﴿لَكُنّا عِبادَ اللَّهِ المُخْلَصِينَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 169] ("and they used to say: If we had a Reminder from the former peoples, we would have been purified servants of Allah"). The unbelievers of Quraysh used to say: if a Reminder had come to us as it came to others among the former peoples, we would have devoted our worship sincerely to Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He. But when it came to them, they disbelieved in it.

zajjaj:170-170.t: ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ("so they will come to know"), that is: they will come to know the consequence of their disbelief, and what will descend upon them of punishment and of vengeance on them in this world and the Hereafter.

zajjaj:171-171.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنا لِعِبادِنا المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ ("and Our word has already gone forth to Our servants, the messengers"), that is: the promise has preceded to them that Allah will help them with proof, with victory over their enemy in this world, and with vengeance on their enemy in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:173-173.t: ﴿وَإنَّ جُنْدَنا لَهُمُ الغالِبُونَ﴾ ("and Our host — they will be the victors"): the party of Allah, theirs is victory.
